events.id: October Bookbinding Workshops at WCBA-Wellington Centre for Book Arts, 262 Thorndon Quay, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: October Bookbinding Workshops at WCBA
events.venue: Wellington Centre for Book Arts, 262 Thorndon Quay, Wellington
events.long_description:
Saturday 24 October
Discover the Endless Possibilities of Carmencho Arregui's Crossed Structure Binding
Deceptively simple, wonderfully adaptable, and full of creative potential, the Crossed Structure Binding is a structure every bookbinder should know. Invented by Carmencho Arregui in 1992, this innovative binding transformed ideas about how books can be constructed, revealing the spine sewing and opening new pathways for both artistic and conservation work.

Working from Carmencho's diagrams and instructions, we'll explore her remarkable structure and look at examples created by binders around the world. Opening perfectly flat and capable of being adapted to soft or hard covers in materials from paper to leather, the structure offers an extraordinary range of decorative and structural possibilities. Join us to discover why this revolutionary binding continues to inspire book artists, conservators, and makers more than three decades after its invention.

Sunday 25 October
Fundamentals of Bookbinding
Start your bookbinding journey with a day dedicated to the essential skills that underpin every successful binding. You'll learn the fundamentals of cutting, folding, sewing, and gluing paper while creating a series of simple projects, including a concertina, one-sheet book, single-signature pamphlets, and, time permitting, a folded slipcase.

Along the way, you'll discover practical tips and tricks, gain hands-on experience with a range of tools, and develop a better understanding of paper and materials. The more accurately you can cut and fold, the more successful your future bindings will be. Whether you're completely new to bookbinding or looking to strengthen your core skills, this workshop provides a solid foundation for your creative journey.

Details on cost and enrolments at https://www.meetup.com/theprintingmuseum

events.name: Colourful Enamel Jewellery Day
events.venue: 3 Market Ln, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011
events.long_description:
Colourful Enamel Jewellery Day
Learn to create beautiful enamelled jewellery with Lisa Sinclair.

Join us for a full-day enamelling workshop where you’ll explore colour, texture, and fire to create vibrant enamelled jewellery in copper or silver.

This hands-on class focuses on the fundamentals of enamelling, showing you how to apply, fire, and layer enamel to achieve rich, expressive surfaces. You’ll make a simple yet beautifully textured pendant or pair of earrings, then learn how to add a pop (or flood!) of colour to bring your piece to life.

Beginners to metalwork are very welcome - pre-formed shapes are available so you can focus on experimenting with colour, pattern, and mark-making. If you have some metalworking experience, you’re encouraged to take things further by creating and texturing your own metal forms before enamelling.

This is a playful, creative workshop and an ideal class for anyone who loves working with colour, surface, and experimentation - whether you’re new to enamels or keen to deepen your skills.

What you’ll learn:
The basics of enamelling on copper and silver
How to prepare metal for enamelling
Applying enamel using different techniques
Firing enamel and building up layers of colour
Creating texture and pattern in metal
Tips for achieving clean, vibrant enamel finishes

The class fee covers enamel materials but NOT metals. Students can choose from a range of pre-cut copper blanks or use their own copper sheet. Findings and chains are available to purchase at a range of good prices to suit all budgets.

Kids aged approximately 12+ are welcome. Any participant under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

For health and safety reasons, students must wear sturdy closed-toe shoes.

Workshop fee $248, early bird $225 till 28 Sept.

events.long_description:
Explore Stonehenge Aotearoa at Your Own Pace

Our self-guided tour includes a map and a 12-minute audio-visual presentation to help you uncover the secrets of the henge. Afterward, head down to the stone circle and try out its unique acoustics — clap your hands and hear the echo respond, or whisper and see how far your voice carries.

A self-guided tour typically takes around 30 minutes, but many visitors stay longer simply because it’s so much fun. The bigger your group, the better the experience!

Please arrive at least 30 minutes before closing time.
Available during our opening hours: 10 AM – 4 PM.

From the delicate A Heart Exposed and the rich depth of The Chocolate Camera, to the savoury kick of The Apricot Proof, each item has been crafted by our award-winning chefs and is ready for its close-up.

Your high tea includes your choice of tea or coffee, with alcoholic beverages available to purchase. Dietary options are available on request.

Every purchase helps support Aotearoa New Zealand’s national museum.


Set Menu
(Includes one of each item per person)

A Heart Exposed
A delicate petite gâteau of tropical guava mousse layered with a vibrant raspberry centre, finished with refined textures and a balance of sweetness, bright berry acidity, and silky indulgence.

The Matcha Take
A refined Japanese-inspired madeleine infused with premium matcha, baked to a tender crumb with gentle earthy depth. Paired with luscious matcha ganache and sharp citrus bursts of yuzu gel.

The Chocolate Camera
An elegant chocolate creation showcasing the rich, velvety depth of premium Whittaker’s chocolate balanced with the vibrant citrus brightness of calamansi.

Golden Hour
A radiant tropical dessert crafted with luscious mango mousse and vibrant passionfruit notes, layered to create a light yet indulgent finish.

The Apricot Proof
A savoury petite muffin featuring sweet roasted capsicum folded through a soft, buttery crumb with delicate pockets of apricot for subtle fruity warmth.

Chicken Strut
Delicately layered smoked chicken paired with crisp cucumber ribbons, peppery rocket, and vibrant red pesto, nestled between soft artisan bread.

Green Screen Sandwich (V)
A beautifully balanced vegetarian finger sandwich showcasing tender grilled courgette, slow-roasted vegetable chutney, and fresh baby spinach.


Dietary Menu
(Includes one of each item per person)

The Mango Still (VE/GF)
A smooth mango mousse encased in a delicate chocolate shell, showcasing the fruit’s natural sweetness.

Peanut Butter Proof (VE/GF)
A rich peanut butter slice topped with a chocolate finish, balancing salty depth with a smooth, indulgent crumb.

Chocolate Darkroom (VE/GF)
Dark chocolate cups filled with smooth espresso-infused ganache, rich and intense from start to finish.

Matcha Moment (VE/GF)
Matcha chocolate shells with a bright citrus centre, balancing earthy green tea notes against a fresh citrus snap.

Apricot Aperture (VE/GF)
A vibrant apricot fruit jelly with an intense natural fruit flavour, finished with a delicate sugar coating for a clean, bright bite.

The Garden Negative (VE)
Tender grilled courgette layered with slow-roasted vegetable chutney and fresh baby spinach.

Fritter in Focus (VE)
Golden corn fritters served with beetroot mayonnaise, mesclun leaves, and vine-ripened tomatoes.

events.id: Rita Angus Cottage open day-194A Sydney St W, Thorndon, Wellington 6011-All Events In
events.name: Rita Angus Cottage open day
events.venue: 194A Sydney St W, Thorndon, Wellington 6011
events.long_description:
Rita Angus Cottage open day
You are invited to come and sketch in the garden at Rita Angus' historic cottage.

The garden at the Rita Angus Cottage (Category 1 Historic Place) will be open to visitors, who are encouraged to stay and sketch the abundant array of flowers and plant life that surround the 1877 cottage where New Zealand artist Rita Angus lived between 1955 and 1970, providing her with much inspiration and subject matter.

Rita Angus Cottage Trustees and volunteer gardeners will be on hand, with drawing material and reproductions of some of Rita’s representations of her Thorndon garden. Some materials will be provided. You are also welcome to bring along your own pens, pencils, pastels and watercolours – and perhaps a picnic.

The house continues as a studio for an artist-in-residence programme and is a part of the legacy that Rita Angus has left to contemporary New Zealand Art.

Cost: Koha

Learn more on our website:
https://wellingtonheritagefestival.co.nz/event/rita-angus-cottage-open-day/

This event is part of the 2026 Wellington Heritage Festival, running 24th October - 15th November. Discover over 160 more events on our website:
https://wellingtonheritagefestival.co.nz/events/

Banner image note: Rita Angus Cottage Trust, 2018

events.long_description:
Susette Goldsmith, author of 'Capital Trees' is your guide to significant and meaningful trees that have shaped our capital and its arboreal legacy.
As part of the wider Wellington Heritage Festival, this 2-hour author-led walking tour guides you through highlights from 'Capital Trees' to trace the living legacies of the city’s rich tree heritage, including arguments around heritage tree listing, the vulnerability of heritage trees, biodiversity, trees as monuments and more. Starts at the Supreme Court and concludes at Te Papa. In the event of bad weather, a presentation covering highlights from the route will take place at Te Papa, and registered attendees will be notified in advance.

Leonard Cockayne devised a schema for native plant conservation at Ōtari. On this walk with Dr Carol West, you’ll learn about the four elements of the scheme and see examples of those that he specifically oversaw the establishment of, along with others that have been implemented more recently.

events.id: Heritage Tour at the Haunted Inverlochy House-Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Heritage Tour at the Haunted Inverlochy House
events.venue: Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington
events.long_description:
Celebrate Halloween with a cuppa and a historic tour of the haunted Inverlochy House. Inverlochy House is a Victorian mansion designed by local architect Thomas Turnbull for the Macdonald family in the late 1870s. In the mid 1920s until 1980 it was divided into nine flats and known as the Inverlochy Flats. Since 1987 it has been the home of Inverlochy Art School. Inverlochy House has had a reputation for being haunted since the 1970s and has been the subject of an ongoing paranormal investigation by several NZ and international groups over the years.

Tour runs for approximately one hour. Stay in town to enjoy dinner at the local cafes in Te Aro.

events.name: After God
events.venue: Circa Theatre, 1 Taranaki St, Wellington
events.long_description:
From the creators of the wildly praised, fiercely original verbatim plays TRANSMISSION and TRANSMISSION:BETA, the New Zealand premiere of AFTER GOD is a theatrical journey across continents and conversations, with one of Aotearoa’s most distinguished actors, Michael Hurst, joining director Miranda Harcourt and writer Stuart McKenzie to explore big questions about meaning, madness and metaphysics.

With a hungry mind and burning questions, McKenzie hits the road — travelling from Wellington to Kathmandu, London and New York. Along the way, he encounters a vivid cast of real-life characters: theologians, Tibetan rinpoches, philosophers, cosmologists, taxi drivers, hotel receptionists, a famous singing nun — and his own mother. Each has their own radically different way of making sense of existence.

Created entirely from real conversations, AFTER GOD is a new verbatim theatre work, transforming interviews, ideas and personal stories into an exhilarating theatrical experience.

It’s a funny, provocative and hopeful exploration of what we believe, what keeps us going and what it means to be alive right now.

events.long_description:
Experience Stonehenge Aotearoa at its most breathtaking — as the sun dips below the Wairarapa horizon.
Our Sunset Guided Tour blends astronomy, storytelling, and the natural beauty of twilight for an evening you will never forget.

Led by one of our knowledgeable guides, this 90-minute experience explores how ancient cultures used the Sun to track time and mark the turning of the seasons. You’ll discover the scientific and cultural thinking behind the Henge’s unique Southern Hemisphere design before watching the sunset alignment from inside the stone circle.

Duration and Schedule
• Allow: Approximately 90 minutes
• Start Time: Begins one hour before sunset
• Availability: Offered any day with advance booking

events.id: The Quickest Route to Salvation-BATS Theatre, 1 Kent Tce, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: The Quickest Route to Salvation
events.venue: BATS Theatre, 1 Kent Tce, Wellington
events.long_description:
If you were faced with the inability to make decisions under pressure, would you outsource your decision-making to a collective consciousness of complete strangers?

When Sol, usually paralysed by everyday decision-making, enrolls in The Seer’s experimental neurological clinical trial, the audience is plugged in as the collective consciousness. They decide in real time how Sol navigates their setbacks. Enter Sol’s mind, where four distinct "Neurons" advocate for each of their conflicting responses to Sol’s dilemmas.

There are many unique mechanics to marvel at. The Branching Narrative gives the audience a unique chance to act as Sol's decision-makers, using voting panels to determine how the narrative progresses in real-time. The Original Score changes Dynamically depending on audience choices throughout the show, and the narrative branches into one of Four Different Endings. The branches feature Abstract Movement and Dance, giving the audience a unique perspective on their choices. There is no way to hear every song, and see every scene in just one night, each show is unique.

events.id: OVO (ITALY) NZ TOUR - WLG-Valhalla, Wellington-Valhalla
events.name: OVO (ITALY) NZ TOUR - WLG
events.venue: Valhalla, Wellington
events.long_description:
For many of us, music can be like a drug. At first everything and anything feels and is beyond amazing, but over time as our consumption increases, this magical euphoria wears off to a hollow and crushing emptiness. The now discerning music addict desperately searches for that new thing that will make them feel the high that they once had. But it gets harder to again feel this way. Until they stumble across something so unique, original, and idiosyncratic they cannot help but feel giddy, childish excitement.

OvO are one of those bands. Curiously infuriating yet dangerously exhilarating in their inability to be pigeon hold into genre or specific sound. Deftly navigating between noise rock, doom, extreme and blackened metal, industrial sludge and even electronica. “Decibel Magazine” have perhaps described them best by hailing the bands sound as “a David Lynch dance party”. Italy’s OvO, continue to rewrite the definition of what alternative music can be. Something which New Zealand audiences can look forward to seeing this October 2026.

Formed by Stefania Pedretti and Bruno Dorella in Milan, Italy in the late 90s. OvO have taken their inspiration from the likes of Suicide, Swans, and Diamana Galas. Centred around the ear piercing banshee-like vocals of Stefania, and a constant guitar drone and dark menace as the undercurrent of their songs. Bruno, equally essential in their music, pounds a stripped down drum-set as if he were the leader of an invading war party. Coupled with intensive percussion samples to help craft a unique and experimental sound.

With 25 years as a band, 11 albums behind them (including their most recent Gemma), over 1000 shows/festivals across the globe, and sharing stages with many of the biggest names in experimental music; Godflesh, Lightning Bolt, Thurston Moore, Sleepytime Gorilla Music, Psychic TV, Dillinger Escape Plan, Big Brave, Ufomammut, among others - New Zealand audiences have their chance to see one of the most unique and experienced bands still active.

events.venue: Moon, Wellington
events.long_description:
BLOOD MOON: HALLOWEEN AT MOON
A thrilling pre-Halloween night of music to featuring some of the hottest bands in Wellington right now - you do not want to miss this one...

COME IN COSTUME!

The acts performing for you are:

✧ CATTAILS
Cattails bring indie-rock from the murky ponds of Te Aro. Coming off headline shows at Valhalla and Meow, Cattails are ready for a night of tunes in Newtown. Blood Moon will debut new songs of this exciting new band who have just recorded their debut single. Cattails have been described as Basketball dunking music- make of that what you will; Cattails will bring a thrilling set.
Cattails is Tyler Curtis (drums), Duncan Petre (guitar), Daniel Walters (guitar), Quentin Stark (piano), Molly Sussex (bass) and Ben Kenny (vocals).

✧ BOYBAND
A semi-chance meetup at a party, a shared love of Aunty Mena’s and a well-timed Hotel Bristol group chat. These are just a few of the things that make Boyband the most fertile band in Wellington. These Boys are extremely ready to bring their blend of pop, neo-soul, and alternative music to the stage at Blood Moon, with the goal of hitting you where it hurts, soothing you where it matters most, and getting you moving!
Boyband is Ellen Lucas (drums), Siena Mckenzie Smith (guitar), Evie White (guitar), Grace Gillanders (bass) and Millie Aislabie (vocals).

✧ HER DEAD BRIDE
Her Dead Bride is a Wellington-based band blending raw energy, distortion, and emotion, inspired by NZ Post 2000's Shoegaze, Duster, and Title Fight. Formed in 2025, the four-piece are releasing their debut single, \Phantom\ on October 23rd!

Under 18s must be accompanied by legal guardian.

events.id: 100 Years of Unity through Sport — New Zealand and India-Frank Kitts Park, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
events.name: 100 Years of Unity through Sport — New Zealand and India
events.venue: Frank Kitts Park, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
This spring, Wellington will celebrate 100 years of sporting connection between India and New Zealand. The city will showcase its strong Indian community and cultural connections. This century milestone traces back to 1926, when an Indian Army hockey team toured New Zealand for the first time, bringing players and communities together. Since then, sport has played an important role in connecting our countries — notably through hockey and cricket, but also across many other sports and exchanges. 

From 23 October to 15 November, Frank Kitts Park and the waterfront promenade will host a free public exhibition. Light Box Historic Walk will feature 10 illuminated light boxes that share stories of Wellington-specific links between India and New Zealand. You’ll also find The Fan Hub on 6 and 7 November as well as 14 and 15 November. Enjoy a feast with local food truck favourites, offering a taste of Wellington's rich culinary scene. Or start the day with sunrise yoga sessions hosted by AWHI Yoga against the stunning waterfront backdrop. To cap off all the excitement, the BLACKCAPS take on India three times in Wellington as part of their summer season.

The Sport100 Fan Hub is proudly delivered through collaboration between WellingtonNZ, Sport New Zealand, Wellington City Council, Cricket Wellington, and New Zealand Cricket, creating a festive gathering place for locals and visitors to connect, celebrate, and enjoy the atmosphere whilst Wellington hosts cricketing giants India in the capital.

events.id: Cornelia Parker-City Gallery Wellington-Wellington NZ
events.name: Cornelia Parker
events.venue: City Gallery Wellington
events.long_description:
After three years of closure, the newly renovated and strengthened City Gallery Wellington Te Whare Toi will host the art of Cornelia Parker. The British visual artist is best known for her innovative and contemporary sculpture and installation art. Her large-scale, immersive installations explore themes of destruction and reconstruction, transformation and metamorphosis. Objects are exploded, crushed, and suspended in a world upended and remade anew.
Curated by independent UK-based curator Andrea Schlieker and City Gallery Wellington’s Senior Curator Aaron Lister, City Gallery Wellington’s exhibition will encompass Parker’s long career as an artist. This includes an immersive sound-and-light installation, ‘Stolen Thunder’. The work gathers the sounds of approaching storms from around the globe and across time. The exhibition will also showcase her paintings, photos, films, and sculptures.
“I have always said this is the one exhibition I want to do before I die,” said Charlotte Davy, Ringatohu Toi Director, Art and City Gallery Wellington. “I have been following Cornelia Parker’s work for the last twenty years. Bringing her mischievous, dark, and literally explosive work to Wellington is incredible.” 
Parker’s work often fills entire rooms and invites the viewer to move through and around the art. Given its physical scale, the blank canvas of the reopened gallery offers the perfect opportunity to host the exhibition. The exhibition will kick off in October 2026 and run through March 2027. 
Charlotte notes the exhibition’s themes are also of particular relevance to Wellington. “I hope that the exhibition and our return to Te Ngākau Civic Square will reflect our city and also help remake it. We are looking forward to opening with a bang.”
Hero image: © Cornelia Parker. Courtesy of the artist and Frith Street Gallery, London

events.long_description:
New Jersey hell-raisers Lorna Shore make their first-ever appearance in New Zealand this October. For the past 15 years, the band has pushed beyond the confines of the heavy band genre. Since forming in 2009, Lorna Shore has evolved into a powerhouse of intense brutality and melodic sorcery. To the mainstream, their signature brand of deathcore has become infamous. Their 2020 album ‘Immortal’, along with the guttural vocal acrobatics of vocalist Will Ramos, has catapulted the group beyond cult status and into global renown. 
Lorna Shore offer the ultimate meeting point between unbridled catharsis, raw emotion, searing sonic aggression and cinematic beauty. Their fifth studio album, 2025’s ‘I Feel The Everblack Festering Within Me’, continues to galvanise a significant fanbase. For the Wellington show at Shed 6, they will be joined by fellow American heavy hitters in The Acacia Strain and local New Zealand death metallers Organectomy.

events.venue: Circa Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Inside Circa Theatre’s waterfront venue, you’ll find two performance spaces. Both offer a smorgasbord of professional theatre throughout the year. Playwrights from international heavy hitters to brilliant Kiwi voices are represented. It also includes programming from comedies and cabarets to contemporary dance and pantomime. 
Before or after your show, visit the on-site café, brasserie and restaurant, Chouchou. It opens out onto a deck, where you can take in views across the harbour. Look up to admire the art installation above. Called ‘Velarium’, it undulates in the wind, mirroring the water in the harbour. 
Circa Theatre began its life in 1976. A breakaway group of actors and theatre practitioners decided that Aotearoa needed a new and innovative approach to theatre. Five decades later, it is still pushing boundaries, making people laugh and cry, and creating theatrical memories. 
If you don’t have your own Circa memory yet, there’s an opportunity to create one nearly every night of the week.

events.long_description:
AWHI Yoga and Wellbeing’s accredited 200hr YTT program is a comprehensive and thorough journey into becoming a 200 hr certified Yoga Teacher. We are the only vinyasa yoga teacher training in the world that blends Te Ao Māori and ancient yoga wisdoms, offering a uniquely 'Aotearoa' experience while retaining universal relevance for teaching and practicing yoga in any part of the world.

Our training is suitable for individuals interested in becoming a yoga teacher, or those looking to take a personal journey towards deepening your own practice and knowledge. Either way, we guarantee a transformative and life-changing experience that will deepen your relationship to yoga, others, Aotearoa and your self.

Our uniquely Aotearoa Teacher Training explores the beautiful marriage between ancient Yoga and Te Ao Māori teachings over five separate modules during our three months together. Our course follows the Māori hauora/wellbeing model of Te Whare Tapa Whā, which takes the same holistic view of health taken by traditional Yoga. As we work through each pillar we start tapping into something way greater than ourselves, enabling us to connect with our purpose in life and how we might share this in service to the world!

A $1,000 deposit reserves your spot.

events.long_description:
A waterfront guided walk by Michael Szabo, author of ‘Wild Wellington Ngā Taonga Taiao: A guide to the wildlife and wild places of Te Upoko-o-te-Ika’.

As part of the wider Wellington Heritage Festival, experience the Wellington waterfront with wildlife expert Michael Szabo, who will highlight the nature encounters you can expect at this time of year. The hour-long walk will start at 11am from the Len Lye Water Whirler sculpture near Frank Kitts Park and end at Te Papa’s Bush City.

In the event of bad weather, a presentation covering the stops will take place at Te Papa, and registered attendees will be notified in advance. Meet 15 minutes prior.

events.name: Crime & Punishment Tour: CANCELLED
events.venue: Bolton Street Cemetery, Bolton Street, Wellington
events.long_description:
We’ll take a wander to find those who were responsible, in the earliest days of the settlement of Wellington (and our country) for creating and enforcing the law, those who sat in the law courts, and those who kept incarcerated the people who failed to observe the law. There’s duellists, police and military law enforcers, and even a criminal or two.

Tours start at the Bolton Street Cemetery Museum, Lower Bolton Street, and will last 1.5 hours. Cost $10 per person, but free for children. Each tour will be limited to 20 people, so book early to avoid disappointment.

This event is not suitable for wheelchairs. Please wear sturdy shoes, as some of the paths are steep and can be slippery. Care is required.

events.long_description:
Looking for a creative night out in Wellington? Join us for a fun beginner-friendly adults painting class in a bar!

Our artist guides you step-by-step, so absolutely no art experience is needed. It’s the perfect excuse to switch off, get creative, and try something a little different.

Whether you’re coming along solo, planning a date night, or organising a catch-up with friends, Paintvine is all about good vibes, creativity, and having fun while you paint – you might even surprise yourself with what you can create!

Drinks: No drinks are included in the ticket price, but drinks are available for purchase.

Food: A delicious menu will be available to purchase throughout the event.

What is Paintvine?
It’s a fun social painting class where our artists will run you through step-by-step instructions on how to create your very own masterpiece in a fun and relaxed bar setting. Perfect for dates, catching up with mates or for meeting new friends!

We provide all the materials you need (high-quality canvas, acrylic paint, brushes). All you need to bring is your creative spirit! Our events are held in licensed venues, so you can purchase drinks to sip on while you paint. At the end of the night, you’ll leave with a painting you created yourself – you might even surprise yourself with what you can achieve!

For tickets, future events, FAQs and more info head to the Paintvine website ⇒ paintvine.co.nz

events.name: New Zealand Cricket: Summer Season
events.venue: Hnry Stadium and Cello Basin Reserve, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
It looks like New Zealand Cricket (NZC) has smashed it for six. The 2026-27 international home season of cricket promises an exciting few months of action across the country. Wellington has scored six major opportunities to see the BLACKCAPS and WHITE FERNS in action. Three formidable opponents are travelling to New Zealand’s shores. The Indian, Bangladeshi, and Sri Lankan teams have booked their tickets for Aotearoa and will play tests, ODIs, and T20 matches against the Kiwi women’s and men’s teams. 
The Indian men’s team will be particularly busy during their visit. With twelve matches booked against the BLACKCAPS, it will be the most internationals scheduled for an Indian men’s tour in NZC history. Fans will get their chance to see them duke it out in all three formats across the capital, beginning with a T20 at Hnry Stadium on 27 October. 
Make sure you don’t miss the WHITE FERNS. They host Bangladesh in Wellington in a T20 and ODI, during their only home tour of the summer. The Wellington schedule finishes with a visit from Sri Lanka for an ODI against the BLACKCAPS on 19 January at the Cello Basin Reserve.   
With games split across Hnry Stadium and Cello Basin Reserve, the city will be bouncing with life. The 2025/26 season saw bumper crowds, and our men's and women's sides are set to build on this exciting momentum.

events.id: Tuesday Jewellery-making: 8-week course for Beginners-Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Tuesday Jewellery-making: 8-week course for Beginners
events.venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
events.long_description:
This class is beginner level only, with each student following the class project.

It starts Tue 27 October and runs for 8 weeks ill Tue 15 December, 5.30pm - 8pm.

Our popular weeknight classes are the best way for beginners to get into jewellery-making in a lively, warm and friendly environment.

The stone-setting process teaches you many fundamental techniques in one project!

We start with basic ring-making and stone-setting in copper or brass. Students will learn measuring, texturing, shaping, cutting and soldering.

Then we move on to making a practice ring set with a Cabochon stone (a cabochon has a flat bottom and a smooth, domed top) in a Bezel Setting.

As you work through your practice ring and setting, you can move on to working in silver and produce another ring with a cabochon stone that you really love. This way, you will learn the basics as you go on your practice ring, before taking the next step in costly silver.

This class has all materials included in the class fee!

Each student receives a carefully curated materials pack including copper or brass, sterling and fine silver for your ring-making projects, as well as two stones from our supply so you get a good stone for your level of experience.

We have loads of gorgeous stones of a range of colours, and they are all appropriate for beginner settings.

Our booking system asks for payment to be made via credit card, Afterpay or PayPal on booking. If you do not have access to these payment methods or need to pay your course fee over time, please email us to arrange this ;)

Explore ancient wisdom on consciousness, karma and the journey beyond the body—and discover how understanding death transforms life.

Death & the Afterlife

We all know death is coming—but do we really know what happens when it arrives? Discover the ancient wisdom of consciousness, karma, and the journey beyond the body—and why understanding death can change the way we live.

End the session on a high note with a delicious plant-based dinner, dessert, and good conversation.

Hriman brings together a rich background in philosophy, contextual studies, and the arts with 20 years spent living as a monk. Through thought-provoking articles, dynamic workshops, and engaging presentations, he brings the psychology of yoga into a contemporary context, making its insights practical, accessible, and relevant. events.name: Understanding and Supporting Your Neurodivergent Child: A Practical Parent Course
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.
If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.
This course is designed for parents and caregivers of neurodivergent tamariki who want practical, evidence-informed strategies to better support their child’s wellbeing, behaviour, and participation at home and school.
Across three sessions, we will explore the foundations of neurodiversity, including different neurotypes, strengths-based perspectives, and neuroaffirming language. You will gain insight into sensory processing, regulation, and the critical role of connection and co-regulation in supporting your child.
The course also provides guidance on navigating Aotearoa New Zealand’s health, education, and disability systems, including how to access supports and advocate effectively for your child. We will explore common challenges such as school refusal, burnout, and meltdowns, with practical strategies for prevention, in-the-moment support, and recovery.
There will be opportunities for discussion, reflection, and shared learning, as well as a Q&A-style panel session incorporating both professional and lived experience perspectives.
This is a group-based learning environment (not individual therapy), with an emphasis on practical tools, connection, and empowerment.
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.id: LA DISPUTE - NO ONE WAS DRIVING THE CAR AOTEAROA TOUR - WELLINGTON-Valhalla, Wellington-Valhalla
events.name: LA DISPUTE - NO ONE WAS DRIVING THE CAR AOTEAROA TOUR - WELLINGTON
events.venue: Valhalla, Wellington
events.long_description:
The post-hardcore innovators of La Dispute, known for their emotionally charged lyrics and ambitious compositions, are hitting Aotearoa this October. These shows will celebrate their critically acclaimed fifth studio album, No One Was Driving The Car.
It’s been six years since La Dispute released their last album, Panorama. Since then, the Michigan post-hardcore band—made up of Jordan Dreyer on vocals, Brad Vander Lugt on drums, Chad Morgan-Sterenberg and Corey Stroffolino on guitar, and Adam Vass on bass—dealt with the stagnance of the pandemic, celebrated the ten-year anniversaries of Wildlife and Rooms Of The House, and began working on No One Was Driving The Car. The fifth studio LP is the first entirely produced by the group, and it came together in Grand Rapids and Detroit, the United Kingdom, Australia, and the Philippines: “I think the change in environment was really helpful to breathing new life into the process each time we came back to it,” Dreyer says.
Partly inspired by the 2017 psychological thriller First Reformed, No One Was Driving The Car reckons with malaise in the shadow of the looming apocalypse, which has noticeably been worsened by the advancement of tech. The title comes from a quote from a police officer Dreyer read in a news article about a lethal self-driving Tesla crash, an absurd event which raises questions about the amount of control we have in our own lives. In fourteen dynamic tracks, the band grapples with the existential topic and the human need to find comfort and a sense of security in an existence where we’re often thrust into chaos without permission. Dreyer yells with a more primal sense and sings in a more refined way, and the guitars have a sharper edge than ever before. “As much as I don’t enjoy the creative process because it’s taxing and often not fun, I also think it’s the most fun that I ever have,” Dreyer contemplates. “It’s the revelations you make, the breakthroughs. It’s banging your head against a wall and suddenly something clicks in a way that feels almost divine, like it came from somewhere else.”
This event is at Meow

events.id: Global ChangeLabs: Breakfast w/ Banny Banerjee & co (WLG)-30 Waring Taylor Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
events.name: Global ChangeLabs: Breakfast w/ Banny Banerjee & co (WLG)
events.venue: 30 Waring Taylor Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Designing Desirable Transformations in a Complex World

With Banny Banerjee and a panel of Aotearoa changemakers.

The challenges we face today; from technological disruption and climate change to organisational transformation and societal change... are increasingly complex, interconnected and difficult to solve through any single intervention.

So how do we design transformations in the context of complex, systemic, and interconnected challenges?

Join us for a special conversation with Banny Banerjee, founder of Global ChangeLabs and Adjunct Professor at Stanford University’s Doerr School of Sustainability.

Before launching Global ChangeLabs, Banny founded Stanford ChangeLabs and spent two decades working across fields and exploring how to approach complex and deeply integrated challenges and design genuinely transformative pathways. Earlier in his career, Banny worked at IDEO during the period when the firm was helping pioneer what became known as Design Thinking.

For this special event, Banny will share insights about how conventional wisdom and deterministic approaches are increasingly ill suited to address the deeply systemic and integrated nature of our challenges.  He will share how his work across sectors - business, government, technology, sustainability and social systems indicates the need for new capacities, leadership models, organizational functions, and platforms to address an uncertain and increasingly complex future.  Given his work on how to leverage a diversity of perspectives, we will also be joined by a panel of local change-makers to explore what these ideas might mean in the Aotearoa New Zealand context.

We’ll explore:

How do we embrace the complexity rather than expect isolated solutions to work?

How must we reframe design and innovation to shape interventions that shift the trajectory of a system?

How do we effectively combine different disciplines, perspectives and ways of thinking?

How do we identify opportunities for meaningful intervention and make them actionable?

What new forms of leadership, collaboration and organisational architecture might be needed for systemic transformation?

How might Aotearoa NZ become a place to demonstrate transformative ways of approaching complex challenges.  What can Aotearoa NZ contribute and learn... Especially, as we navigate our own economic, technological, environmental and societal transitions?

This will be an opportunity to hear a distinctive international perspective, connect it with the experiences of people working on complex challenges here in Aotearoa, and consider what it might mean to design the conditions for a different future.

Who is this for?

Anyone working to create meaningful change in complex environments: including leaders, designers, strategists, innovators, entrepreneurs, policymakers, researchers, funders, social-sector practitioners and people working across organisational and sector boundaries.

Come curious.

Bring a complex challenge.

Leave with new perspectives on where, and how, change might be possible.

We'd love for you to join us for this breakfast event, to explore how we can Designing Desirable Transformations in a Complex World

🔹 Date & Time: Wednesday 28 October 2026, 8 - 9:30am
🔹 Location: Precinct Flex, 30 Waring Taylor St (Te Whanganui ā Tara / Wellington NZ)
🔹 Registration: $20 unwaged | $45 waged (To cover venue hire, coffee, tea & breakfast pastries)

Ngā manaakitanga | We look forward to seeing you there!

events.venue: Hawkes Bay,Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Shea McAleese: The Evolution of a Four-Time Olympian
What does it take to perform on the world's biggest stage?

And perhaps more importantly, what happens when the cheering stops, the jersey comes off, and it's time to reinvent yourself all over again?

Join four-time Olympian and New Zealand hockey legend Shea McAleese for an inspiring Learning Lunch exploring the highs, challenges and lessons of a life spent pursuing excellence.

From a young Hawke's Bay athlete with a dream to representing New Zealand at four Olympic Games and four Commonwealth Games, Shea's journey offers a fascinating insight into commitment, resilience and what it really takes to perform at an elite level.

But this isn't simply a story about sport.

It's about leadership, teamwork, personal growth and learning how to evolve through different chapters of life.

Today, Shea works as an international coach and leadership mentor, helping individuals and teams perform at their best. Drawing on lessons from elite sport, he shares a practical and human perspective on building trust, developing culture and creating environments where people thrive.

Expect honest stories, valuable insights and a fascinating look behind the scenes of life as an Olympian, coach and leader.

Meet Shea 🎤

Shea McAleese is one of New Zealand's most celebrated hockey players and a proud son of Hawke's Bay. Over a 16-year international career he represented the Black Sticks 320 times, competing at four Olympic Games and four Commonwealth Games. Since retiring from international hockey, he has transitioned into international coaching and leadership development, working with elite teams and building a global following through his coaching platform, Inside Hockey.

What We'll Explore
• The realities of competing at four Olympic Games
• Lessons from elite sport that apply to everyday life
• Leadership, trust and building high-performing teams
• The transition from athlete to coach
• Resilience, growth and adapting through life's different chapters

events.id: America After Trump: What will it mean for Asia and the World?-Hunter Building Kelburn Parade, Kelburn, Wellington 6012, New Zealand-Humanitix
events.name: America After Trump: What will it mean for Asia and the World?
events.venue: Hunter Building Kelburn Parade, Kelburn, Wellington 6012, New Zealand
events.long_description:
With the U.S. midterm elections just around the corner, the race to replace Donald Trump is just about to kick off. In this lecture, one of the sharpest observers of contemporary American foreign policy, Zack Cooper, will discuss how the American approach to foreign policy is changing and explore what a post-Trump world view might mean for Asia in particular.

Zack Cooper is a senior fellow at the American Enterprise Institute, where he studies US strategy in Asia, including alliance dynamics and US-China competition. He also teaches at Princeton University. He previously worked at the National Security Council and in the Office of the Secretary of Defense. Dr. Cooper is the author of Tides of Fortune: The Rise and Decline of Great Militaries from Yale University Press. He has also co-authored books, reports, and articles on US strategy and alliances in Asia. His writing has appeared in academic journals and popular press, including International Security, Security Studies, Foreign Affairs, the New York Times, the Washington Post, and the Wall Street Journal, among other outlets. Dr. Cooper graduated from Princeton University with a PhD and an MA in security studies and an MPA in international relations. He received a BA in public policy from Stanford University.

Refreshments will be provid at the event.

events.long_description:
Everyone is welcome to this fun class! Whether you have a little more experience, or are starting from scratch, if you want to draw people, this workshop is for you.

Here you will be closely tutored in how to draw people, from faces to anatomy, and you will learn technical skills while having fun in an encouraging environment.

In this class, artists will learn and extend their skills with drawing and painting.

Perfect for both beginners and more experienced artists, Ellie will help the students experiment and learn while having fun and creating wonderful pieces of art. Our classes builds self-confidence, traditional techniques, and creative experimentation.

We will focus on anatomy, and over the 2 hour session will work through different techniques of drawing faces and bodies, with the support of having a life model there to draw.

The tutor, Ellie Lee-Duncan is an artist, writer, and curator based in Kirikiriroa Hamilton. They have an MA in Art History and have taught classes at the Waikato Society of Art for 8 years. They previously ran Tacit Art Gallery in Hamilton, and have worked at both the Waikato Museum and the Adam Art Gallery.

This event is a fun, safe space for all, including LGBTQ+ and the site includes a gender-neutral bathroom for students.

events.long_description:
F*ck the Small Talk: Wellington #7 🌈
🎟️ Sign up here: https://luma.com/ftst7wellington 🎟️

F*ck the Small Talk has traveled the world from Berlin, Melbourne, London, Lisbon, and Mexico City, to Lisbon and is now coming to Wellington! 🇳🇿


📦 WHAT'S THIS ABOUT?

FTST is a one-of-a-kind social experience where strangers come together for an afternoon of meaningful, fun, and deep conversation. It’s also just a different & cool way of meeting new people by getting a bit out of your comfort zone and skipping the small talk!

Join us for games, talks, and connections with friends you haven’t met yet. Join if you get annoyed after being asked what you do, where you are from, and how long you have been in Wellington every single time you meet someone. If you feel that there are better questions in life then this is the place for you. 🙌


🎈 HOW DOES IT WORK?

We start with a short & sweet intro talk followed by a few light-hearted group games to warm up. Don't worry, nothing too awkward! After that, we split you up into small groups and start with the conversation rounds (with 3-4 people). We'll have awesome question cards that will guide the flow of the conversation. You’ll never have to speak in public if you don’t want to!


🕹 HOW TO JOIN?

Take 2 minutes to fill out our form 👇🏼
https://luma.com/ftst7wellington

Our events are limited to 30 handpicked guests to ensure a cozy atmosphere. We prioritize a balance in gender and cultural diversity, making each gathering a unique blend of perspectives! If you're invited you'll receive an invite with a special link via our ticketing platform Luma :)


🧧 HOW MUCH IS IT?

The cost to attend is NZD 23-28 and includes the following:

⏰ 3 hours of facilitated and curated activities
🥪 Light snacks to keep the energy going (only if outdoors)
👥 A space to meet new people in the least boring way possible
💛 Supporting our mission to slowly eliminate small talk around the world
🎫 Also includes those pesky ticket fees!


🌳 WHERE IS IT?

We host our events in awesome cafes, rooftops, and bars across the city. We only reveal the location to ticket holders 24 hours before the event.


💛 WHAT THEY SAY

🗣 “Great way to connect with people in a more meaningful way. Get to the heart of the matter, dive straight into what really counts!” - Matthias


🗣 “This is the kind of activity humanity needs every weekend. Thank you for all.” - Sonya


🗣 “F*ck the Small Talk changes the narrative from "Where are you from?" to "When was the last time you laughed uncontrollably?" and I think that's beautiful.” - Monika


🗣 “I loved F*ck the small talk, I was a little bit nervous at first but they are pros at making you feel comfortable with the rest of the group, the activities are really fun and I enjoyed every second (consider that the one who's saying this is very, very shy). Give it a try!” - Brenda


🗣 "it’s a wonderful experience, it’s like being a kid again, when you were at the park, playing with other kids, and just decided you were going to be best friends for the next hours. Maybe you’ll never see those kids again. But that hour was amazing because you both opened up and trusted each other." - Sara


🗣 “Lively, interesting, introspective, completely open and no judgement. Everyone that joined was ready for great conversation and helped with different perspectives. So much fun! I can't wait for the next one! “ - Yaz


Check out our 100+ Google reviews: https://goo.gl/maps/TpZy77bfPFkGoikn7 🫶


🤓 FAQ

• Can I come alone?
Of course, in fact, we encourage it! 99% of people do.


• I signed up but never got an invite. Why?
We usually get a high volume of sign-ups yet we like to keep it cozy & only about 30 people. We believe this is a good number to ensure an awesome experience! Please try again next time if do not receive an invite - no hard feelings 💛


• Why do you charge?
We value our time and put a lot of love, planning, and effort into creating & designing these experiences. ♥️ This is our project/business and what we give to the world and we think everything should be a fair exchange! However, money should never be the reason for people not to attend. If you can’t afford it simply get in touch with us :)


• I'm digging this! Can I get involved somehow?
Sure thing, send us a message!


• Can I bring my cute dog/llama?
It depends on where the event is! Message us to make sure. But it's always a YES in our hearts.


• Can I get a refund if I can't make it?
Unfortunately, we do not offer refunds or ticket transfers to another event date if you cannot attend with a notice of less than 5 days notice. BUTTTT feel free to pass on your ticket to a friend, provided they also sign up for the form :)

events.id: New Zealand String Quartet presents: Legend | Wellington-Prefab Hall, 14 Jessie St, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: New Zealand String Quartet presents: Legend | Wellington
events.venue: Prefab Hall, 14 Jessie St, Wellington
events.long_description:
The New Zealand String Quartet presents their 2026 Season: Storytellers.

Across a three-part Wellington series, we'll explore three distinct programmes: Origins, Transform and Legend. We’ll boldly explore more compositional voices than ever before, beginning with classical masterworks that resonate through the centuries, through to modern-day Grammy winners and the distinctive voices of Aotearoa. The three string quartets of Benjamin Britten form the heart of our 2026 Season, to mark the 50th anniversary of the composer’s death.

Storytellers showcases a rich cross-section of our society and celebrates the art of storytelling through music. Join us in 2026 as together we explore these musical stories.

PROGRAMME:
Sara Arain The Internal Eclipse
Ludwig van Beethoven String Quartet No. 11, in F minor, Op. 95 ‘Serioso’
Interval
Benjamin Britten String Quartet No. 3, in G major, Op. 94
Claire Cowan Sweet Suite: Hansel & Gretel highlights for String Quartet

The programme opens with emerging composer Sara Arain’s The Internal Eclipse, selected by the Quartet as the winning work in their competition for New Zealand School of Music – Te Kōkī students. Committed to supporting the next generation of composers, the NZSQ will perform this beautiful work - based on an ancient Persian mystical tale - across five dates on their Legend tour.   

The programme continues with Ludwig van Beethoven’s high-octane and form-breaking String Quartet No. 11, Op. 95, that continues to surprise and thrill audiences to this day.

To complete their year-long tribute to the fiftieth anniversary of Benjamin Britten’s death, the NZSQ will perform his third and final string quartet. This quietly luminous piece, based on themes from his final opera, Death in Venice, serves as a poignant musical farewell, made even more profound by the fact it was the last major work Britten ever composed.

The Quartet will bring their 2026 Season to a jubilant close with acclaimed Aotearoa composer Claire Cowan’s ‘Sweet Suite: Hansel and Gretel highlights’ - a magical reimagining of her internationally celebrated ballet score, which was the first full-length ballet composed by a New Zealand woman and enjoyed an incredible 5-week, sold-out national tour by the Royal New Zealand Ballet in 2019.

The concert programme, crafted in the NZSQ’s signature style, aims to engage audiences of all levels of familiarity with chamber music. Each piece is preceded by a friendly and informative introduction by the Quartet members, shedding light on the stories behind the music, making it an enriching experience for everyone. The NZSQ is looking forward to welcoming you all to this special evening of music and storytelling!

events.id: LA DISPUTE - NO ONE WAS DRIVING THE CAR AOTEAROA TOUR - AUCKLAND-Valhalla, Wellington-Valhalla
events.name: LA DISPUTE - NO ONE WAS DRIVING THE CAR AOTEAROA TOUR - AUCKLAND
events.venue: Valhalla, Wellington
events.long_description:
The post-hardcore innovators of La Dispute, known for their emotionally charged lyrics and ambitious compositions, are hitting Aotearoa this October. These shows will celebrate their critically acclaimed fifth studio album, No One Was Driving The Car.

It’s been six years since La Dispute released their last album, Panorama. Since then, the Michigan post-hardcore band—made up of Jordan Dreyer on vocals, Brad Vander Lugt on drums, Chad Morgan-Sterenberg and Corey Stroffolino on guitar, and Adam Vass on bass—dealt with the stagnance of the pandemic, celebrated the ten-year anniversaries of Wildlife and Rooms Of The House, and began working on No One Was Driving The Car. The fifth studio LP is the first entirely produced by the group, and it came together in Grand Rapids and Detroit, the United Kingdom, Australia, and the Philippines: “I think the change in environment was really helpful to breathing new life into the process each time we came back to it,” Dreyer says.

Partly inspired by the 2017 psychological thriller First Reformed, No One Was Driving The Car reckons with malaise in the shadow of the looming apocalypse, which has noticeably been worsened by the advancement of tech. The title comes from a quote from a police officer Dreyer read in a news article about a lethal self-driving Tesla crash, an absurd event which raises questions about the amount of control we have in our own lives. In fourteen dynamic tracks, the band grapples with the existential topic and the human need to find comfort and a sense of security in an existence where we’re often thrust into chaos without permission. Dreyer yells with a more primal sense and sings in a more refined way, and the guitars have a sharper edge than ever before. “As much as I don’t enjoy the creative process because it’s taxing and often not fun, I also think it’s the most fun that I ever have,” Dreyer contemplates. “It’s the revelations you make, the breakthroughs. It’s banging your head against a wall and suddenly something clicks in a way that feels almost divine, like it came from somewhere else.”

This event is at Hollywood Avondale in Auckland

Tickets here

events.long_description:
DUE TO OVERWHELMING DEMAND, MUDHONEY HAS UPGRADED VENUES TO MEOW NUI.
For the first time in over a decade, Mudhoney return to New Zealand for a run of intimate shows. Renowned for their ferocious live performances, the band continue to deliver the same high-voltage mix of sludgy riffs, pounding rhythms and Mark Arm's unmistakable snarl that made them one of the most influential rock bands of their era.
Formed in Seattle in 1988, Mudhoney helped define the sound that would become known as grunge, combining garage rock, punk and heavy distortion into something raw, loud and entirely their own. As one of the cornerstone acts of legendary independent label Sub Pop, the band became a crucial influence on the explosion of alternative rock that followed, with tracks like 'Touch Me I'm Sick' and 'Suck You Dry' remaining enduring underground classics.
More than 35 years on, Mudhoney remain as vital as ever, continuing to release acclaimed new music and proving night after night why they are regarded as one of the greatest live rock bands of their generation.
"When it comes to grunge, or even just Seattle, I think there was one band that made the definitive music of the time. It wasn't us or Nirvana, but Mudhoney. Nirvana delivered it to the world, but Mudhoney were the band of that time and sound." – Eddie Vedder (Pearl Jam)
A rare chance to experience genuine grunge royalty up close.

events.long_description:
Overview

Discover the key numbers that drive profit and learn how to maximise your returns without working harder.

More work does not always mean more profit

You can have a full calendar, a busy team and plenty of sales coming through the door—and still wonder where the profit has gone.

Often, the issue is not how much work the business is doing.

It is the type of work, the customers being served, the costs that quietly blow out, and whether pricing reflects the true value being delivered.

Profit: Find Your Sweet Spot is a practical 90-minute session designed to help local business owners identify the numbers and decisions that have the greatest effect on profit.

During the session, we will look at:

Which customers, products or job types make you the most money
Which parts of the business may be consuming time without producing enough return
Where time, materials, discounts, stock, rework or debtor costs may be blowing out
Simple ways to protect your margin when unexpected costs arise
How to deliver more value to your best customers
Where pricing may need to be reviewed or better aligned

You will leave with a clearer picture of your business’s profit sweet spot and one practical action you can begin applying immediately.

This is not about working harder, chasing every possible sale or making dramatic changes overnight.

It is about understanding what is already happening inside your business and making more deliberate decisions about where your time, people and resources go.

Who should attend?

This session is suitable for owners of trades, retail, wholesale, manufacturing, professional service and other locally owned businesses.

Event details

Date: 30 October 
Time: 10:30 am–12:00 pm 
Venue: Paraparaumu Beach Golf Club 
Cost: Free

Places are limited, so please register early.

Mum's & Bub's — A 4-Week Connection Series

Join us for a relaxed, expert-led series designed to support you through those early postpartum months - no pressure, no judgement, just a space to connect.

Each week we welcome a different guest expert to share their knowledge and answer your questions on the topics that matter most after having a baby. While you listen, chat and ask away, bub has their own comfy little play space set up right there in the room - so there's no need to juggle or step away.

Sessions are split by age group, so you're with mums at a similar stage

Each day there are three session time options - 10.15am, 11.30am

🚼 Thursdays
Starting Thursday 8th October, running for 4 weeks

Week 1 — Thursday 8th October: Lactation/Feeding/Pumping with Jo from BlissfulBubs

Week 2 — Thursday 15th October: Starting Solids with Dr Julie from Dr Julie Bhosale

Week 3 — Thursday 22nd October: Naturopathic postpartum care with Anna from Anna Reeves Naturopathy

Week 4 — Thursday 29th October: Sleep with Fran from thegentlesleepconsultant

A new guest expert each week, covering key postpartum topics

Open Q&A - bring your questions, nothing is off-limits

A comfy, safe play space for bub within the session

Light morning tea provided

Time to connect with other local mums going through the same stage

☕ BYO coffee welcome (with lid to keep babies safe)

Pricing

$120 for the full 4 weeks (Girl maths $30 per session)

Pricing is per Mum - so twin/multiple mums only need the 1 ticket

What to Know

Feeding, crying and leaving early are all completely okay

We'll come together as a group at the start to introduce ourselves - no pressure to be on time, the doors will stay open, and the expert talk is expected to begin around 20 minutes in

These sessions are suited for first-time or multiple-time mums. Tickets are per mum (twin mums just need the one ticket)

events.id: The Trajectory of the Indian Economy over the Past Four Decades: A Story of Mixed Experiences-16 Kelburn Parade, Kelburn, Wellington 6012, New Zealand-Humanitix
events.name: The Trajectory of the Indian Economy over the Past Four Decades: A Story of Mixed Experiences
events.venue: 16 Kelburn Parade, Kelburn, Wellington 6012, New Zealand
events.long_description: The lecture will discuss India’s developmental experience over the past four decades. Since this is a vast subject, the discussion will be limited to only some of the principal features. India’s experience is one of mixed messages, both positive and negative. India historically recorded a low growth rate, around 3.5%. This was accompanied by a high tariff regime along with bureaucratic controls that have been described as a ‘license permit raj’. India experienced a serious balance of payments crisis in 1991 with foreign reserves barely enough to pay for 2 weeks’ food imports. This set in motion a series of trade liberalisation reforms initiated by the then Finance Minister, Dr Manmohan Singh, consisting of removal of trade barriers and reduction of high tariffs on several items. This propelled India to one of the fastest growing economies accompanied by increase in per capita income and reduction in poverty. India ranks third on aggregate GDP (on PPP) though on per capita GDP she falls well down the list. India’s sizeable middle-class swamps that of the EU and many of the smaller economies thus providing a large market. There has been widespread digitalisation of transactions leading to reduction in corruption. But there has also been a large increase in inequality and according to the World Inequality report, 2026, India is one of the most unequal countries in the world. There is lack of skilled jobs to employ the educated youth making India unable to exploit the advantage of ‘demographic dividend’ she enjoys over China. The talk will compare living standards between India and China.

events.venue: Ngā Pou Ruahine, Level 2, Te Matapihi, 65 Victoria Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
This event will take place in Ngā Pou Ruahine on Level 2 of Te Matapihi.

Between the Lines is a monthly early-evening chamber music series and book club that brings music and literature into conversation. Presented in the beautiful setting of Ngā Pou Ruahine in Te Matapihi, the series invites audiences to listen, think, and chat. No prior knowledge of music or literature is required, just a curious mind.

Taking place monthly from April to October on the final Thursday of each month, Between the Lines has been co-created by New Zealand String Quartet, Orchestra Wellington, and New Zealand School of Music. Each month these organisations will take turns presenting a talented group of musicians to perform music and host discussion on a different literary theme. From devil's bargains to language games, the obsessive tortured artist to the intimate private lives of writers and composers, this book club will delve deep into themes that span across artforms.

Each session will feature carefully selected music and a reading list highlighting the theme of the month. So, arrive solo or bring your book club to Te Matapihi for a new kind of conversation.

The theme of our October musical book club is language games.

Music to be performed: Walton – Façade

Language Games explores the joy, absurdity, and musicality of words.

In the early 20th century, artists began to break language apart and rebuild it in new ways. Meaning became fluid, rhythm took centre stage, and sound itself became a kind of play. Words were no longer just vehicles for ideas, but material to be shaped, stretched, and reimagined.

This programme draws on that spirit of experimentation. Here, language slips between sense and nonsense, clarity and confusion. Familiar patterns are disrupted, and new ones emerge. The result is something playful, unpredictable, and deeply expressive.

Music and speech meet on equal terms. Rhythm becomes meaning. Timing becomes everything. Like a poem that resists easy interpretation, the experience is not about finding a single answer, but about enjoying the movement of thought as it unfolds.

In this world, language is not fixed. It dances, it misbehaves, and it invites us to listen differently.

events.long_description:
Our popular weeknight block classes are the best way for keen makers to get into jewellery making in a lively, warm and friendly environment. This class will be held at our new waterfront location, Market Lane!

The course starts on Thursday 29 October and runs for 8 weeks till Thursday 17 December, 5.30pm-8pm.

This class is designed for students who already have some skills and are ready to develop their craftsmanship in a lively, warm, and supportive environment. Guided by our highly skilled tutors, you’ll build confidence, refine your techniques, and gain the satisfaction of making jewellery that reflects your personal style.

If you’re brand new to jewellery making, we recommend beginning with our Tuesday Evening 8-Week Beginners’ Block, which gives a solid foundation in essential techniques before moving on to this class.

At Level 2, the focus is on precision and technique. Students explore the art of chain making, a classic jewellery making project that develops fine soldering skills and accuracy in construction. This project is an excellent way to build confidence with the torch and create a piece of jewellery that is both functional and beautiful. The finished chain can become a pendant, bracelet, or necklace, or you may choose to adapt it into a design of your own.

At Level 3 and above, the emphasis shifts toward creativity and design development. Students at this stage are encouraged to take on more complex projects, experiment with new and challenging techniques, and bring their own design ideas to life. With the guidance of our skilled and supportive tutors, you’ll learn how to push your skills further, problem-solve during the making process, and refine your eye for detail and design.

Evening classes are not just about the technical side of jewellery making - they are also a chance to slow down, enjoy the process, and be part of a creative community. Many students return term after term, finding the rhythm of regular making both mindful and rewarding.

Please note: this class does not include a materials allowance, giving you the flexibility to choose your own metals, stones, or other materials. You only pay for what you use, making it easier to customise your projects and work at your own pace.

Our booking system asks for full payment at the time of registration (via credit card, PayPal, or AfterPay). If you don’t have access to these options or would like to pay in instalments, please email us and we’ll happily arrange an alternative.

events.venue: 113 Taranki St, Te Aro, Wellington 6011,113 Taranaki St, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand, Wellington
events.long_description:
AI and Authoritarianism: Panel Discussion
Pōneke Anti-Fascist Coalition and Critical Signals invites you to a panel event about the various ways that Generative AI can be, and is being, deployed to advance authoritarianism. Panellists Aditi Tiwari, Dr Mike Joy, Lelitu and Anne Campbell will talk about the authoritarian implications of Generative AI in relation to topics that are important to them, including data sovereignty, workers rights, education, environmental harm, and militarism and surveillance. This will be followed by an open discussion where anyone is free to ask questions, share their own observations about GenAI and authoritarianism, or put forward ideas for resisting this technology.

Please register here for tickets https://buytickets.at/criticalsignals/2462201/share/2426de0105228d20791c50469e358ffa

More about the panellists:
Aditi Tiwari (she/her) on Data Sovereignty and Indigenous Data Sovereignty:
Aditi is a Master of Professional Business Analysis student at Victoria University of Wellington, whose research explores digital leadership, AI governance and Indigenous data sovereignty in AI-enabled public sector systems through a Te Tiriti o Waitangi lens. Her work examines the intersections of emerging technologies, power, accountability and data sovereignty, particularly how decisions about the collection, ownership and use of data can reinforce existing structural inequalities. As a first-generation migrant and community advocate, Aditi brings both academic and lived perspectives to conversations about digital equity, representation and the concentration of power in technological systems. She is particularly interested in how AI governance can uphold Indigenous rights, strengthen democratic accountability and ensure communities retain meaningful control over their data and digital futures.

Lelitu (it/is) on GenAI and Workers' Rights:
Lelitu is a software engineer in Te Whanganui A Tara with a decade of experience in commercial software development. Its experience has been radicalising at times, driving home the importance of workers rights and protections. It is extremely concerned about how bosses are driving very anti worker practices around the use and adoption of LLMs in the workplace.

Dr Mike Joy (he/him) on Environmental implications of AI:
Dr Mike Joy is a Senior Research Fellow in the School of Geography, Environment and Earth Sciences at Te Herenga Waka Victoria University of Wellington, and an outspoken advocate for environmental protection in New Zealand. His research includes ecological modelling, freshwater bioassessment, environmental policy development, biophysical limits to growth, and the role of energy in society. He has provided expert evidence for high court, environment court and Waitangi Tribunal cases, and has communicated extensively about the influence of vested interests on environmental policy. Mike is the recipient of numerous awards for his research and science communication, including the Morgan Foundation's inaugural River Voice Award, the inaugural NZ Universities Critic and Conscience award, an Ecology in Action award from the NZ Ecological Society, the Charles Fleming Award for environmental achievement, and the Callaghan Medal for science communication from the Royal Society of New Zealand.

Anne Campbell (they/she) on GenAI's impacts on education, learning and the psychological wellbeing of children and users:
Anne is a writer and local activist in Te Whanganui A Tara who has recently started working in primary education. Many of the tamariki they work with have independently expressed a wide range of concerns about AI, increasing her interest in how digital technologies affect learning and emotional development.

Valerie Morse (she/her) on AI, militarism and surveillance:
Valerie is a peace activist, gardener and writer working to oppose the expansion of military spending, the use of AI in the military and deployment of lethal autonomous systems.

TEQ Talks Wellington | Thursday 29 October 2026 | From 6:00pm

Victoria University of Wellington – Te Aro Campus, LT1
139 Vivian Street, Wellington

TEQ Talks is back in Wellington with another evening of short, sharp talks from fascinating people about the things they’re most passionate about, across VFX, art, science, culture, and beyond.

This edition brings together four very different perspectives — from delivering feature-grade VFX from a boutique Wellington studio, to sculpting dragons, creative technology and the arrival of MDMA-assisted therapy in Aotearoa New Zealand.

Four speakers. Four different perspectives. One evening of ideas, creativity and conversation.

Join us from 6:00pm for drinks, nibbles and networking, with talks kicking off at 7:00pm.

Speakers

Scott Chambers | Founder & Senior VFX Supervisor, 808 Ltd

Punching Above Our Weight: VFX from a Boutique NZ Floor

How a small Wellington studio ships feature-grade visual effects without a Hollywood machine behind it and what that means for craft, crew and clients.

Scott Chambers is Founder and Senior VFX Supervisor at 808 Ltd, a Wellington boutique studio delivering feature and episodic VFX.

Kim Beaton | Sculptor

Making the World, One Dragon at a Time

The story behind the creation of a universal sculpting material, Pal Tiya Premium.

Kim Beaton is a veteran sculptor of 30 years and a passionate advocate of magic realism in sculpture.

Dr G | Psychiatrist

MDMA-Assisted Therapy Has Arrived in Aotearoa New Zealand! Or: Can Psychedelics Change the World?

MDMA-assisted therapy has been approved in New Zealand for two psychiatrists. What is MDMA-assisted therapy, and what could its arrival mean for Aotearoa New Zealand?

Dr G is a consultant psychiatrist, professor of psychiatry and neuroscience, author and researcher with a passion for psychedelic therapies. He is one of the first two doctors in New Zealand approved to prescribe MDMA.

Delainy Jamahl | Creative Director, Artificial Imagination & Co-Founder, The Grid

Solving Problems with Creative Technology

Delainy works at the intersection of art and technology, leveraging technology to create art that moves while developing new techniques and tools to solve problems throughout the creative process.

Event Details

6:00pm – Drinks, nibbles and networking
7:00pm – TEQ Talks begin
9:00pm – Talks wrap
From around 9:30pm – Continue the conversation at Havana till late

Drinks and nibbles will be provided at Vic Uni.

Tickets

FREE – VES members
FREE – VFXG members
FREE – Victoria University of Wellington students
$10 – Students (non-members)
$20 – Professionals (non-members)

Spaces are limited and TEQ Talks does sell out, so grab your ticket early.

TEQ Talks Wellington is presented in partnership with the Visual Effects Society New Zealand Chapter, VFX Professionals Guild and Victoria University of Wellington.

Overview

Discover how your nervous system shapes your habits and learn practical tools to create lasting change and thrive.

Wired to thrive: regulate & rise




Events now start at 6pm. Please try to arrive by 5:45pm so we can get everyone into the event and start on time at 6pm.




How might we shift from who we are to who we want to be?

Join this 75-minute practical introductory workshop to get under the hood of what’s really running the show: your nervous system and your neuromodulators.

You’ll learn about serotonin and dopamine, what they do, why they matter, and how understanding them can help you make more supportive choices and shape the life you want.

You’ll explore practical, body-based tools drawn from somatic wisdom, neuroscience and polyvagal theory, with a focus on turning knowledge into habits you can actually use.

Walk away with 5 practical tools you can start using immediately, because theory alone isn’t enough.

And because the real value comes from putting knowledge into practice, you’ll also receive access to a special online community for the month of November, where you’ll take part in the Wired to Thrive 21-Day Challenge.

You’ll receive:

A simple 1-page habit tracker
Daily prompts to help you put the tools into practice
Q&A and ongoing support throughout the challenge
A community of like-minded people
Accountability and encouragement along the way
A reflection and celebration call at the end

Set yourself up for a thriving summer season.




Event followed by a plant-based dinner and dessert, all included in your ticket!
Meet your host, Freda:

I’m a mum, yoga teacher, retreat host, somatic therapy student, ocean swimmer, connector, curator and founder of Goodlife Collective.

Growing up surrounded by the mountains and ocean in Nelson, I’ve always been drawn to nature, connection and wellbeing. I discovered yoga at 18 in a 400-year-old church in Belgium, where, despite not understanding the French, I experienced a profound sense of calm and presence.

My travels, Psychology studies and own journey into health and healing shaped my passion for inner development, holistic wellbeing and creating spaces for meaningful connection. I completed my 200YTT with Nico Luce in 2019 and founded Goodlife Collective to help unlock our collective potential through connection, possibility and hope.

events.name: Mudhoney
events.venue: Meow Nui, 92 Vivian Street, Te Aro, Wellington, 6011, Wellington
events.long_description:
For the first time in over a decade, Mudhoney return to New Zealand for a run of intimate shows. Renowned for their ferocious live performances, the band continue to deliver the same high-voltage mix of sludgy riffs, pounding rhythms and Mark Arm's unmistakable snarl that made them one of the most influential rock bands of their era.

Formed in Seattle in 1988, Mudhoney helped define the sound that would become known as grunge, combining garage rock, punk and heavy distortion into something raw, loud and entirely their own. As one of the cornerstone acts of legendary independent label Sub Pop, the band became a crucial influence on the explosion of alternative rock that followed, with tracks like 'Touch Me I'm Sick' and 'Suck You Dry' remaining enduring underground classics.

More than 35 years on, Mudhoney remain as vital as ever, continuing to release acclaimed new music and proving night after night why they are regarded as one of the greatest live rock bands of their generation.

"When it comes to grunge, or even just Seattle, I think there was one band that made the definitive music of the time. It wasn't us or Nirvana, but Mudhoney. Nirvana delivered it to the world, but Mudhoney were the band of that time and sound." – Eddie Vedder (Pearl Jam)

A rare chance to experience genuine grunge royalty up close.
