events.long_description:
Power Up the Hutt – Central Lower Hutt

A more comfortable home. Lower energy bills. Greater peace of mind.

If you've been wondering whether electrification could make a real difference to your home and your household budget, this free community event is the perfect place to start.

Join us at Hutt Bowling Club, 6 bMyrtle Street on Thursday 29 October at 7:30 pm for an informative and welcoming evening where local people share how they've transformed the way they live.

From warmer homes in winter and lower running costs to cleaner indoor air and greater energy independence, electrification is helping Hutt Valley households enjoy a better quality of life while reducing their environmental impact.

You'll hear firsthand experiences from local residents who have installed heat pumps, solar panels, home batteries, electric hot water systems, induction cooktops and electric vehicles. They'll explain what motivated them, what the process was like, what they would do differently, and the benefits they're now enjoying every day.

Whether you're just beginning to explore your options or you're ready to take the next step, you'll leave with practical ideas, greater confidence, and a clearer understanding of where to begin.

This is a community event—not a sales presentation. There are no technical lectures or pressure to buy anything. Just honest conversations, practical advice, and the opportunity to ask questions in a relaxed and friendly setting.

Businesses, schools and community organisations interested in electrification are also welcome.

Free admission. Everyone welcome.

Come along and discover how simple changes today can create a home that's more comfortable, more affordable to run, and better prepared for the future.

events.long_description:
Power Up Central Hutt
Come to the first of the new 2026 Power Up The Hutt information sessions in the Hutt Bowling Club, Myrtle Street on the evening of Thursday 29th October at 7:30pm.

Power Up the Hutt is a free five-part community event series bringing together Hutt Valley residents who want to cut their power bills, reduce their carbon footprint, and future-proof their homes.

New Zealand has reached an electrification tipping point — households can now save money and significantly reduce their emissions by switching their appliances and vehicles to electric. But knowing where to start can feel overwhelming.

These friendly, practical evenings — hosted by local volunteers with experience in electrification and drawing on the research of Rewiring Aotearoa — will walk you through the real options available right now: solar panels and home batteries, electric vehicles, heat pump hot water systems, induction cooking, and making the switch from gas to electricity.

Businesses, schools, or community organisations interested in electrification are also welcome. No jargon. No sales pitch. Just straight talk from your neighbours about what works, what it costs, and how to get started.

events.long_description:
To celebrate the summer, we return to a much-loved Royal New Zealand Ballet production from 2011: Greg Horsman’s fairytale version of The Sleeping Beauty.
The age-old story of the princess who pricks her finger and falls into an enchanted sleep, only to be wakened by true love, is brought to life in picture-perfect designs by Gary Harris, classical choreography and Tchaikovsky’s magical music. A touch of wizardry from Wellington’s Wētā Workshop adds to the joy and wonder, making this the perfect pre-Christmas treat for audiences of all ages.

More than 42,000 people saw the premiere of this glorious production around New Zealand in 2011. Choreographer Greg Horsman left the Royal New Zealand Ballet in 2012 to take up a new role at Queensland Ballet, and this production has now been staged there several times to great acclaim.

Book more than one show from our 2026 season through our ‘Subscribe and Save’ package, and save up to 20% on your tickets

events.name: The Fright Crawl | Wellington Halloween Bar Crawl 2026 | Thursday, October 29
events.venue:
The Welsh Dragon Bar
Wellington
events.long_description:
Overview

Kickoff night of Wellington's Halloween weekend. One wristband, 4+ bars, a host, a live map and no cover. Thu, Oct 29. 18+

🎃🕸️ WELLINGTON HALLOWEEN FRIGHT CRAWL 2026 🕸️🎃

One wristband. 4+ of Wellington's best bars. No cover at any of them. The Fright Crawl kicks off Halloween weekend in Wellington on Thursday, October 29th, 2026: a host who runs the night, a live crawl map that always knows where the party is, and up to 800 people in costume moving through the city together. Thursday is the warm-up, the easiest crawl to get into, and the one your Friday self will thank you for.

📍 Crawl Stops: The Welsh Dragon Bar, Panhead Tory Street, The Rogue & Vagabond and El Horno.

🕙 Kickoff: Doors open at 7:30 PM. Wristbands must be picked up by 10:00 PM. The crawl runs until 2:00 AM.

🎶 Music: Live DJs spinning the biggest hits and Halloween classics all night.

🗺️ Live Crawl Map: frightcrawl.com/map/fright-crawl/wellington. Every stop, every time, updated live on the night.

🎟 Tickets: Prices climb as tiers sell, and the launch tier is capped at a handful of tickets that always go first, so grab yours early. Doing more than one night? The Weekend Pass in the ticket menu covers all four Wellington crawls for less than buying them separately.

Throw on your wildest costume and crawl the city with a crowd that is all in costume. Creepy, cute, or covered in fake blood, this is the crawl to be a part of this Halloween weekend. 🧟‍♀️

⭐ Over 10,000 crawlers joined The Fright Crawl last Halloween.

💬 "There were 9 of us and somehow everyone enjoyed it which is honestly rare for our group 💀" Olivia N., 2025 crawler

💬 "My friends and I did this because nobody wanted to be responsible for planning where to go lol. Made the night way easier and every stop had a pretty good crowd." Samantha L., 2025 crawler

🚨 This event is limited to 800 attendees, so grab your tickets early before they sell out! Kickoff night is where the weekend starts, and the crews doing all three nights lock this one in first. Secure your spot before it's too late.

👉 See last year's photos, the full lineup and more reviews at frightcrawl.com/wellington

How It Works

1. Grab your ticket here. The early tiers go first.

2. On the night, show your QR code at the wristband venue between 7:30 PM and 10:00 PM and get your wristband.

3. Follow your host from bar to bar, with the live crawl map showing every stop. No cover anywhere.

4. Everyone ends up at the final venue for one big party.




What's Included in Your Ticket:
🎟️ One wristband, 4+ bars. No cover at any participating venue.
🎤 An on-site Fright Crawl host. Checks you in, hands you your wristband and leads the group to every venue.
🗺️ The interactive crawl map. Every stop, address and time on your phone, with live updates as the night moves.
🟢 Live venue status. See where the crowd is right now and which stop is peaking.
💬 Live online support all night. Ask FrightCrawl on the map, from doors to the last venue, and a real person from the crew when you need one.
📲 Crawl texts. Opt in on the map and you are always in the loop when the group moves.
🏆 Costume contest, judged on the night.
🍹 Drink specials at participating venues.
🎵 Live DJs spinning Halloween hits and party anthems.
🎃 Up to 800 crawlers in the craziest costumes you will see all year. Come with a group or come alone, you will not be alone for long.
🛂 Your Digital Halloween Passport. Stamp every stop as you hit it, straight from the map.
🌿 The Wishing Willow. One wish, made before the crawl. It comes with every ticket, and so does the link.
🎬 Your personalised Crawl Wrapped. When the night ends, the map builds your recap card from your passport, ready to post.
🎧 The official Fright Crawl Halloween playlist. Fifty tracks to get ready to, yours with the ticket.
📱 Your own "you're in" page after you book: your crawl card to post, your nights, and a link to bring your people.
🕺 A massive final party at the last venue, everyone together.

👻 Costume up and crawl your way through Wellington's hottest bars. Expect eerie drink specials, electric energy, and a Halloween you won't forget!

CANCELLATION REFUND GUARANTEE

👌 If a crawl is canceled and not rescheduled, every ticket is refunded automatically. No vouchers, no credits.

🔁 Plans might change? Add the Flexible Ticket at checkout and you can cancel for any reason up to the cutoff shown on this listing.




WRISTBAND PICKUP INSTRUCTIONS & POLICY

Where and When to Pick Up Wristbands

WRISTBAND VENUE:

The Welsh Dragon Bar

🕒 7:30PM-10:30PM

📍 10a Cambridge Terrace, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand

Details: Please arrive at our first stop to scan your ticket and collect your wristband. You have from 7:30 PM to 10:00 PM to arrive and pick up your wristband for the night. Your host leads the group on from this venue at 10:00PM.

MIDDLE STOPS:

Panhead Tory Street

🕒 8:30PM-11:30PM

📍 1 Tory Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand

Details: This is a middle stop. Your host leads the group here between 8:30 PM and 11:30 PM. The live crawl map shows every stop and its time window.

The Rogue & Vagabond

🕒 8:30 PM – 11:30 PM

📍 18 Garrett Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011

Details: This is a middle stop. Your host leads the group here between 8:30 PM and 11:30 PM. The live crawl map shows every stop and its time window.

FINAL VENUE:

El Horno

🕒 11:30 PM – 2:00 AM

📍 34 Courtenay Place, Te Aro, Wellington 6011

Details: This is the final stop! Everyone should meet at this final venue at 11:30PM for a massive final Halloween party!




Wristband Policy

This is a hosted crawl with an open format. You must start at the first venue to collect your wristband. Once you have it, you can follow your host, or visit any participating venue labeled as a "Middle Stop" at your convenience between 8:30 PM and 11:30 PM, or stay at the wristband venue until 10:00 PM. After 11:30 PM everyone meets at the final venue for the final party.

Please remember that you need to collect your wristband at the first stop (wristband venue), as it is required for entry into all venues except the first one. Wristbands are no longer available after 10:00 PM at the first venue. No refunds will be given if you show up late and miss the wristband pick-up window!

This is a walking bar crawl. All venues are within walking distance of each other. Please plan accordingly for transportation and your walking schedule.

Wristbands for entry will be provided by event staff only. To pick up your wristband, please check in with the event staff at the front reception or host stand.

events.long_description:
Overview

AELERT Regulatory Masterclass on Regulatory Integrity, Ethics and Professionalism ft. Keith Manch and Dr Marie Doole.

Two of NZ's top regulatory leaders lead a discussion-based masterclass on integrity, ethics and professionalism in Wellington.

AELERT Regulatory Masterclass on Regulatory Integrity, Ethics and Professionalism ft. Keith Manch and Dr Marie Doole

October 30 | Te Iho (Bowen House)

Integrity is the foundation of regulatory legitimacy. When it holds, regulators make defensible decisions, resist undue influence and retain public trust. When it slips, the damage is slow, quiet and hard to reverse.

Across Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand, regulators are being asked to uphold that standard in a harder environment: reform is reshaping mandates, resourcing is stretched, and pressure arrives from regulated parties and from within the authorising environment alike. This masterclass brings together two of Aotearoa's most respected regulatory leaders, Keith Manch and Dr Marie Doole, in central Wellington to work through what integrity, ethics and professionalism require in practice, and how agencies can strengthen them deliberately rather than assume they will hold.

What's included

Full day masterclass (9:00am to 3:30pm) with Keith Manch and Dr Marie Doole
Discussion-based sessions covering the fundamentals of good regulatory practice, integrity in the authorising environment, integrity in agency operations, and the mechanics of regulatory capture
Refreshments during the break and coffee on arrival where available
Certificate of attendance for CPD and capability records
Complimentary post-masterclass social event from 4-7.30pm including canapes and social drinks at the Thistle Inn (please RSVP by October 21 to adam.slater@sa.gov.au)

Who should attend

Regulatory staff at every level: frontline practitioners in compliance, enforcement, investigations, monitoring and assessment; managers and team leaders responsible for regulatory decisions and relationships; senior leaders and executives accountable for regulatory strategy, culture and capability; integrity, ethics, assurance and governance professionals; policy and legislative professionals; legal advisers to regulators; and academics, researchers and students working on regulatory practice and integrity. Mixed cohorts are encouraged, since integrity risks are tested daily across an agency, not only in senior roles.

Location

This Wellington masterclass is hosted by the Ministry for Regulation at Te Iho (Bowen House).

Rooms 20.01/02.

Pricing

$500 AUD inclusive of GST and booking fees.

Please review the AELERT event registration terms and conditions.

Event sponsors

The Regulatory Masterclass on AI and Emerging Technologies is proudly brought to you by AELERT and our exclusive technology sponsor Objective Corporation.




For full details about this masterclass please visit the AELERT website.

events.id: What is Gouache?-Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: What is Gouache?
events.venue: Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington
events.long_description:
Come explore the versatile and expressive world of gouache in this hands-on, experimental workshop. Designed for both beginners and those looking to loosen up their painting practice, this session is an opportunity to play, experiment and discover what gouache can do.

We’ll begin with a brief introduction to the origins and history of gouache, looking at how the medium has been used across different periods and by a range of well-known artists. We’ll explore examples of gouache in practice, drawing inspiration from the distinctive ways artists have used its bold colour, opacity and versatility.

From there, we’ll get stuck into the medium through a series of playful exercises and experiments. You’ll learn the fundamentals of working with gouache — from mixing colours and exploring opacity to layering, mark-making and creating different textures — while being encouraged to develop your own approach.

Rather than focusing on creating a perfect finished painting, this workshop is about curiosity, experimentation and enjoying the process of discovering what gouache can do.

All materials included.

Thirty minute lunch break - bring a packed lunch to enjoy in our historic house or explore the local Te Aro cafes. Coffee and tea provided at lunch.

events.venue: The Screening Room, 435 Queen St, Masterton
events.long_description:
OFFICIALSELECTION: Sundance Film Festival -
OFFICIAL SELECTION: Glasgow Film Festival -

From Executive Producer Emma Thompson and BAFTA-winning director Felipe Bustos Sierra comes Everybody to Kenmure Street, a multifaceted picture of one of the most memorable moments in Glasgow’s recent history.

On May 13, 2021, UK Home Office immigration enforcement launched a dawn raid in Pollokshields, one of Scotland’s most diverse neighbourhoods. Local residents rushed to the streets to stop the deportation of their neighbours. As word spread, a handful of protestors quickly grew to a crowd of hundreds, flooding Kenmure Street and completely blocking an immigration enforcement van.

The eight-hour stand-off made international headlines as the community organised itself in an extraordinary act of peaceful solidarity.

Everybody to Kenmure Street uses a combination of crowd-sourced footage from the day, archive film and dramatic re-enactments to examine the power of grassroots collective action, solidarity, and empathy in confronting state authority.

events.venue: The Screening Room, 435 Queen St, Masterton
events.long_description:
OFFICIAL SELECTION: Thessaloniki International Documentary Festival -

What happens when your neighbour goes completely wild? Derek vs Derek is a funny, insightful and heartwarming documentary that charts the turbulent relationship between two farmers.

On a country road in Devon live two ideologically opposed neighbouring farmers- both called Derek. Derek Banbury believes in the intensive farming of his land, while Derek Gow is focused on creating a “rewilding” oasis for nature and wildlife on his land.

Shot over three years, Derek vs Derek wonderfully juxtaposes the two wholly opposing approaches to farming, as tempers fray, wild animals run amok, and the land is radically transformed.

The two Dereks’ story will at turns amuse, entertain and provoke thought about environmental issues and the future of farming.

Award-winning director James Dawson celebrates the potential for understanding in this wonderful film about land use and farming, told by farmers. Packed to the brim with English humour, Derek vs Derek is essential viewing.

Overview

Re-use, Re-Purpose, Beautify with Gold!! Come along and learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Sip & Kintsugi.

Come and experience this unique Sip & Kintsugi workshop at the lovely Bond Store Distillery. You will get a gin tasting tray on arrival with three different gins with tonic. And why not come a little earlier and grab a bite to eat beforehand. (Must be 18+ yrs of age)

Learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Workshop. You can bring along a piece of your own pottery to restore in this beautiful style. (I'll also have a few as back up if you don't have your own piece) (All Levels)


Friday 30th October - 5:30pm - 7:30pm

Kintsugi

It's called kintsugi (金継ぎ), or kintsukuroi (金繕い), literally golden (“kin”) and repair (“tsugi”). This traditional Japanese art uses a precious metal – liquid gold, liquid silver or lacquer dusted with powdered gold – to bring together the pieces of a broken pottery item and at the same time enhance the breaks.

You will take away your wonderful finished work, plus your knew skills which will enable you to further your own Kintsugi in your own time.

This class is not just for budding or accomplished artists. It is for everyone to enjoy a relaxing day of art and design with Ema.

What you will take away:

A finished artwork piece

A understanding of Kintsugi

Knowledge and History of this beautiful art form.

BELTANE SONG & SOUND CEREMONY
Beltane Sound & Voice Ceremony

Sing, Sound and Meditate — Friday 30 October, Paraparaumu

Beltane, the ancient Celtic festival marking the start of summer, is a threshold of fertility, creation and abundance. The earth is bursting into life, and so are we.

You are warmly invited to gather with me in a ceremonial circle to celebrate this turning of the wheel. Together we'll tune into the sacred energies and possibilities of this time, opening ourselves to balance, nourishment, new growth and positive change.

Part one: Voice and Spirit

We begin by calling in the supportive presence of Spirit, the ancestors, the forces of Nature and our highest Selves. The land and the unseen realms have always been at the heart of my practice, and they will hold us throughout.

From there I'll guide you through meditation, gentle Qigong, and conscious sounding and toning to balance and align your energy system. We'll sing beautiful healing chants from many traditions, and play with guided vocal improvisation for freedom, upliftment and joy.

There's something quietly powerful about co-creating a sacred group sound. It lifts us, supports us in releasing what we no longer need, and makes space for new visions to take root. We'll honour that with journaling prompts inspired by Beltane and a moment of intention setting for the season ahead.

Part two: Sound Healing

The second half is a dedicated sound bath. You'll lie back and simply receive, letting the sound carry you into deep relaxation, stillness and peace, with the gratitude that often arrives in that stillness.

Conscious voice work and sound healing can support us physically, mentally, emotionally, energetically and spiritually, and a growing body of research backs up what so many of us feel. I'm happy to share more about these benefits if you'd like to read further.

All are welcome

You might not think you can sing and sound. Come and find out. No experience or preparation is needed, just your willingness to gather.

Details

Friday 30 October · 6.30pm-9pm, Paraparaumu Memorial Hall, Corner of Aorangi / Tutanekai Streets
2.5 hours · Limited spaces

🎶 This Dance Floor we have a Halloween special, where you are free to dress up in your fav halloween costume while still feeling cozy to dance your bum off! We will have some halloween treats and what a treat it is to have Lili DJ for us from Dunedin.

Lili Eve | Ecstatic Dance Dunedin

Lili Eve weaves sound into immersive sonic journeys, layering rhythms, textures and melodies to move dancers through a spectrum of moods, energies and emotions.

Creating each set with intention, she draws on a broad musical palette, moving between earthy grooves, melodic soundscapes, ethereal textures and deep, bass-driven beats. Her sets unfold like a wave, building, shifting and flowing to invite dancers to explore, express and surrender to the music.

For Lili, the dancefloor is a space of possibility, connection and discovery, where music becomes an invitation to let go, feel deeply and come home to yourself.

A freeform, drug- and alcohol-free dance experience where you move however your body wants. The music flows like a wave — starting slow, rising to ecstatic peaks, then softening into stillness. It’s therapeutic, uplifting, and a powerful way to connect with yourself and community.

Please note, that this Ecstatic Dance is not verbally guided, we let the music guide you 😊. Dance freely how your body moves you.

🎶 The Sound System

Here at Ecstatic Dance Wellington, we believe in using a phat sound system with lots of bass for our dances. We will be bringing an ultra vibey and super bassy experience for you!

We are very much looking forward to co-creating with the conscious dance community in Wellington and sharing our magic.

❤️ What to Bring

Water bottle

A friend!

Drug & alcohol free event

Silence on the dance floor

events.long_description:
INDUNA - FAVOURITE COLOURS (RELEASE SHOW)
Following recent performances supporting internationally acclaimed Nigerian artist Seun Kuti & Egypt 80, Aotearoa-based South African artist InDuna is set to release his new single 'Favourite Colours' and celebrates with a special headline show at Moon, Newtown, Wellington on Friday 30th October 2026.

Blending Afro-pop, R&B and folk, InDuna's live show brings infectious rhythms and uplifting energy alongside the more personal stories behind the songs. 'Favourite Colours' is an atmospheric anthem about identity, healing and resilience, using colour as a metaphor for how anxiety, grief and disconnection can drain the vibrancy from life, and the journey back to yourself.

﻿
InDuna will be joined by a special guest support act, to be announced.


Wheelchair accessible, seated and standing available.


About InDuna

Artist and producer InDuna draws on his South African roots, raised between Johannesburg and Limpopo before moving to Aotearoa at fourteen. His sound fuses African rhythm with contemporary pop and electronic production. Highlights include the King's Trust Young Global Achiever Award (2024), his single 'Dreams' (Best Original Song, International Online Web Fest; Official NZ Hot Singles Chart; featured in 'Ink and Gold'), and his 2025 EP 'Go High' (#16, Official Top 20 Aotearoa Albums Chart). He's supported Seun Kuti & Egypt 80 and opened for JessB, Estère and Deva Mahal, with headline shows across Wellington and Auckland.

'Favourite Colours' is supported by New Zealand On Air.

events.long_description:
Hailing from the music-filled streets of Melbourne, Australia, Shaun Kirk is an award-winning blues and soul troubadour recognised for his exceptional talent as a born entertainer. His unique talent has not only earned him many accolades but also much praise from fellow artists, such as three-time Grammy Award Winner Fantastic Negrito, who has declared his show as "One of the best one-man shows he’s ever seen!"

Kirk's vocals exude a gritty, soulful depth that seems to transcend far beyond his years, with critics continually acclaiming him as "one of the finest blues voices Australia has ever heard" (Buzz Mag). Complementing his vocal artistry, Kirk's vintage guitar tones and raw grooves pay tribute to the timeless influences that have shaped his musical journey, resulting in a distinctive sound fast becoming his own.

Shaun’s musical journey has taken him to stages all over the world, where he's not only performed but consistently sold out shows, leaving audiences enthralled by his magnetic presence. From iconic festival stages like Bluesfest Byron Bay, where he's become a familiar name, to sharing the billing with legends like Robert Plant of Led Zeppelin, John Mayer, Paolo Nutini, John Butler Trio, and The Teskey Brothers; Kirk's artistic prowess is in esteemed company. Moreover, he's also had the honour of opening for household names such as blues maestro Joe Bonamassa, soul sensation Allen Stone, and the indomitable Beth Hart; further solidifying his place in the landscape of contemporary music. This remarkable journey is a testament to Kirk's unmatched talent and ability to connect with audiences across genres and generations.

WHAT THE PRESS IS SAYING ABOUT SHAUN KIRK

“It’s rare to see someone bring down the house as an opener, but Australia’s Shaun Kirk did exactly that. He connected with the crowd immediately” – Soundcheck Entertainment, Canada

“One of the most explosive acts Australia has to offer” – Mixdown Magazine, Australia

"My faith in this generation’s music has been restored.” - Dearhead Press

“Simply astounding." - Forte Magazine, Australia

Special guest: Joe Cole

events.name: WOW: Meet the Makers
events.venue: Te Raukura ki Kāpiti,32 Raumati Rd, Raumati Beach, Paraparaumu 5032, New Zealand, Paraparaumu
events.long_description:
WOW: Meet the Makers
Step inside the World of WearableArt® and hear from the people at the heart of the spectacle.

WOW: Meet the Makers is an inspiring evening of stories, creativity and insight, featuring some of the region's most accomplished WOW designers. Hear from 2026 Supreme WOW Award winner Kayla Christensen as she shares her journey to the top of the world's premier wearable art competition, alongside fellow Kāpiti designer Rebecca Bond, whose imaginative work has earned recognition on the WOW stage. Guests will also enjoy reflections from legendary WOW designer Fifi Colston, a 30-time entrant and multi-award winner whose extraordinary body of work has helped shape the competition's history.

Hosted by Sarah Nathan, Head of Competition for WOW, the evening offers a rare behind-the-scenes look at how a WOW entry evolves from an initial spark of inspiration to a world-class performance. Through designer conversations, creative storytelling and insights into the competition process, guests will discover what it takes to create work that captivates audiences and judges alike.

Whether you're a long-time WOW fan, an aspiring creative, or simply curious about the people behind the spectacle, this exclusive event offers a rare opportunity to connect with the makers, stories and artistry at the heart of WOW.


WOW: Meet the Makers is presented by Visit Kāpiti.

Your panel:
Sarah Nathan
Head of Competition
Gain a unique behind-the-scenes perspective on the WOW Competition as Sarah shares insights into artistic excellence, creative innovation, and what it takes for designers to stand out on the world stage.

Kayla Christiansen
Local Artist and WOW Supreme Award Winner 2026
Kayla Christiansen is a local artist with a passion for all things creative, from fine arts to wearable arts and everything in between. Join Kayla to hear about the journey to becoming a WOW Supreme Award winner and where here imagination is taking her for her next creative journey.

Fifi Colston
WOW Finalist Designer
Discover how storytelling, costume, and craftspersonship come together in wearable art as Fifi shares creative insights from three decades at WOW, revealing the imagination and process behind award-winning designs.

Rebecca Bond
Multidisciplinary Artist and WOW Designer
Kāpiti Coast based artist Rebecca Bond works across contemporary jewellery, silversmithing, wearable art, performance drawing and community arts. Hear Rebecca share insights from her creative journey inspired by people and nature and how her practice explores identity and connection.

Through designer conversations, creative storytelling and insights into the competition process, guests will discover what it takes to create work that captivates audiences and judges alike.

Whether you're a long-time WOW fan, an aspiring creative, or simply curious about the people behind the spectacle, this exclusive event offers a rare opportunity to connect with the makers, stories and artistry at the heart of WOW.

WOW: Meet the Makers is presented by Visit Kāpiti.

Early Bird ticket: Limited to 50! Get yours before they fly away.

A HALLOWEEN NIGHT OF HORROR, LOCAL FILMMAKING AND 1990s NOSTALGIA
Get ready for a special Halloween celebration at Regent 3 Cinemas, Masterton, marking the 30th anniversary of Wes Craven's SCREAM (1996).

But there's more this Halloween...
WORLD PREMIERE: THE BOXER (2026)
A NEW WAIRARAPA HORROR SHORT
We are thrilled to premiere a brand-new horror short from local filmmaker Mark Pacey. Filmed right here in the Wairarapa, the film features a Wairarapa cast and crew. This special Halloween screening gives audiences the opportunity to see a new piece of local filmmaking on the big screen, alongside one of the most influential horror films of the 1990s. Film details coming soon.

SCREAM (1996) | 30TH ANNIVERSARY
Dir. Wes Craven | USA | 1h 51m | Horror, Mystery, Thriller
Get ready to answer the phone…

Celebrate 30 years of SCREAM (1996), the iconic horror film that reinvented the slasher genre for a new generation. When a masked killer known as Ghostface begins terrorising the small town of Woodsboro, teenager Sidney Prescott and her friends find themselves caught in a deadly game where the rules of horror are anything but predictable.

Starring Neve Campbell, Courteney Cox, David Arquette and Drew Barrymore, Wes Craven's clever, funny and genuinely frightening classic blends suspense, scares and self-aware humour into one of the defining horror films of the 1990s. Experience SCREAM the way it was meant to be seen: on the big screen, with an audience, and with the phone ringing somewhere in the darkness.

YOUR PRE-HALLOWEEN NIGHT
Your $15 ticket includes:
The premiere of new Wairarapa horror short THE BOXER (2026) + SCREAM (1996) on the big screen

events.long_description:
Overview

Wellington's Friday Halloween takeover. One wristband, 4+ bars, no cover, a host and a live crawl map. Fri, Oct 30. 18+

🎃🕸️ WELLINGTON HALLOWEEN FRIGHT CRAWL 2026 🕸️🎃

One wristband. 4+ of Wellington's best bars. No cover at any of them. The Fright Crawl takes over Wellington on Friday, October 30th, 2026: a host who runs the night, a live crawl map that always knows where the party is, and up to 800 people in costume moving through the city together. Friday is the big takeover, the night the whole city comes out, and the one that fills right behind Halloween night.

📍 Crawl Stops: Sassy Loves Cash, The Rogue & Vagabond, Panhead Tory Street and Cavern Club.

🕙 Kickoff: Doors open at 7:30 PM. Wristbands must be picked up by 10:00 PM. The crawl runs until 2:00 AM.

🎶 Music: Live DJs spinning the biggest hits and Halloween classics all night.

🗺️ Live Crawl Map: frightcrawl.com/map/fright-crawl/wellington. Every stop, every time, updated live on the night.

🎟 Tickets: Prices climb as tiers sell, and the launch tier is capped at a handful of tickets that always go first, so grab yours early. Doing more than one night? The Weekend Pass in the ticket menu covers all four Wellington crawls for less than buying them separately.

Throw on your wildest costume and crawl the city with a crowd that is all in costume. Creepy, cute, or covered in fake blood, this is the crawl to be a part of this Halloween weekend. 🧟‍♀️

⭐ Over 10,000 crawlers joined The Fright Crawl last Halloween.

💬 "Good mix of places. Started off just drinking and talking and by the last couple stops everyone was dancing 💀 Pretty much exactly what we wanted." Kevin D., 2025 crawler

💬 "We bought tickets mostly because our friends were doing it and ended up having such a good night. Would go again next Halloween ❤️" Brianna F., 2025 crawler

🚨 This event is limited to 800 attendees, so grab your tickets early before they sell out! Friday fills right behind Halloween night, and it does not wait for the last minute. Secure your spot before it's too late.

👉 See last year's photos, the full lineup and more reviews at frightcrawl.com/wellington

How It Works

1. Grab your ticket here. The early tiers go first.

2. On the night, show your QR code at the wristband venue between 7:30 PM and 10:00 PM and get your wristband.

3. Follow your host from bar to bar, with the live crawl map showing every stop. No cover anywhere.

4. Everyone ends up at the final venue for one big party.




What's Included in Your Ticket:
🎟️ One wristband, 4+ bars. No cover at any participating venue.
🎤 An on-site Fright Crawl host. Checks you in, hands you your wristband and leads the group to every venue.
🗺️ The interactive crawl map. Every stop, address and time on your phone, with live updates as the night moves.
🟢 Live venue status. See where the crowd is right now and which stop is peaking.
💬 Live online support all night. Ask FrightCrawl on the map, from doors to the last venue, and a real person from the crew when you need one.
📲 Crawl texts. Opt in on the map and you are always in the loop when the group moves.
🏆 Costume contest, judged on the night.
🍹 Drink specials at participating venues.
🎵 Live DJs spinning Halloween hits and party anthems.
🎃 Up to 800 crawlers in the craziest costumes you will see all year. Come with a group or come alone, you will not be alone for long.
🛂 Your Digital Halloween Passport. Stamp every stop as you hit it, straight from the map.
🌿 The Wishing Willow. One wish, made before the crawl. It comes with every ticket, and so does the link.
🎬 Your personalised Crawl Wrapped. When the night ends, the map builds your recap card from your passport, ready to post.
🎧 The official Fright Crawl Halloween playlist. Fifty tracks to get ready to, yours with the ticket.
📱 Your own "you're in" page after you book: your crawl card to post, your nights, and a link to bring your people.
🕺 A massive final party at the last venue, everyone together.

👻 Costume up and crawl your way through Wellington's hottest bars. Expect eerie drink specials, electric energy, and a Halloween you won't forget!

CANCELLATION REFUND GUARANTEE

👌 If a crawl is canceled and not rescheduled, every ticket is refunded automatically. No vouchers, no credits.

🔁 Plans might change? Add the Flexible Ticket at checkout and you can cancel for any reason up to the cutoff shown on this listing.




WRISTBAND PICKUP INSTRUCTIONS & POLICY

Where and When to Pick Up Wristbands

WRISTBAND VENUE:

Sassy Loves Cash

🕒 7:30PM-10:30PM

📍 24 Courtenay Place, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand

🍸 Halloween Menu on Site

Details: Please arrive at our first stop to scan your ticket and collect your wristband. You have from 7:30 PM to 10:00 PM to arrive and pick up your wristband for the night. Your host leads the group on from this venue at 10:00PM.

MIDDLE STOPS:

The Rogue & Vagabond

🕒 8:30 PM – 11:30 PM

📍 18 Garrett Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011

Details: This is a middle stop. Your host leads the group here between 8:30 PM and 11:30 PM. The live crawl map shows every stop and its time window.

Panhead Tory Street

🕒 8:30PM-11:30PM

📍 1 Tory Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand

Details: This is a middle stop. Your host leads the group here between 8:30 PM and 11:30 PM. The live crawl map shows every stop and its time window.

FINAL VENUE:

Cavern Club

🕒 11:30 PM – 2:00 AM

📍 22 Allen Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand

🍸 $7 house spirits and house wines

Details: This is the final stop! Everyone should meet at this final venue at 11:30PM for a massive final Halloween party!




Wristband Policy

This is a hosted crawl with an open format. You must start at the first venue to collect your wristband. Once you have it, you can follow your host, or visit any participating venue labeled as a "Middle Stop" at your convenience between 8:30 PM and 11:30 PM, or stay at the wristband venue until 10:00 PM. After 11:30 PM everyone meets at the final venue for the final party.

Please remember that you need to collect your wristband at the first stop (wristband venue), as it is required for entry into all venues except the first one. Wristbands are no longer available after 10:00 PM at the first venue. No refunds will be given if you show up late and miss the wristband pick-up window!

This is a walking bar crawl. All venues are within walking distance of each other. Please plan accordingly for transportation and your walking schedule.

Wristbands for entry will be provided by event staff only. To pick up your wristband, please check in with the event staff at the front reception or host stand.




2026 CRAWL MAP:

View The Crawl Map Here

Bookmark it now. On the night it is your guide: every stop and time, live venue status, your Digital Halloween Passport, crawl texts and live support all live there.

🎟️ General Admission

Everything above: the wristband, the host, the live map, the contest, the passport and the playlist. No frills, just the fun.

───────────────────────────────────────

👑 VIP Ticket

Includes everything in GA, plus a VIP kit emailed to you after you book and the VIP-only experiences unlocked on your page:

🔮 A collectible Fright Crawl tarot card, one per order
🃏 A full tarot reading for your night, VIP only
🪞 The Haunted Mirror, VIP only
🕯️ The Digital Ouija Board, VIP only
🔎 The Halloween scavenger hunt game
🍸 The Spooky Cocktails ebook
🎲 The Halloween Games ebook
🚀 First dibs on future crawl drops and pre-sales

───────────────────────────────────────

🤯 Ultra VIP

For the dangerously curious. Includes everything in VIP, plus what only Ultra gets:

📜 A personalised Certified Crawl Legend certificate in your name
🏆 Your name on the Crawl Wall of Fame on the live Wellington crawl map, for everyone on the crawl to see
❓ A mystery bonus item we legally can't describe 👀

───────────────────────────────────────

👯 Coming as a crew? Look for the Group Discount tiers in the ticket menu (minimum 2 per order). Groups are who this was built for: one plan, one wristband each, nobody stuck organising.

🎫 Doing more than one night? The Weekend Pass in the ticket menu covers all four Wellington crawls, Thursday through Halloween night, for less than buying them separately. Or see the Weekend Pass listing.

WHY THE FRIGHT CRAWL BEATS ONE BAR

One bar means one cover, one room and one vibe for the whole night. The Fright Crawl gives you Wellington's best bars on a single wristband, a host who moves the crowd so nobody has to organise anything, and a finale where every crawler ends up in the same room at the last venue.

THE FRIDAY TAKEOVER

Friday is the night everyone who could not get Saturday off comes out, and the night the Saturday crowd warms up. Wellington's best bars, one wristband, a host moving the crowd, and a final venue where the whole crawl lands together. It fills right behind Halloween night. 🧛‍♀️

WHO THIS IS FOR

Groups who don't want to be the one planning. Visitors who don't know the bars. Birthdays that land on Halloween weekend. Solo crawlers who want a built-in crowd. Anyone whose costume deserves more than one room.

💬 "If you're coming from out of town for Halloween I'd recommend it. We wouldn't have known which places to go to otherwise." Rachel H., 2025 crawler

💬 "First bar crawl I've done and I'd do another one. I liked being able to move around instead of paying cover somewhere and being stuck there all night." Marcus J., 2025 crawler

GET YOUR TICKETS BEFORE THEY VANISH!

Spots are filling fast, so now's the time to lock in your night. Round up your friends, pick your costume, and get ready to sip, dance, and crawl your way through the biggest Friday of the year in Wellington. Halloween only comes once a year. 🎟️

❓ Questions first? Read the FAQ or reach the crew at frightcrawl.com/support.

18+ EVENT / GOVERNMENT ISSUED ID REQUIRED




TIPS FOR OUR CRAWL
Pick Up Wristbands On Time: Collect your wristband during the designated check-in window at the wristband venue, before 10:00 PM. Late arrivals will not be accommodated. No wristband, no entry.
Assign a Proxy if Needed: Can't make check-in? Any friend with your ticket QR code can pick up your wristband for you.
Day-Of Updates: Check the live crawl map on the morning of the event for any last-minute changes or venue updates. It updates live during the night too.
Check Venue Schedule: Each venue's crawl time is listed on the crawl map. Wristbands and drink specials are valid only during these scheduled times.
Costumes: Non-negotiable. Nothing that looks like a weapon, nothing highly offensive, and you are good.
Getting Home: Every stop is walkable from the last, and the final venue is on the map, so book your ride from there.

Age Requirement: You must be 18+ years of age with a valid government-issued ID to participate in this event. No exceptions.
Wristbands: Your wristband is your key to entry. You must present your ticket or QR code at check-in to receive your wristband. Wristbands must be worn at all times to access participating bars and venues. Wristband pickup location and time are listed on the crawl map. If you do not pick up your wristband at the designated location and time, it may not be available, and you will not be able to access crawl venues. No wristband, no entry.

In case of event cancellation without a rescheduled date, a refund (excluding fees) will be automatically issued. Event lineup, venues, and specials are subject to change without notice.

If refused entry at one venue, you may visit alternative crawl venues available at that time. No refunds will be given if you are denied entry for any of these reasons.
Capacity and Late Entry: Some venues may hit capacity during the event. If a venue reaches capacity or you arrive late, you may have to wait in line to gain entry. There is no guarantee of immediate access or entry to any specific venue once capacity is reached, and no refunds will be provided due to waiting times or access issues.
Hosted Crawl: Your crawl host checks you in, hands out wristbands, and leads the group from venue to venue. The live crawl map shows every stop, so you can find the group again if you get separated.
Venue Awareness: If bar staff are unaware of the crawl, message the crew through the live chat on the crawl map or contact the venue representative listed there. If you cannot reach anyone, consider that venue unavailable and proceed to an alternative crawl venue open at that time. Nightlife venues may reach capacity or close early, and not all staff members may be aware of the crawl.
Drink Specials: Drink specials are offered by participating venues and may be modified or discontinued at any time without notice.

Security Checks: Wristbands do not entitle you to skip venue security checks. All attendees must comply with security screening before entry.
Costume Policy: Do not wear costumes that include items which could be considered or used as weapons. Highly offensive costumes are not tolerated and may result in denial of entry without refund.
No Weapons or Costume Weapons: Weapons of any kind are strictly prohibited at every crawl venue, and that includes costume weapons: replica or toy guns, knives, swords, axes, bats, chainsaws and any similar prop. The fact that an item is fake makes no difference. Any attendee found in possession of a weapon or costume weapon will be immediately removed from the crawl without a refund.
Crawl Notifications: Sign up for crawl texts on the crawl map to receive updates about when to move to the next venue. Your host also calls out each move in person.

events.long_description:
LA-based Kiwi singer-songwriter Greg Johnson announces a six-date, career-spanning tour celebrating his 60th birthday.

The tour in October and November will feature fan favourites from Johnson’s rich catalogue, including hits such as Isabelle, Don’t Wait Another Day, Save Yourself, Now The Sun Is Out, and Liberty, alongside songs from his highly anticipated new album, Some Night, Somewhere, to be released in October.

Said Johnson: “We’re performing in some of New Zealand’s nicest performing arts venues, and I can’t wait to see everyone.”

The tour features the full Greg Johnson band and will be a memorable journey through decades of iconic songs, combining beloved classics and fresh new material.

Greg Johnson is a winner of the APRA Silver Scroll, and New Zealand Music Award. Somenight, Somewhere will be his 14th studio album.

events.id: The Nomad 30 Year Anniversary NZ Tour-MEOW, 9 Edward St, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: The Nomad 30 Year Anniversary NZ Tour
events.venue: MEOW, 9 Edward St, Wellington
events.long_description:
ReGenerate – 30 Year Anniversary NZ Tour

After three decades of making music, DJing and pushing Aotearoa’s bass culture forward, The Nomad returns to the road this October, November and early December for his national ReGenerate – 30 Year Anniversary NZ Tour.

Joined by MC Antsman and featuring immersive visuals from warpTV, the tour will bring The Nomad’s signature blend of dub, reggae, house, jungle and drum & bass to dancefloors across Aotearoa, with local support at each stop.

The tour celebrates the release of ReGenerate, a 16-track album marking 30 years of original music from one of New Zealand’s pioneering electronic artists. Beginning with Locust in 1996 and evolving into The Nomad in 1998, his journey has consistently crossed genres while remaining rooted in bass culture, experimentation and the dancefloor.

ReGenerate is more than a retrospective. It’s 30 years of sound, experience, experimentation and connection, regenerated for a new generation. Built through decades of studio production and live performance, the album reflects the sounds, people and communities that have shaped Aotearoa’s electronic music landscape.

The album will receive a deliberately limited physical release, with the complete 16-track record available on double vinyl, CD and cassette. The first pressing features just 300 copies of the double album on metallic red vinyl, making it a genuine collector’s edition. Only a selection of tracks will be released digitally, with the physical editions offering the complete album experience, from the sequencing and artwork through to the full musical journey.

Live, ReGenerate takes that history to the dancefloor. Expect heavy bass, dub, reggae, house, jungle and drum & bass, backed by MC Antsman’s energy and warpTV’s immersive visual production.

This isn’t just a DJ set. It’s 30 years of original music.

events.id: The Opera House: After Dark-The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
events.name: The Opera House: After Dark
events.venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
This Halloween, step inside The Opera House after hours for an R18 guided experience. Explore the theatre's hidden corners, colourful history, and lingering mysteries. Over the course of an hour, you’ll be led through the building by a guide. They’ll share tales from The Opera House’s past. This includes stories, legends, and strange happenings that have endured long after the final curtain call.   

As you move through the darkness, mysterious figures, unexpected encounters, and eerie effects will keep you wondering what — and who — might be waiting around the next corner. Once you’ve made it back into the light, unwind in the foyer with a complimentary drink and nibbles, included with your ticket.   

Blending theatre history, storytelling, and a touch of Halloween mischief, The Opera House After Dark offers a unique way to experience one of Wellington’s most iconic venues.

Accessibility and safety
You need a good level of mobility to go on this tour. You will be walking through foyers, stairways, and spaces. While there are railings and several rests throughout the tour, you will not have the opportunity to sit for a long period during the tour.   
This tour is currently not accessible for wheelchair users. If you are a wheelchair user, or have other accessibility needs, and would like to attend a tour, please contact us at guestexperience@wellingtonnz.com 
Some sections of the tour will enter seating areas that are steep and may not be suitable for patrons who experience vertigo. 
Closed-toe, flat shoes are required for the tour. No heels or open-toe shoes.

events.name: Baking with Yeast - Beginners
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
As a beginner baker it is important to understand yeast and how it interacts with different flours as well the processes involved in baking. In this class, expert baker Veronika, will guide you to learn about the ingredients and practices needed to make beautiful baked goods from around the world. Learn how to read, understand and follow recipes and bake cinnamon rolls, pizza, chocolate babka and much more!

Veronika is passionate about baking and will share her extensive knowledge so you can gain confidence and mastery of this useful skill. Practice a wide range of baking techniques including kneading, shaping, proofing, types of glazing and the baking process itself. Once you’ve mastered baking you will have a new stress relief technique that is creative, practical and produces delicious baked goods for you and your friends and family to enjoy.  

All ingredients provided but bring an apron, tea towels and a dish cloth and containers to take any leftovers home. 

By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:

Read, follow and explore new recipes.
Mastering yeast dough from scratch.
Use baking knowledge to bake different yeast based products.
Use skills in unexpected situations.
Demonstrate increased confidence in the kitchen.
Share your new found skills with your friends and family.

events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki St, Wellington
events.long_description:
Masala is the Indian word for curry. Spend the day making a range of curries both from scratch and by adapting spice packets, for family meals and special occasions. All ingredients provided.

Take a day and create a range of delicious and different Indian masalas, using both Manjula’s tried-and-true recipes but also some of the new spice mixes now available in Indian shops. You’ll also learn how to make a variety of breads (naan, roti and parathas) to serve with the curries.

By the end of the workshop, you’ll be able to:

Create several different masalas (curries)
Make tasty Indian bread accompaniments
Adapt ready-made spice mixes to enhance the flavours
Use a range a different Indian spices with more confidence

All ingredients provided but bring an apron, dishcloth, tea towels and containers to take any leftovers home.

Presented by Manjula Patel.

events.id: Finding Peace in the Digital Age - Meditation Half-Day Course-Tararua Tramping Club Hall, 4 Moncrieff Street, Mount Victoria,Tararua Tramping Club Inc., 4 Moncrieff St, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand, Wellington-All Events In
events.name: Finding Peace in the Digital Age - Meditation Half-Day Course
events.venue: Tararua Tramping Club Hall, 4 Moncrieff Street, Mount Victoria,Tararua Tramping Club Inc., 4 Moncrieff St, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand, Wellington
events.long_description:
Finding Peace in the Digital Age - Meditation Half-Day Course
Is it possible to find genuine peace in this digital age?

We live in a fast-paced world filled with distractions, constant notifications, and endless comparisons. It’s easy to feel overwhelmed, restless, and disconnected from ourselves. But peace doesn’t come from switching off the world—it comes from changing the way we relate to it. Buddha’s timeless wisdom shows us how to stay calm and centred, no matter what is happening around us.

At this half-day course, Buddhist monk and National Spiritual Director, Gen Kelsang Rabten will share practical Buddhist insights and guide simple meditations to help us step back from the busyness of life, quiet the inner noise, and reconnect with clarity, focus, and joy.

Everyone welcome

Cost
Standard: $60*
Course, Study & Great Card holders: $42*
*Plus a $2 Stripe surcharge

Venue & Parking
Paid street parking is available on Moncrieff Street and the surrounding streets. Please allow an extra 10–15 minutes to find a parking space.

To book visit: https://meditateinwellington.org/events/finding-peace-digital-age

events.name: Posture Perfection Is Possible
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki St, Wellington
events.long_description:
Are you a computer slouch, feeling stiff and tense at work? Do you find it difficult to maintain a good posture? Does your posture cause back, neck or shoulder tension? Would you like to enjoy more freedom in everyday activities?

Under the guidance of an experienced teacher, we'll explore movement in ways that help you reduce tense unhelpful habits. Movement lessons are done on the floor or sitting on a chair and are based on the pioneering work of Israeli physicist and engineer Dr. Moshe Feldenkrais. This workshop is suitable for all ages (over 16) and fitness levels.

Outcomes
By the end of the workshop, you'll be able to:

Identify and reduce muscle tension
Move with more lightness and freedom
Improve your posture
Describe some basic anatomy
Have tools to use at home and at work

Bring two blankets (or a mat and a blanket) and wear loose, warm and comfortable clothing. Tea and coffee provided but bring your lunch.

Please note that instructions are given verbally rather than by demonstration, so good hearing and understanding of English is required.

1 Day
Presented by Sue Field.

Are you a computer slouch, feeling stiff and tense at work? Do you find it difficult to maintain a good posture?  Does your posture cause back, neck or shoulder tension?  Would you like to enjoy more freedom in everyday activities?
Under the guidance of an experienced teacher, we'll explore movement in ways that help you reduce tense unhelpful habits.  Movement lessons are done on the floor or sitting on a chair and are based on the pioneering work of Israeli physicist and engineer Dr. Moshe Feldenkrais.

events.long_description:
Auditions – Tom Jones the Operetta
Auditions: Principal Cast & Chorus for Tom Jones (the Operetta)

🕺 Not Tom Jones the Welsh singer
📖 The Tom Jones of classic literature!

🗓 31 October & 1 November
📍 Te Whaea, Newtown

Rehearsals: 28 February 2027 –
Show Dates: 24 April – 9 May, 2027

Directed by Alison Hodge & Michael Vinten

Book your audition slot:
https://sites.google.com/view/wgslo

Tom Jones is a retelling of Henry Fielding's comic novel, a bawdy tale of 18th century virtue and villainy, in a musical setting by Edward German. This production transports our hero to 1960s London, when an explosion of youth culture disrupted the traditional British class divide. The result is a fast-moving musical farce, with a diverse range of characters, full of colour and energy. The production will be accompanied by a small instrumental ensemble.

Operetta = Vintage Musical

An operetta is a comic opera with dialogue, just like musical theatre (but without microphones). Operettas are what came before classic musicals such as The Sound of Music. An operetta can be performed with small orchestra or piano, and does not necessarily require operatic singers. We encourage all confident singers to audition.

Book your audition slot:
https://sites.google.com/view/wgslo

Mātātupu Mātauranga: Future Thinkers celebrates rangatahi (15–24yo) and their unique perspective on the world. Get involved with te taiao-related creative workshops, tours, and activities, and then round out the day with a wānanga on how rangatahi envision a climate-focused future.

Painting the Future
10.00am–1.00pm, The Promenade
Dream up a sustainable future – bring it to life through painting and drawing. Work collaboratively with others to create a collaged vision of a climate-focused future.

Print Planting
10.00am–1.00pm, Signs of a Nation
Join illustrator Tayla Hartemink (Tūhoe, Te Arawa) to learn about stamp printing and plants growing in your backyard. Bring something from home to stamp or get creative on paper and fabric.

Fa‘atupu: Giving new life to old words (registration required)
10:30–12.00pm, Hīnātore
Join Mauatua Fa‘ara-Reynolds for this writing workshop inspired by the propagation of the aute plants across the Pacific. Participants are invited to bring excerpts of their own writing, or words from others, and use them as seeds for generating new work.
Registrations required for this session: https://events.humanitix.com/fa-atupu-giving-new-life-to-old-words

Beyond Be-leaf: Plant Stories in Bush City
10.30–11.30am and 12.00–1.00pm, Bush City Kiosk
What can plants teach us? What stories lie beyond the leaf? Join Curator Botany Leon Perrie for a tour of Bush City and work together to identify plants that are growing in our backyard during kōanga.

Holding Light: Slow Looking Tour
10.30–11.30am, 12.00–1.00pm, Slow Burn | Ahi Tāmau
Join slow looking tauira in a tour of Slow Burn | Ahi Tāmau – venture deep into photographic works made by rangatahi artists to discover how light illuminates stories.

Climate Wānanga
1.00–2.00pm, Rongomaraeroa, the marae
Indigenous rangatahi are the rākaugloss holding up the sky. This wānanga brings together young leaders in climate education and environmental justice to share how their work brings us closer to a climate-focused future.

Guest speakers announced very soon.

events.venue: 274B Jackson St, Petone, Lower Hutt 5012
events.long_description:
Old Jail Museum Open Day
Did you know Petone was the first place in New Zealand to have a Police force? Find out about this and other interesting Petone stories in the Old Jail Museum.

Come to the Old Jail Museum – a well-preserved former lockup. See an exhibition on Policing in Petone from 1840. Read about Jackson Street's heritage, plus various Petone stories, including our rich sporting history. It has information on Jackson Street businesses, directories, Petone walking tours, kids activity sheets, and more to take away.
Either our Heritage Office or a JSP Ambassador will be onsite.
Built in 1908 on Elizabeth Street, it was once the most senior Police Station in the Hutt Valley with ten constables and one sergeant. In the early 1950s, the Police Station and lockup (jail) were moved behind the old courthouse at 13 Elizabeth Street. Police used the courthouse as an office, but the lockup continued to be used – mainly for intoxicated offenders until 1978.


Cost: Free entry; koha is welcomed.

Learn more on our website:
https://wellingtonheritagefestival.co.nz/event/old-jail-museum-open-day-26/

https://wellingtonheritagefestival.co.nz/events/

Health & Safety:

events.long_description:
Overview

Re-use, Re-Purpose, Beautify with Gold!! Come along and learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Workshop.

After several SOLD OUT workshops in Wellington here is the next one... Oct 2026

Learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Workshop. You can bring along a piece of your own pottery to restore in this beautiful style. (I'll also have a few as back up if you don't have your own piece) (All Levels)

Saturday 31st October - 10:30am - 12:30pm or 2:00 - 4:00pm

Have you ever wanted to try Kintsugi.... It's an ancient Japanese art form where you fix broken pottery with gold - making its imperfections its beauty. - A truly wonderful philosophy to live by. Nothing is ever really broken but new life and meaning is brought back making your piece a work of art and truly something special. You can also apply this technique on various materials like glass, wood, greenstone and shells.


Kintsugi
It's called kintsugi (金継ぎ), or kintsukuroi (金繕い), literally golden (“kin”) and repair (“tsugi”). This traditional Japanese art uses a precious metal – liquid gold, liquid silver or lacquer dusted with powdered gold – to bring together the pieces of a broken pottery item and at the same time enhance the breaks.

You will take away your wonderful finished work, plus your new skills which will enable you to further your own Kintsugi in your own time.

What you will take away:
A finished artwork piece
A understanding of Kintsugi
Knowledge and History of this beautiful art form.

Where: Toi Poneke Arts Centre, 3 Market Lane, Te Aro,, Wellington 6011.
When: Saturday 31st October
10:30am - 12:30pm or 2-4pm

events.name: This Is Grief: On the Road
events.venue: Paraparaumu Public Library, 9 Iver Trask Place, Paraparaumu
events.long_description:
Grief is part of being human, but we still struggle to talk about it.

This Is Grief: On the Road is a free community event bringing honest conversations about grief, loss, love and the life that continues around them into communities across Aotearoa.

Join author and This Is Grief founder Kirsten O'Connor for a relaxed, human conversation about what grief really looks like, beyond the clichés, timelines and expectations we so often place around it. Kirsten will share from her own experience of grief and from her work writing and talking about loss, before opening the space for conversation and connection.

You don't need to have the right words. You don't need to share anything you don't want to. This is a space for anyone living with loss, or anyone who wants to better understand and support someone who is.

Come along, listen, talk if you'd like to, and be part of a conversation we don't have nearly often enough.

This is a free community event. Registration is recommended as places may be limited.

Visit the Upper Hutt Blockhouse
Discover one of the few remaining buildings associated with the New Zealand Wars.

Tucked down a side street in Trentham, the Upper Hutt Blockhouse is a rare example of a building connected to the New Zealand Wars.

Peek through the balistraria, explore the exhibition, have a good chat with our friendly and knowledgeable team, and find out what became of the Blockhouse in the many decades after its use as a defensive fortification.

Cost: $10 suggested koha

Learn more on our website:
https://wellingtonheritagefestival.co.nz/event/visit-the-upper-hutt-blockhouse-26/

This event is part of the 2026 Wellington Heritage Festival, running 24th October - 15th November. Discover over 160 more events on our website:
https://wellingtonheritagefestival.co.nz/events/

Health & Safety:
The Upper Hutt Blockhouse is a heritage building with a steep, narrow internal staircase. It may not be accessible for visitors with mobility issues.

All Heritage NZ properties are smoke and vape-free sites.

events.long_description:
Tucked down a side street in Trentham, the Upper Hutt Blockhouse is a rare example of a building connected to the New Zealand Wars.

Peek through the balistraria, explore the exhibition, have a good chat with our friendly and knowledgeable team, and find out what became of the Blockhouse in the many decades after its use as a defensive fortification.

Drop in between 11am and 2pm, and stay as long as you like!

This rare opportunity to visit the Upper Hutt Blockhouse is proudly offered by Heritage New Zealand Pouhere Taonga as part of the Wellington Heritage Festival 2026.

The open day is free to attend, but a koha is greatly appreciated.

Accessibility: Upper Hutt Blockhouse is a two-storey building with internal stairs and uneven surfaces, including a curb onto the grass and grass surrounds. The second floor may not be suitable for people with mobility issues due to the steep angle of the stairs. There is a drop-off point adjacent to the blockhouse for visitors with limited mobility. Unfortunately, due to the age and build of Upper Hutt Blockhouse it may not be accessible to people in wheelchairs. Our visitor hosts can share the history of our site with you from outside the building, showing you some of the features still on show from when the building was in use as a functioning blockhouse.

events.long_description:
Overview

Join us and learn more about this beautiful town!

🍇 Bienvenue en Charente ! Tucked away in south-west France, this is the land of cognac, comic books and some of the prettiest villages in the country, and most visitors drive straight past it.

Join Thomas for a fun and immersive workshop (en français !) and set off on a journey through the département, one stop at a time. You'll follow the Charente river through centuries of history, from the Abbaye de Saint-Amant-de-Boixe to the château of La Rochefoucauld. You'll wander the villages of Aubeterre-sur-Dronne and Verteuil-sur-Charente, then head through the vineyards to Cognac. And you'll explore Angoulême, the medieval city on the ramparts that became the world capital of la bande dessinée 💥

And of course, no trip to Charente is complete without its specialities: cognac, pineau, la galette charentaise and the famous cagouilles. Don't know what those are? Come and find out 🐌

🗯️ French A2/B1 level required
🗓️ Saturday, 31 October 2026, 11.30am–1pm
📍 Alliance Française Wellington (78 Victoria Street, Wellington)
🎟️ $30 for AF members & $35 for non-members

events.id: Concept to Completion: Masterclass with Charlie Faulks | Halloween 26-Aratoi Wairarapa Museum of Art and History, 12 Bruce St, Masterton-Event Finder
events.name: Concept to Completion: Masterclass with Charlie Faulks | Halloween 26
events.venue: Aratoi Wairarapa Museum of Art and History, 12 Bruce St, Masterton
events.long_description:
Concept to Completion: Masterclass with Charlie Faulks | Halloween 2026

How does a 19-year-old Screen Arts student get almost half a million dollars to make an animated zombie series set on a rural New Zealand farm?

That’s the story behind Bloke of the Apocalypse, and the starting point for an intimate masterclass with animator and filmmaker Charlie Faulks.

Charlie began developing Bloke of the Apocalypse while studying Screen Arts, making the first episodes independently before the project grew into a professionally funded animated series.

In this 90-minute masterclass, Charlie will take you behind the scenes of that journey, exploring how an idea develops, how early work can lead to bigger opportunities, finding collaborators, pitching and funding, animation and production, and what it takes to get a project through to completion.

There’ll be video excerpts and behind-the-scenes material, with plenty of time for questions and conversation.

This masterclass is for secondary students, aspiring filmmakers and animators, emerging creatives, writers, artists, storytellers, or anyone curious about how a screen idea becomes a finished project.

No previous filmmaking or animation experience is required.

Saturday 31 October 2026
1:00pm–2:30pm
Aratoi Wairarapa Museum of Art and History, Masterton

Adults $35
Secondary students $15

Places are strictly limited to 15.

This masterclass has been subsidised with grateful thanks to the Masterton District Creative Communities Scheme, helping make this professional development opportunity more accessible to the Wairarapa community.

Part of Halloween 2026 with The Story Studio.
