events.long_description:
Overview

Awaken your energy through guided breath, movement, sound and stillness in a powerful Kundalini activation experience.

Guided Kundalini Activation




Events now start at 6pm. Please try to arrive by 5:45pm so we can get everyone into the event and start on time at 6pm.



A guided kundalini activation. Breath of fire and kundalini pranayama, simple repetitive movement, sound and stillness, sequenced to wake up energy that has been sitting dormant along the spine and let it move.

Who is this for

People who already have some breathwork or movement practice and want something more activating than a wind-down class. You are curious about kundalini but want it held by someone who works with the nervous system, not bypasses it. You are willing to feel a lot and stop when you need to.

Not the right fit as a first-ever breathwork experience. The Root or a gentler breath class is a better start.

What to expect
Arrival and a short orientation: what kundalini activation is, what is normal, and how to opt out of anything
Progressive breath and movement rounds that build energy and heat
A peak where the practice is most active: emotion, shaking, heat, tingling, sound can all come up, all normal
A long, quiet integration: stillness, slow breath, nothing to do
A few minutes to land and share if you want to, before you leave
Benefits
A felt sense of energy moving where it had been stuck
Emotional release without needing a story for it
A reset for a system that has been running flat or wired-and-tired
A clearer, more spacious baseline for a day or two afterward

(No health claims. This is a practice, not a treatment.)

Pre-class prep
Skip heavy food and alcohol in the hours before.
Eat something light beforehand, not a full meal.
Come a few minutes early to settle
If you are pregnant, have a heart or blood-pressure condition, epilepsy, glaucoma, recent surgery, or are in acute mental-health crisis, message Lynn before booking so she can advise or adapt
Wear layers you can move in and get warm in.
Contraindications

Kundalini pranayama and breath of fire are intense. Please do not book, or check with Lynn first, if any of these apply: pregnancy, cardiovascular disease or uncontrolled high blood pressure, epilepsy or seizure history, glaucoma or detached retina, recent abdominal or chest surgery, acute psychosis or an unstable mental-health condition. If you feel dizzy or overwhelmed at any point you stop, breathe normally, and rest, that is always allowed.

We'll close the evening with a nourishing plant-based dinner and dessert, a gentle space to connect and ease back into your evening.


Meet your host, Lynn:
About Lynn

Lynn Tiang is an Integrative Somatic Coach, breathwork facilitator, and Reiki practitioner based in Aotearoa, New Zealand. Lynn supports people who are high-functioning on the outside but chronically tense, exhausted, or quietly stuck on the inside.

Lynn’s work blends three pillars:

Somatic breathwork to regulate the nervous system, soften protective patterns, and restore a steadier baseline in the body
Reiki to support energetic clearing, heart coherence, deep rest, and integration, in a gentle, consent-based way
Life coaching to translate what opens in a session into grounded change in relationships, work, boundaries, and daily life

Lynn’s approach is trauma-aware, practical, and spiritually spacious. The focus isn’t on forcing transformation, it’s on creating enough safety for your system to unwind, receive support, and reconnect with its natural capacity for calm, clarity, and connection.

1:1 Integrative Somatic Coaching. A November spot is open

If you feel a yes in your body during this session, you’re invited to go deeper. Lynn is opening a private 1:1 Integrative Somatic Coaching spot in November for someone ready to work with nervous system regulation, somatic inquiry, breathwork, Reiki, and grounded life coaching support.

To enquire, email hi@lynofuro.co.nz with the subject line: November 1:1.

Read less

events.long_description:
Overview

A welcoming men’s circle for honest conversation, deep connection and brotherhood in a space of trust, presence and belonging.

Men’s Circle: Rooted in Connection




Events now start at 6pm. Please try to arrive by 5:45pm so we can get everyone into the event and start on time at 6pm.




The evening offers a supportive space for men to come together, connect, and speak openly about life. Whether you’re moving through a period of change, looking for deeper connection, or simply wanting a space where you can show up as you are, you’re welcome here.

The conversations are honest, open, and grounded in mutual respect. There’s no pressure to speak, share, or have everything figured out. You’re just as welcome to listen and be present. Together, we create a space rooted in confidentiality and non-judgement, where everyone can feel safe, heard, and free to be themselves.

Structure of the Circle
Gathering in a Circle: Participants sit in a circle to symbolize equality and unity.
A short meditation or moment of silence may be included to help everyone arrive and connect.
Talking Object: A sharing stick or object is placed in the center. Only the person holding the object may speak, ensuring uninterrupted sharing.
Open Sharing: Anyone may choose to share while holding the object. Sharing is optional, and passing is always respected.
Active Listening: While one person shares, others listen attentively without speaking, interrupting, or offering advice. The focus is on witnessing and being present.
No Judgments or Advice: Participants refrain from judging or offering unsolicited advice, creating a safe space for authentic expression.
Closing: The circle may conclude with a group reflection, a moment of gratitude, or a simple acknowledgment of the shared experience.
Circle Agreements
Supportive Environment: We are here to uplift and support one another, fostering trust and brotherhood.
Focus on the Present: Share what's alive for you now, focusing on your emotions and experiences to deepen emotional awareness.
Use "I" Statements: Speak from your personal perspective using "I" statements to promote authenticity and responsibility. Avoid generalizations like "we" or "us."
No Judgment or fixing: Refrain from judging others sharing or offering unsolicited advice, ensuring a safe and non-critical space.
Confidentiality: What is shared in the circle stays in the circle. You may discuss your own experience outside the group but keep others' details private.




After the circle, stay for a wholesome plant-based dinner and dessert ($20 or $10 for students). Sharing a meal is a simple way to extend the sense of community and connection. This gathering is offered on a non-profit basis.
Meet Your Host: Sri Jiva

Since childhood, Sri Jiva has been fascinated by meaning, purpose, and authentic life fulfilment. This, among other things, led him to join a monastery at the age of 19. After years of monastic training, he chose to marry and pursue a career. He felt called to use his monastic experience to help others understand themselves, and to find wisdom, meaning, and purpose in their own lives. Inspired by this calling, he went to university to study counselling. Now, Sri Jiva and his wife live near Wellington, where he works with a small team of counsellors, supporting clients individually and in groups.

events.name: Pub Sing
events.venue: The Empire, 175 Jackson St, Petone, Lower Hutt
events.long_description:
Pub Sing - where the audience (you) turns into the choir at the pub, with a live rock band.

No sheet music, no experience needed, and absolutely no solos.

Katy reveals three songs on the night (usually a crowd-pleaser, a ballad, and a banger), and even if you don’t know them, you’ll pick them up fast with colour-coded lyrics on screen.

You learn different harmony options, sing along with the band, and blend into a room of up to 80 voices, so no one’s listening to you; they’re singing with you.

There’s banter, laughs, a bit of silliness, and a whole lot of feel-good energy. It’s not karaoke (shudder), it’s everyone singing together just for the fun of it, and it’s the perfect end-of-week lift you needed.

*Please check the booking link for updates or changes to dates*

*Tickets are $10pp, and all proceeds go directly to the band!

STRINGS & NEEDLES is an independent documentary project about young transgender musicians in Te Whanganui-a-Tara, underscored by the rising tensions of anti-trans politics in the parliamentary buildings right in earshot of Wellington's transgender population. events.long_description:
Spring is the ideal season to detoxify, reset your gut microbiome, and restore balance to your nervous system — a powerful step toward lasting vitality and emotional resilience.

Join Seleno Health for an inspiring and evidence-informed 2-hour workshop, where you'll discover our transformative 12-Week Gut Reset program. Drawing from ancient Peruvian wisdom (including revered superfoods like maca, cacao, yacon, and tocosh) and modern nutritional neuroscience, this practical guide empowers you to heal your gut, optimize your gut-brain axis, and support profound improvements in mental health, mood, energy, and overall well-being.

The workshop dives deep into the gut-brain axis — the bidirectional communication highway linking your gut microbiome, enteric nervous system, vagus nerve, immune pathways, and brain. Emerging neuroscience shows that a balanced gut ecosystem profoundly influences neurotransmitter production (such as serotonin — with ~90% made in the gut — and dopamine), stress response via the HPA axis, inflammation levels, and even neuroplasticity. Dysbiosis (imbalanced gut bacteria) is increasingly linked to conditions like anxiety, depression, chronic fatigue, brain fog, and mood instability, while nurturing beneficial microbes can promote emotional regulation, reduced stress reactivity, mental clarity, and resilience.

You'll learn science-backed strategies to:

Rebuild a thriving microbiome with targeted prebiotics (e.g., yacon syrup's FOS and inulin to feed good bacteria), probiotics (e.g., fermented tocosh as a wholefood "Penicillin of the Andes" for potent gut repopulation), digestive enzymes, and gut-healing foods (bone broth, collagen, slippery elm, turmeric).

Harness mood-enhancing superfoods: adaptogenic maca for hormone balance, stress management, and vitality; mineral-rich cacao loaded with flavanols, theobromine (a gentle energizer), tryptophan (serotonin precursor), phenylethylamine (the "love chemical" that boosts dopamine reward pathways), and bliss molecules that elevate mood, cognition, and creativity while reducing inflammation — all supporting the gut-brain connection.

Boost detoxification, immunity, and cellular protection with GPx Immune Protect, which enhances your body's natural glutathione peroxidase systems (and related antioxidant enzymes) to combat oxidative stress — a key factor in fatigue, burnout, chronic inflammation, and mood disorders.

Integrate nervous system reset tools: mindful eating, breathwork, gentle movement/yoga, and daily mindfulness practices to calm the vagus nerve, lower cortisol, and enhance parasympathetic "rest-and-digest" mode — directly benefiting both gut function and mental/emotional health.

The session also explores how these interventions tie into the endocannabinoid system (ECS) — your body's master regulator of stress, mood, inflammation, and homeostasis. A healthy microbiome supports ECS signaling (via microbial metabolites and fatty acid precursors), which can help alleviate anxiety, depression symptoms, and anhedonia (lack of pleasure/motivation), creating a virtuous cycle for brain and gut health.

You'll receive actionable tools, including:

The full PDF 12-Week Gut Reset daily planner and holistic guidance.

Personalized ideas for chronic fatigue, autoimmunity, hormonal imbalances, or stress-related conditions.

Tips to reduce reliance on medications through natural, food-first approaches.

Interactive Q&A, real-life case studies (showing gains in energy, mood stability, skin clarity, reduced inflammation, and emotional well-being), and practical integration steps ensure you leave empowered and equipped.

Whether you're seeking preventive wellness, mood optimization, or support for persistent challenges, this gut-centric, neuroscience-informed approach — rooted in wholefoods and ancient remedies — helps you unlock your body's innate healing potential from the inside out.

Spaces are limited — register now to revitalize your gut, brain, and life this Autumn!

Register now to begin your journey to a vibrant, healthier you!

-Dr Corin Storkey (PhD – Med Chem) has over 20 years of academic and research experience, specialising in medicinal antioxidant chemistry, oxidative diseases, cellular protection and integrative health. He has previously struggled with and overcome chronic fatigue syndrome and promotes an integrative and holistic approach to managing chronic health conditions. He currently leads the New Zealand based Maca and cacao research program that studies Andean and Amazonian plant medicines and their bioactives. Their latest project "From Bean to Brain" is investigating how ancestral cacao biodiversity and processing impacts on gut microbiota and the mechanisms of how cacao acts to health the gut and improve mood.

events.long_description:
Home Brew are one of Aotearoa’s most beloved hip-hop groups, rising to equal parts greatness and infamy through their extensive run of EPs through the early 2010s and culminating in their now-classic #1 self-titled debut. The band re-entered the charts with their brand-new album Run It Back in 2023, securing them a raft of new fans.
Their aggressively DIY ethos has endeared them to many in the New Zealand Hip-Hop music scene, and they have cemented their place in history as one of the country's most authentic, uncompromising acts.
Following the overwhelming response to their sold-out Auckland Town Hall performance earlier this year, audiences across Australia and New Zealand will now experience one of Aotearoa's defining hip-hop releases performed live in full, alongside the songs that have shaped the band's enduring legacy.

events.long_description:
Overview

Join us for a long weekend of sewing at Himitangi Lodge. - a weekend of stitching, and relaxation! 6 - 9 November 2026 COST:$390pp

Spring Sewing Retreat - Friday 6th to Monday 9th November.

Please add yourself to the event if you are interested in attending :-) We can take up to 14 people.

Beautiful new location for the Spring retreat! Bring your own machine and supplies and head off into the countryside with some like minded fabric hoarders.

COST Cost is $390 per person for three nights for an individual room and vegetarian catering provided.

Upon signing up you will be sent an invoice for the cost of the Retreat, which can be paid in installments or all at once. All payments must be completed by 3 weeks before the event (16th October).

If you pay and are unable to come, we cannot issue a refund but you can get someone else to take your place.

In the event of you being unable to attend due to Covid, I will provide as much of a refund as I am able without leaving me personally out of pocket for any expenses that i am not able to recover.

BEDDING Linen and towels are provided, but consider bringing an extra towel and blankets etc if you get cold.

FOOD Food is catered from Friday evening. Meals included are Friday dinner, Saturday breakfast, lunch and dinner, Sunday breakfast, lunch and dinner, Monday breakfast and lunch. Please let us know at time of booking if you have special dietary requirements - there may be a small surcharge for special food requests.

TRANSPORT We will try to car pool so those without their own transport get to come and we can cut down on petrol costs. If you share a car (and aren't driving) you will be expected to contribute to petrol costs. Car pooling is generally arranged between participants themselves, but let us know if you need help with this.

OTHER INFORMATION What to bring
For sewing: Desk and chair will be provided. Please bring your own multi-point plug and extension cord. A desk lamp may also be appropriate.
For sleeping: bedding is provided, but bring your hot water bottle if you like.
Shared resources: if you are able to bring an irons, ironing boards, and cutting boards to share, please say so in the Facebook event discussion so that we can get coordinated and arrange to communally share these.
Activities - Walking shoes for relaxing walks, and swimming togs and towel if you want to use the pool! Please let us know of anything else you think we should add to this list.

UPDATES As new information is asked for, I will update this description to keep all the relevant information together. Please ask any questions you would like answered by email.

Read less

events.name: EMBERS: Food By Fire With Chef Dale Keith
events.venue: Alexia Urban Winery, 197 West Street, Greytown
events.long_description:
From the open-air hearths of the Mediterranean, spit-roasting has long been at the heart of seasonal feasts, old traditions and the simple pleasure of gathering around good food.

An ancient art that demands hours of patience & a watchful eye. It is the ultimate expression of hospitality — a labour of love, made to be shared.

We’re bringing the art of the slow spin to Alexia with food by fire, a two-part dinner series celebrating the beauty of slow food cooked over open flames by pitmaster Dale Keith — part chef, part alchemist of fire, smoke, sizzle and crackle...

Part one: Greece.

A journey to the heart of Greek tradition arni sti souvla, where lamb turns slowly over the fire, preparing for a gathering of hungry guests.

Elemental cooking. Generous feasting. A little fire-fuelled theatre.

Follow the smoke to Alexia.

Bookings essential.

events.name: Mini Mosaics - Taster Class
events.venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
events.long_description:
Mini mosaics are really quick and simple to make - but can create a real design punch with colourful glass pieces and a set of three mosaics to make a “triptych” set.

You can have the finished items as either:
A triptych set on a backing board
A set ready to hang on a wall as singles
On a large sturdy jumpring ready to hang as a cute pendant set (or earrings).
On a cord for an heirloom Christmas ornament.

The class covers:
Preparing your bases and materials
Planning and choosing simple designs to make your mosaics really pop
How to snip your glass down into tiny pieces if needed (most pieces are already cut for you)
Working with adhesives, tips and tricks with tools.
Finally we will cover grouting and finishing your mosaics - including mounting options and more.

Some students may finish in time to grout your pieces - seeing these pieces are SO small, they are often dry enough for grouting. Or you can take your grout away to do at home, or leave with us to grout for you and collect in a few days. (There’s a small fee attached to that part.)

This is a warm and friendly class with excellent support and learning for complete beginners and those who want to begin to work with hand-cut glass terrerae.

All tools are supplied, though you are welcome to bring your own tools and glass if you have them.
Your materials for the class projects are supplied as part of your course fee.

Young makers aged 12 and up are welcome to join the class, as long as they are able to work safely with sharp glass and tools.

Anyone under the age of 16 must attend with an enrolled parent or caregiver who is there to support them and participate alongside them.

No notes, no powerpoints, just raw, personal, real stories.
Afterwards people stay to chat, connect and tell a few more (informal) stories before the night wraps up.

After a highly successful Auckland/Northland tour the Korimako Trio are back in Wellington with a new programme.    

The Korimako Trio (Helene Pohl, violin; Rolf Gjelsten, cello; Michael Endres, piano) brings together three internationally renowned musicians with decades of experience who are beloved in New Zealand for their powerful communication as well as the intelligence of their playing.

In this concert they bring you music ranging from Zemlinsky's Trio, opus 3 ("the epitome of 1890s Vienna: lush, grand, romantic, impassioned") to the exuberance of Chopin's Introduction and Polonaise brilliante (cello and piano), and Janacek 's dramatic Sonata for violin and piano.

The programme closes by returning to the composer who established the piano trio as a genre. Haydn's Trio in A major crowns the evening with luminous grace, wit and a joyful affirmation of music's power to delight.

events.long_description:
Restoring what was wounded. 

Recovering what was lost. 

Becoming who God created us to be.

 

Do you at times struggle to fully embrace your identity as a son or daughter of God? Do you feel like you know who you are in Christ, but struggle to walk in it completely?

Then this event is for you!

 

Join us for a powerful journey of healing, hope, restoration, and discovery of your identity in Christ led by Sandra Sellmer-Kersten.

Through biblical teaching, prayer ministry, and compassionate support, you’ll be invited to encounter Jesus in the places where you’ve experienced pain and discover His invitation to healing and wholeness.

Whether you are personally seeking healing or want to gain some tools to help others walk in and embrace their identity in Christ, this event offers practical insights, spiritual encouragement, and opportunities for prayer and ministry.

 

Sessions include:

The Heart: Restoring what has been wounded and broken.

The Identity: Remembering who God says we are—and learning to live from that truth.

The Voice: Recovering what shame, fear, pain, and rejection have silenced.

The Song: Reawakening the unique “song” God has sung over each of us from the beginning.

The Calling: Rediscovering what we were created for—and stepping into what God has entrusted to us with His power and authority. 

 

What to Expect:

Biblical teaching on trauma and healing

Opportunities to receive prayer

A safe, compassionate, and supportive environment

Encouragement, hope, and practical tools for restoration

Included in your ticket:

Morning and afternoon tea will be provided, but please bring your own lunch

A comprehensive manual, usually sold separately for $25

About Sandra:
Sandra Sellmer-Kersten is the founder of House of Nacham Ministries, New Zealand, which she leads alongside her husband, Peter. She previously served for nine years with Elijah House Ministries USA, where she worked as a prayer minister and teacher under the leadership of John and Paula Sandford. Since moving to New Zealand, Sandra began working alongside Elijah House New Zealand, where she facilitates schools, teaches lessons, and has served as a Small Group Leader for 14 years.

Sandra has a deep passion for seeing people encounter the healing love and transforming power of Jesus Christ. Through teaching, prayer ministry, mentoring, and training, she helps people understand the impact of trauma and woundedness, and to find healing, rediscover their God-given identity, and step more fully into who God created them to be.

Her teaching combines biblical truth, practical understanding, personal experience, and more than two decades of ministry experience, with an emphasis on creating a safe and compassionate space for people to honour their stories and encounter Jesus.

This event is not suitable for those under 16.

events.long_description:
Eigenface are heading out on a tour around Aotearoa to celebrate the release of their debut album, with support from Michaela Tempers.

Eigenface is a New Zealand/New York trio that blend folk intimacy, dream-punk atmospheres and electronic experimentation. Their songs move between comfort and unease, pairing bright melodies with dissonance, layered vocal harmonies and richly textured arrangements.
"Eigenface have developed a softly charming style that finds beauty in uncertainty. Their sound finds comparison with US indie rock acts Loma and Son Lux (both also trios), but for many the apparent connection will be to the stellar likes of Radiohead and Portishead." (Richard Thorne, NZ Musician). "It's the type of thing you can listen to over and over again" (Chi-Chi Attard, Happy Mag - Australia). "Dynamic, intriguing and addictive: it pulls you in and refuses to let go" (Oliver Zurita of Expansión Radial - Spain).

The band comprises Penelope Esplin (French for Rabbits, Lake South, Grawlixes) on synth and vocals, Elliot Vaughan (CNZ/NZSM Composer in Residence 2024, Moth Quartet, RNZ Concert Presenter) on bass and vocals, and Logan Valentine (Moon Lander) on electric guitar and vocals. For these shows, Penelope and Elliot will be travelling as a duo, bringing Eigenface into a more intimate live setting. The group formed from an impromptu challenge to write and perform on one another's work, the result became a cohesive set of songs, resulting in Eigenface's self-titled debut album.

Released on Home Alone Records, Eigenface arrives on October 2, 2026. Recorded and mixed by Vaughan and mastered by Harris Newman (Wolf Parade, Buck Meek, Godspeed You! Black Emperor), the album features Vaughan's lush string arrangements throughout. Across its songs, the band explores memory, place, relationships and the tension between beauty and discomfort through expansive arrangements, electronic textures and intimate storytelling.

Eigenface’s debut single, House by the Sea, reached #1 on RDU (Christchurch), #4 on Radio1 (Dunedin) and #2 on the Student Radio Network Charts. Their second single, Slow Exposure, reached #1 on RDU, #3 on Radioactive (Wellington) and #2 on the SRN Charts. Their third single, Twizel, reached #1 on RDU and #1 on the SRN Charts. They've now been nominated for the SRN People's Choice Awards 2026. Eigenface have appeared at Day in the Bay, The Performance Arcade and Newtown Festival, and shared stages with Lake South, Julian Temple and The Broken Heartbreakers.

Michaela Tempers is a writer and musician based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara, Aotearoa. Tempers singing voice has been described as “a rare warbling instrument that will leave you grasping for comparisons” (Tony Stamp, RNZ). “Her voice and musical vision establish her as a striking new presence in our ever growing and evolving folk music landscape – honest, rich, insightful.” (Tim Gruar, Muzic.NZ).

Tempers’ debut EP, recorded alongside producers Brooke Singer (French for Rabbits) and Chris Armour (Miles Calder, Louis TM ), is brimming with “sincerity leavened by wit and uniquely dynamic constructs” (Richard Thorne, NZ Musician). Tempers will be joined by Dayle Jellyman (organ) for the North Island shows, and Chris Armour (guitar) for the Wellington show. She has opened for Creedence Clearwater Revival, Holly Arrowsmith, Jed Parsons, Irish folk band Boega, as well as Australian folk artists Boy & Bear.

Eigenface Album Release Tour
Friday 2nd October – Space Academy, Christchurch
Saturday 3rd October – Pearl Diver, Dunedin
Friday 6th November – Vogelmorn, Wellington
Saturday 7th November – Porridge Watson, Whanganui
Thursday 12th November – Big Fan, Auckland
Friday 13th November – Last Place, Hamilton

Tickets on sale via undertheradar.co.nz

events.long_description:
★★★★★ "There can be few more accomplished raconteurs at the Fringe than James Nokise."
— The Wee Review

★★★★★ "Nokise is a joy to have onstage."
— The Scotsman

There's three things you can count on this election year; Ministerial soundbites that age like milk, policy walk-backs hours after announcements, and James Nokise having hot comedic takes on the chaotic campaigns around the country.

One Night Rant returns in 2026 with a new hour of frenetic furious funny aimed at politicians across the spectrum. No Party or policy is safe as Nokise lets loose on the political powers that be.

Book early as this is the one show where the news cycle does half the research for a night of comedy, catharsis, and fist shaking, boot stomping fun.

"If you've long suspected Parliament might be a comedy of errors full of farcical characters, this show will bring receipts." — James Nokise

You've seen him on TVNZ, heard him on RNZ, and read him on Stuff. Now he's bringing the election to your town — for one night only.

Topp Prize winner 2024 · Fred Award 2019 · The Last Voyage of the Rainbow Warrior — Best Documentary, 2025 NZ Radio & Podcast Awards

—

And a few unsolicited character references:

"The cheapest hour of therapy you'll get this election year."
— A Ministerial Press Secretary, speaking anonymously (obviously)

"The funniest hour you'll spend this election season."
— Every Political Reporter in the Press Gallery, off the record

"He's coming all this way to vent about politicians. Least you can do is turn up."
— A Local Resident, speaking voluntarily (allegedly)

—

THE DETAILS
The Fringe Bar, Wellington
Friday 6 November, 8pm. Doors 7.30pm.
Election eve. This show is being filmed and livestreamed.
Approximately 60 minutes, no interval.
Early bird $27, then $30 general admission from 11 September. Limited door sales $35. Booking fees apply.
Tickets from iTICKET.

Adult themes, coarse language, and political satire throughout. Recommended 16+.

Full tour dates and more info at jamesnokise.com

events.long_description:
Midwave Breaks celebrate the release of their first full-length album, with four special shows across New Zealand.

Tauranga Alt-Rock Duo Midwave Breaks invite you to celebrate the release of their first full-length album, alongside Special Guests, with four shows across the Motu.

Since launching in 2021, Midwave Breaks have captivated fans, across airwaves and stages around New Zealand, with 8 independent radio singles hitting the NZ Top 10 Rock Airplay Charts, a nod for Best Rock Act at the 2024 Aotearoa Music Awards, and Highlight-Reel live performances in support of Incubus, Live, and Devilskin.

As a two-piece, Midwave Breaks deliver a huge sound, infectious live energy, and dynamic performance. Special guests across the tour include, The Response, The Rainfall, Courtnay and The Unholy Reverie, No Pilot, Not Exact, and Van Brookes.

Echo. Tide. Awake. is the first full-length studio album from Midwave Breaks, featuring 13 new tracks for 2026 – all written, recorded, mixed, and mastered by the band themselves, in the spare room of a farmhouse, overlooking the Bay of Plenty coastline in New Zealand. Midwave Breaks reimagine the sounds of their youth through a modern lens, epitomized by 80’s-90’s alternative rock/pop - evoking hints of Springsteen and Petty, Cornell and Vedder, and a melting pot of musical influences from past to present. Echo. Tide. Awake. explores cyclical themes of time and perspective, reframing the past to better illuminate the present.

events.long_description:
Central Region RWC Introduction Course
The Rescue Water Craft (RWC) commonly known as a Personal Water Craft (PWC) or Jetski is specially outfitted for surf interaction and operated by experienced Surf Lifeguards.

As the operator of a Rescue Water Craft you are responsible for the safety of your crew, the public and yourself. It is important that you understand the risks inherent in operating this type of equipment and your role in assessing and minimising risk.

The qualification has a number of theoretical and practical components such as driving in the surf, patient pick up and maritime regulations to prepare experienced Surf Lifeguards for RWC use.

Prerequisites:

Current & active member of a SLS club
Surf Lifeguard Award (Refreshed)
20 years of age minimum on the first day of the introductory course.
Radio Communication Module or Maritime VHF Operator's Certificate
Senior Lifeguard Award - IRB Driver (Refreshed)*
Surf First Aid (Refreshed)**
400m Pool swim under 7.30 minutes
*A minimum of 2 years from IRB Award including 2 seasons operating as a IRB driver is required (at a minimum one IRB driver refresher must have been completed in the last year)
**An RWC Operator must hold a Surf First Aid prior to attending their RWC exam.

Link to more information and the application form is in the comments.
Send the completed application form to Justine at

events.name: Rathkeale Christmas Fête 2026
events.venue: Rathkeale College Auditorium, Willow Park Drive, Masterton
events.long_description:
Welcome to the Rathkeale Christmas Fête 2026.

Walk through the gates of Rathkeale College on 7 November and be welcomed by a diverse range of colourful stalls, the aroma of freshly cooked food, and plenty of festive inspiration.

Now in its 23rd year, the Christmas Fête has become a must-do event on the Wairarapa spring calendar. Stallholders travel from around the North Island to sell their wares and offer Christmas shoppers plenty of inspiration. From festive decorations, clothing, arts and crafts, to flowers, toys, and plants, there is something for everyone.

Gourmet food is always a highlight at the Fête. Think freshly made gourmet burgers, lamb and mint sausages, salads, and the ever-popular berries and ice cream. There is always a huge variety of flavours to tempt the taste buds. Devonshire teas and home baking served in the Rathkeale Homestead rose garden is a time-honoured tradition, while refreshing cold drinks can be enjoyed as visitors listen to live music performed by students at various times throughout the day. The popular Christmas cake stall features again this year, but visitors are encouraged to get in early, as the cakes often sell out by midday.

The beauty of this Fête is that it’s a day out for the whole family. In addition to the 120-plus stalls, there is plenty to entertain children, including a barrel train ride, face painting, and magic shows throughout the day.

Visitors can also explore the beautiful, expansive grounds of Rathkeale College, including the school gardens designed by Alfred Buxton, the recently installed Paul Dibble sculpture The Choice, the Greek Amphitheatre, and the 3km eco-trail, which weaves through large stands of native trees, including ancient kahikatea.

EFTPOS is available, but visitors are encouraged to bring cash.

Koha / gold coin entry

Rathkeale College is a five-minute drive north of Masterton in the Wairarapa.

events.id: Cheesemaking - Brie And Queso Fresco-Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki St, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Cheesemaking - Brie And Queso Fresco
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki St, Wellington
events.long_description:
During this intensely practical, hands-on workshop, you will be guided through each step of the cheesemaking process while making your very own round of Double Cream ‘NZ style’ Brie. You will also be shown how to make Queso Fresco cheese which you will get to sample afterwards. All ingredients included in course fee.

The ultimate class in practical cheese making! Learn all you need to know to replicate making NZ style Brie and Queso Fresco at home. You will be guided through each step of the cheesemaking process while making your very own round of Brie. Then, while the Brie is ripening and setting (don't worry, all terminology will be explained!), we will make Queso Fresco together.

All ingredients are provided as are recipes and detailed handouts to take away with you. Bring an apron, a dishcloth, 3 or 4 tea towels, a pen to take notes and a 2 litre container and plastic re-sealable food bags to take your cheese home.

During the workshop, the following topics will also be covered: Milk and where to source it, hygiene and sanitation, equipment required and the origins of the cheeses you are about to make. You will also receive comprehensive instruction on how to mature your Brie cheese over the next few weeks.

A small break will be provided and you will have the opportunity to purchase equipment and cheesemaking ingredients after the workshop should you wish to replicate the experience at home.

By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:

Make Brie and Queso Fresco
Recall the best milk to use and where to source it from
Name and identify what equipment and ingredients you need to make Brie and Queso Fresco

Note: Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

1 Day
Presented by Alexis Murti.

Gain an introduction to the Māori art of flax weaving in an intensive one-day workshop, suitable for beginners and those with some experience.   
By the end of the workshop, you'll be able to:
•  Identify commonly-used types of harakeke
•  Describe how to harvest and prepare harakeke for use

events.venue: 4 Rawhiti Street, Stokes Valley, Lower Hutt 5019,4 Rawhiti St, Stokes Valley, Lower Hutt 5019, New Zealand, Lower Hutt
events.long_description:
Nature in the Making: A Children’s Nature-Inspired Art Adventure
Let curiosity lead the way in this nature-inspired art adventure for children.

With gentle prompts and plenty of room to explore, children can experiment with paint, texture and mark-making, and may also try collage. There’s no prescribed picture to copy and no expectation of a particular result. The focus is on noticing, experimenting and following the artwork as it develops.

No art experience is needed. Each child can take part in their own way and discover what they enjoy making.

Nature in the Making is a fundraiser for an overseas mission trip.

A ticket supports the trip and gives children a chance to enjoy a creative session inspired by nature.



Who's it for? any children in Year 4 upwards.

Who will be supervising? Kim Shaw (registered teacher and church youth leader) with other police-checked helpers.

What's involved? Children will be supervised outside on the church property observing natural elements, like trees, leaves, flowers, moss, shadows. Weather dependent they will either work indoors in the hall or outdoors on their artwork.

What do they need? a willingness to get curious and have a go, clothes they can get a bit messy and/or a painting shirt or apron.

events.long_description:
Overview

The Old St Paul’s Craft & Curio Market returns – and in 2026, we’re got even more going on!

Brought to you once again in association with the Wellington Heritage Festival, this year the interior, forecourt and lawn of Old St Paul’s will fill with a bigger line-up of designers, collectors, artists, food producers and small businesses.

Expect vintage surprises, heritage crafts, leather goods, textiles, embroidery, clothing, artisan food, candles, Christmas decorations, children’s wares, collectibles and plenty more – with new stalls joining returning favourites from last year.

As well as weaving and embroidery demonstrations, try some biscuit decorating inspired by our stained glass and learn about bellringing! Join one of our guided tours of Old St Paul’s and experience the pipe organ in action. There is absolutely loads to do and eat, so you won’t go hungry!

Koha entry.

Bring the whole whānau and spend your Election Day Saturday discovering something new (and not so new!) at Old St Paul’s.

Stallholders include tailored children's clothing line, Moonland; Taxidermy Art by Antoinette Ratcliffe; She Means Biscuits, The Wellington Embroiderers' Guild; Micro Mill; Thread Journeys; Thorns & Aces; Miriam Tong Art, and many, many more.

Guided tours of Old St Paul's: 10.30am + 11.30am

Live jazz performance by members of The Guiding Tones: 11.15am-11.45am

Wellington Combined Society of Bellringers demonstration: 12.00pm-12.45pm

Wellington Embroiderers' Guild stitching demonstration + Micro Mill weaving demonstration: 10.00am-2.00pm

Plus! We have an amazing surprise guest!

events.venue: Mangaroa Farm, 98 Whitemans Valley Road, Te Awa Kairangi, Upper Hutt
events.long_description:
Join Mangaroa Farms for a Sourdough Bread Baking Workshop with Doris Zuur, who has been baking the slow way for decades: rye sourdoughs raised on a living starter, wholemeal loaves that rise through an afternoon, Swiss Zopf plaited by hand, focaccia, and a fermented buckwheat loaf for those who can't take wheat. Her bread is the kind that fills a house with its smell and a table with quiet conversation.

Spend an afternoon with her in our kitchen. You'll mix, knead, plait and bake alongside her. You'll learn how to keep a starter alive, how to read a dough by touch, and the small decisions — temperature, time, a bit of gusto — that turn flour and water into a good loaf.

You'll leave with:

A jar of living starter to take home
A warm loaf from the oven
Doris's full recipe collection (rye sourdough, wholemeal, Swiss Zopf, fermented buckwheat, focaccia, Oaties)
Her "0800 bread helpline" for when you need a hand at home

Afternoon tea included. Bring a clean glass jar with a lid, an apron, and a willingness to slow down.

Good bread likes it slow.

We will begin at Sat 7th November | 10:00am at Wharekai - 298 Whitemans Valley Road

Any questions, please email events@mangaroa.org

A fun Storybook Stomp! Pop your Red Bands or gummies on and join Pukeko and our storytellers, Rachel Solomon and Alice Horsham for this story walk in lovely Carrington Park in Carterton.
The walk will finish with a Sausage Sizzle.
Meet at the High Street side of Carrington Park, where the playground and toilets are.

This walk is one of 3 oral language and numeracy events during the Wairarapa Walking Festival this year and you are invited to attend as many as you would like to.
On Saturday, 7 November, there will be a Storybook Stomp and Sausage Sizzle in Carrington Park, Carterton.
On Tuesday, 10 November, in Masterton and Thursday, 12 November, in Greytown, there will be a special walk around a quiet area of town discovering shapes, numbers, colours, letters and wonderful things to talk about.
The activities and times are designed for parents and grandparents to join in and pick up fun ways for encouraging curiosity and chatter with the children they care for.

This walk suits young children and babies, their parents, grandparents, homeschoolers, teachers and carers.

events.long_description:
Overview

Try your hand at the creative skills behind the movies — from special effects makeup and costume to sword-making, slime and more!

With fantastical creatures, elven jewels, warriors’ armour, vampire portraits and more, Scene Stealers shines the spotlight on the artists behind Aotearoa New Zealand’s film industry. Many of these incredible craftspeople who make movie magic will be at The Dowse to celebrate the opening of this exciting exhibition. There will be opportunities for you to hear from them, see them in action…and even get in on the action yourself.

Scars and Scrapes with Wētā Workshop. Scare your friends with the addition of a special effects scar applied by the team from Wētā Workshop.

Barbarian Productions Dress Up Jam. Get into character with Barbarian Productions and their seemingly bottomless wardrobe department of costumes for you to try on and style. Dress up, act up and wig out!

Fighting and Falling. Stunt Master Allan Henry will teach the tricks of the trade and have you looking like you’re rumbling with the heavyweights without ever landing a punch.

These activities are part of a day of programmes celebrating the opening of Scene Stealers. This also includes industry experts in panel talks:
10.30-11.30am Scene Stealers In Discussion: Creative Costuming
12-1pm Scene Stealers In Discussion: Behind the Lens

Dive into the fantastic realm of foliage and discover what plants have to teach us about worlds present and past.

Join us for a 60 to 75-minute guided walk exploring the fascinating world of plants and the stories they tell. From ancient survivors and remarkable adaptations to the clues plants give us about changing landscapes, you'll discover how foliage can reveal both the history of our planet and the natural world around us.

The Cottage is celebrating its 150 birthday this year!

Come and explore the home of John and Jane Golder and their 12 children. Take a peek into the past and marvel at the way Upper Hutt people lived before electricity and water were installed. events.name: Designing Your Next Permaculture Project
events.venue: Mangaroa Farm, 98 Whitemans Valley Road, Te Awa Kairangi, Upper Hutt
events.long_description:
Join Mangaroa Farms for a Permaculture Design Workshop that goes well beyond the garden patch. This afternoon session introduces you to permaculture as a design tool for life itself — your community projects, your business, your relationships, even your next family meal.

We'll explore the design process together, then apply it to real situations in small groups. You'll learn to use permaculture ethics as a lens: Is what I'm doing caring for the planet and people? Is it ensuring a fair share of resources? This isn't about following recipes — it's about principles, careful assessment, and truly listening to what each unique situation needs.

When you reach a crossroads in life, whether chosen or unexpected, the permaculture design tool offers a framework. A scaffold for moving forward with intention, embracing diversity and care, and making good use of your time and energy.

This is an introductory session. The topic is as vast as life itself, and as diverse and magical as the natural world around us.

We'll gather in the garden if weather allows, otherwise in the Whare Kai. Expect circle work and small breakout groups where we'll learn from each other's experiences.

We will begin at Sat 7th November | 2:00pm at the Mangaroa Events space at 298 Whitemans Valley Road.

Any questions, please email events@mangaroa.org

events.long_description:
Join us for this fabulous introduction to working with colourful molten glass!

This class is a great way for absolute beginners to get a taste of working with glass to produce beautiful beads that can be used in a myriad of ways, including making a unique gift for your loved one (or yourself!).

As one of the earliest forms of human adornment, beads have long functioned as a way to express individuality, and what better way to do that than to learn to make your own unique beads?

Students are shown correct lampworking techniques to produce several decorative beads in just 3 hours! How many beads you make is up to you; some students make up to 10 while others make fewer using trickier techniques.

Kids over 12 (or so) are welcome to take the class, but anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

events.name: Tukutuku workshop
events.venue: 3 Market Lane, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
This workshop will demonstrate the very basics of Tukutuku where each participant will come away with a form of Tukutuku and knowledge to inspire their own mahi toi. 

All materials supplied. Prior to the workshop participants are encouraged to research Tukutuku patterns and become familiar with the meanings.

 

Artist biography.
Elena Rei
Ngāti Toarangatira, Ngāruahine, Ngāti Koata, Ngāti Tama, Sāmoa 

Elena Rei’s creative practice sits within the realm of Te Whare Pora, weaving together customary and contemporary processes of raranga, whatu muka and tukutuku. Interlaced throughout her works are collective dreams, moments of remembering and profound experiences with the materials she uses. Much of Elena’s practice is intuitive, emulating the ways of her tūpuna and drawing from a visual language that has been woven through time. Her works reimage and make familiar our inherent connection to ngā atua wāhine, through themes of aroha, grief, whakapapa and reconnection. 

Elena studied design and textiles at Massey University, where she gained early insights into practices within Te Whare Pora. A formative experience during this time was learning tukutuku under the guidance of Kohai Grace during classes at Whitireia, an experience that continues to inform her practice today.

events.long_description:
French Pastry for Beginners
A 4-Week Hands-On Series

Step into the world of French pâtisserie with our beginner-friendly four-week course designed to teach you the essential techniques behind some of France's most iconic pastries. Guided by Le Ciel's experienced pastry chef and owner, Shuchi, you'll build your confidence week by week as you learn the foundations of classic French baking.

This progression-based course is perfect for anyone who loves baking, wants to develop professional techniques, or is looking to begin their pastry journey. Each class focuses on a new skill while building on what you've learned in previous weeks, making it easy to continue growing as a baker.

Week 1 – French Macarons

Take on one of France's most famous pastries with confidence. Learn how to create smooth macaron shells, perfect feet, balanced fillings, and troubleshoot common problems so you can recreate them successfully at home.

Week 2 – Choux Pastry

Master the fundamentals of pâte à choux as you learn to mix, pipe, bake, fill, and finish classic French favourites including profiteroles and éclairs. You'll also learn how to make silky pastry cream and achieve perfectly crisp shells.

Week 3 – French Tarts

Discover the secrets to beautiful French tarts by learning sweet pastry dough, blind baking, creamy fillings, fruit finishing, and professional presentation techniques.

Week 4 – Mille-Feuille

Complete the course by creating the elegant Mille-Feuille. Learn how to work with puff pastry, prepare rich vanilla crème pâtissière, assemble delicate layers, and finish with a professional glaze.

What's Included
Four hands-on classes
Step-by-step instructions from professional pastry chefs
All ingredients and equipment are provided
Recipe booklet to take home
Your creations to enjoy and share
Small class sizes for personalised guidance

Who is this course for?

This course is ideal for complete beginners and enthusiastic home bakers. No previous baking experience is required—just bring your enthusiasm and a love of French pastries.

By the end of the four weeks, you'll have mastered a range of foundational pastry techniques and be ready to continue into our future intermediate pastry workshops.

Spaces are limited to ensure every participant receives plenty of individual guidance. Early booking is recommended.

We will be running 2 starts for this course:
Dates for course:
First course: September 5th, 12th, 19th and 26th
Second course: November 7th, 14th, 21st and 28th

events.name: Exhale Evolution

events.long_description:
Exhale Evolution
✨ Grounded Grace Counselling x Alchemy Ascending ✨

https://momence.com/Yoga-Corner/EXHALE-EVOLUTION/143442298

3 hour workshop, Movement ~ Breathwork ~ Sound Journey

Saxon Brazier from Grounded Grace Counselling and Kez Milne from Alchemy Ascending bring you a 3-hour immersive workshop combining Somatic Movement, Conscious Connected Breathwork and Sound Odyssey.

A deep dive into the body — creating space to slow down, rest, digest and reconnect with what is happening beneath the surface.

You might arrive carrying stress, emotions, old hurts, tension, overwhelm or simply the weight of everyday life.

Through conscious connected breathwork, somatic movement and sound, we create a safe and supported space to explore what your body may be holding — without needing to force, fix or figure anything out.


🌿 CONSCIOUS CONNECTED BREATHWORK

Conscious Connected Breathwork is a rhythmic breathing practice where the inhale and exhale are intentionally connected, creating a continuous flow of breath without pause.

As we consciously connect the breath, we bring greater awareness into the body. Physical sensations, emotions, thoughts and patterns may begin to come into awareness, creating space to notice and explore what is present.

Rather than trying to think our way through an experience, the breath invites us to move out of the thinking mind and into the body — meeting whatever arises with curiosity, awareness and compassion.

The practice is centred around presence and allowing, rather than forcing an emotional release or trying to create a particular outcome.


🎶 SOUND ODYSSEY

Following the breathwork, Saxon's Sound Odyssey will invite you into a deeply immersive sound experience designed to help you settle, integrate and reconnect with the body.

Having previously sold out her Sound Odyssey experiences, Saxon weaves together drums, medicine drum, guitar and vocals to create a rich and organic soundscape.

Moving from rhythm and activation into softer, settling vibrations, the sound journey offers space to simply lie back, breathe and receive.

A meeting point of sound, vibration, voice and stillness — allowing the body and nervous system time to integrate whatever has arisen during the breathwork.


✨ YOUR FACILITATORS

Kez Milne — Alchemy Ascending
400-hour accredited Conscious Connected Breathwork Facilitator.

Saxon Brazier — Grounded Grace Counselling
Registered trauma-informed counsellor with training in breathwork and somatic facilitation.
https://www.groundedgrace.nz/

Together, Saxon and Kez will hold a grounded, carefully facilitated container for you to explore breath, body, emotion and sound.


⚠️ SAFETY & CONTRAINDICATIONS

Safety is paramount. Breathwork is not suitable for everyone.

Conscious Connected Breathwork involves sustained, active breathing and can produce significant physical and emotional experiences. For this reason, there are certain circumstances where participation may not be appropriate.

This workshop may not be suitable for you if you:

• Are pregnant or may be pregnant
• Have a history of cardiovascular disease, heart attack or significant heart problems
• Have uncontrolled high blood pressure
• Have a history of stroke, aneurysm or significant vascular disease
• Have epilepsy or a seizure disorder
• Have severe or uncontrolled asthma or significant respiratory disease
• Have a current serious psychiatric condition, psychosis or significant difficulty distinguishing internal experiences from external reality
• Are experiencing acute psychological distress or significant mental health instability
• Have recently undergone major surgery or have another significant medical condition that may make intensive breathwork unsafe
• Are under the influence of alcohol or recreational drugs
• Have another medical or psychological condition that may make an intensive breathwork practice unsafe for you

If you are unsure whether this practice is appropriate for you, please speak with your doctor or qualified healthcare professional before booking.

Participation is voluntary and you can stop or modify the practice at any time.

Every participant will be required to read the full disclaimer and contraindications and sign a waiver confirming that they understand and agree to the terms before entering the workshop space.

We take the responsibility of holding this space seriously. Safety, consent, choice and nervous-system awareness are paramount throughout the experience.


🌿 BOOKING & ONBOARDING

Once your booking has been made, we will send you a full onboarding pack with everything you need to know before the workshop, including what to bring, how to prepare and important instructions for arriving and entering the space.


3 HOURS

Somatic Movement • Conscious Connected Breathwork • Sound Odyssey


Come as you are.

Create some space.

Breathe. Move. Feel. Listen. Integrate.

Tickets here:

https://momence.com/Yoga-Corner/EXHALE-EVOLUTION/143442298

After hearing their parents fight, Finn (Roman Griffin Davis, Jojo Rabbit) and Charlie (Dexter Sol Ansell, breakout star of A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms) sneak out of their house in Doncaster.

So unfolds an epic road trip from Yorkshire, over land and sea, to the wild West Coast of Ireland. Their destination? The small seaside town of Dingle, County Kerry, where they will reunite with their beloved Grandfather, John (Nighy).

It’s a long, treacherous journey - 500 miles where a lot could go wrong... And while Dingle holds happy memories for the boys, Grandpa John has remained estranged from Finn and Charlie’s parents after fateful events the previous summer.

With knockout performances from all involved, 500 Miles will make you laugh, cry, and hug the people you love.

events.long_description:
Kina:suttsu (Japan) + vegetable.animal.machine
Pyramid Club is excited to present Japanese musician, performance and visual artist Kina:suttsu. Utilising saxophone, electronics, noise, and field recordings, Kina:suttsu creates immersive performances that blur the boundaries between ancient ritual and contemporary experimental music.

Since releasing her first album in 2005, she has performed and exhibited in Japan and internationally. Her releases include music on labels in the UK and France, including a cassette as NAVU and a collaborative release with Phil MFU, Zongamin, E-Da (ex Boredoms, Seefeel). She has recorded with legendary bassist Jah Wobble and released a live recording with Damo Suzuki. In 2021, she appeared in and composed the soundtrack for British filmmaker Daisy Dickinson’s short film Kaki no Shizuku, which was selected for the Los Angeles Film Awards.
-
vegetable.machine.animal (vma) is an interspecies improvisational trio led by drummer Kieran Monaghan, which transforms the electrical signals of living plants and fungi into sound, fusing modular synths and live percussion in performances that are spontaneous, rhythmic, and unpredictable. This is music as a living system - a real-time collaboration where non-human organisms shape the sonic outcome alongside human performers.


Special thanks to Creative NZ and Wellington City Council for supporting Pyramid Club's programme.

events.name: Duntulm Farm Wairarapa Dog Walk
events.venue: Duntulm Farm, 820 Mangatarere Valley Road, West Taratahi, Carterton
events.long_description:
The Wairarapa Dogwalk Group is an informal group of dog owners who get together once a month to exercise our dogs. The aim of the walks is to go somewhere in the region where we can walk the dogs off lead.
The Duntulm Farm walk is one of our favourites.
On private property in a seldom visited area of the Tararua foothills that offers two walks. Both stop at the Trotternish Shed which is located beside a hidden large pond on a remote corner of the farm for a cup of tea / coffee and a snack.

The Valley Walk follows a gentle 4WD track up a steep sided valley to the shed.
Depending on the weather the return walk can go down the opposite side of the valley via Side by Side vehicle tracks.
Walking time is about 60 minutes including an approximately 15 minute stop at the shed.

The UP and Over walk is for the fitter walkers.
It climbs steeply up Side by Side tracks up to the ridgeline. There is a lookout point with unique views into the Tararuas. A 10 minute stop to catch your breath then the track descends quickly down into the valley and around to the shed for drinks and snacks.
We return to the carpark via the Valley walk 4WD track.
Around a 2 hour walk (including stops).
Walkers on this walk are recommended to carry a small backpack with water and extra clothing.

events.name: Stained Glass Suncatcher Day
events.venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
events.long_description:
Create gorgeous simple leadlight suncatchers with Lisa Sinclair.

A super fun day-class, ideal as a stand-alone experience, or as a day to get stuck into projects with your tutor at hand.

Beginners choose from a range of achievable patterns and choose their colour palette. They will learn to cut the glass, and prepare it before foiling and soldering each piece, creating a simple elegant colourful glass project.

The aim of this one day class is to leave with a completed small leadlight glass item.

More experienced students may bring existing projects to work on in class - though emphasis will be placed on focusing on the same techniques of flat, nicely soldered simple designs.

This is a warm and friendly class with excellent support and learning for complete beginners and more advanced students. All tools are supplied, though you are welcome to bring your own tools and glass if you have them.

Your materials for your beginner project are supplied as part of your course fee.
Additional materials and tools are available to purchase.

Not suitable for children. Older teenagers (16+) are welcome.

Visit Llandaff, Brancepeth and the Masterton Greek Orthodox Church as part of the Wellington Heritage Festival.

Robin Dunlop and Ed Beetham are offering their support for this year’s Wellington Heritage Festival by arranging a tour of two significant heritage homesteads in the Masterton area, Llandaff and Brancepeth, and a visit to the Greek Orthodox Church.

events.name: Twin Peaks The Return: Parts 13, 14, 15
events.venue: 7 Colombo Street, Newtown, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
events.long_description:
"It was a dream...We live inside a dream"

-Phillip Jeffries

We are now hurtling towards the brilliant conclusion of the series with our second LAST screening of "The Return: Parts 13, 14, 15"

These episodes are truly incredible with arguably the most emotional moments of the entire show.

Also ever since "Fire Walk With Me", every single fan has been haunted for 25 years by the inexplicable lore surrounding David Bowie's character. Get ready to come "full circle" as we meet once again the original head and founding member of the Blue Rose Task Force: The enigmatic Special Agent "Phillip Jeffries" in The Return!

Last seen at "The Palm Deluxe Hotel" in Buenos Aires, Argentina. We will be screening the mythic, uncut original and extended David Bowie performance from "The Missing Pieces of FWWM" to melt our minds in preparation.

It's gonna be a big session filled with emotional highs and lows and filled to the coffee cup brim with lore. So if you're a Twin Peaks fan you can't miss this one!

We'll be playing Parts 13,14,15 from the "Z to A" Blu-ray projected from a 4K player onto a 5.5m x 3.7m screen.

Written by Mark Frost, David Lynch and directed by David Lynch.

This is what we will be watching :

David Lynch "Weather Report" and song of the day.

"Previously on Twin Peaks"

The Missing Pieces: "Buenos Aires, Above the Convenience Store" (23mins)

The Return: Part 13 - "What story is that, Charlie?" (58mins)

Intermission

The Return: Part 14 - "We are like the dreamer." (55mins)

The Return: Part 15 - "There's some fear in letting go." (53mins)

WHERE: Newtown Community Centre. 7 Colombo St. Newtown.

(nb: There is no onsite parking and parking on surrounding streets can be hard to find)

 

WHEN: Gather from 10:45am on Sunday 8th November 2026.

The screening shall start at 11:00am SHARP!



COST: A lucky $7.

This is a small (<40) not for profit community event put on for the love of Twin Peaks and the fans!

All proceeds go to help pay for the venue hire and fun snacks! So come join your fellow Twin Peaks fans as we "shovel our way" through some donuts, "two cookies and a coke...it's phenomenal!"


RULES:
1. Please purchase a ticket for each person beforehand, as capacity is limited to ~40 seats

2. All attendees MUST be 18yo +

3. This is a safe, friendly, INCLUSIVE place. There is ZERO tolerance for discrimination, disrespect or creepy gross behavior of any kind. By attending you agree to the Code of Conduct.

4. Doors close and it's lights off and "Shhhh Shush!!!!" at 11:00am. Don't be late!

5. No Alcohol / No Smoking is permitted.

Thank you! "This is your shiny, gold shovel. Two coats, guaranteed."

Join us for more Twin Peaks community screenings at:

www.facebook.com/fishinthepercolator

www.instagram.com/fishinthe.percolator

events.long_description:
Overview

Love cake? So do we! Join us at The Cake Club Picnic – a one-of-a-kind gathering dedicated exclusively to cake. You don't want to miss it!

Welcome to The Cake Club Picnic! 🍰

By popular demand and our first cake picnic was a success, we are happy to host another epic Cake Picnic!

Join us for a deliciously fun day out at Bellevue Gardens Hotel on Sunday, November the 8th, 2026.

Whether your a professional baker, a passionate home baker, or simply someone with a sweet tooth, The Cake Club Picnic is the perfect event to indulge your love of all things cake!

Entry requires both a ticket and a cake - one per person.
Everyone attending must bring a cake of their own. No cake, no entry - no exceptions. This rule keeps things fair and fun for everyone involved.

Even if you're bringing a guest under tickets you have purchased, they must bring a cake too. Sharing one cake between two people won’t cut it. We appreciate your understanding and commitment to the cake-loving community!

🎂 What to Expect:

A relaxed indoor and outdoor garden setting - enjoy the space rain or shine!

A shared cake table filled with baked goodies brought by everyone attending - taste, share, and show off your creations!

Chill vibes and great company - meet fellow cake lovers, swap stories, and make sweet memories.

Picnic-style seating - bring a blanket, find a sunny spot, or grab a seat indoors.

A self-service tea and coffee station to keep your cup full as you sample cakes.

Cake Size Requirement:
Please bring a cake that can generously serve at least 12 people. Think full-sized bakes -enough to share and make sure everyone gets a proper slice (or two)! 🎂✨ - REMEMBER - CAKE ONLY!

Cake Set-Up:
You’re welcome to do final touch-ups at the venue, but please avoid full setups or major decorating on-site. Display tables will be shared with other guests, so we want to keep things smooth and stress-free for everyone.

Serving Tools, cake detailed label & Cake Stands:
Please remember to bring your own serving tool so guests can easily cut and enjoy your cake.

We will provide you with a cake label card and card insert stick for everything to look uniformed!

Want to show off your creation? Feel free to bring a cake stand to elevate your cake-literally and visually! 🍰🔪✨

Boxes & Utensils:
We've got you covered! The host will provide boxes for you to pack up cake slices during the event, along with forks, spoons, napkins, and water to keep things easy and enjoyable. 🍴📦💧

Rubbish:
Let’s keep the vibes sweet and the space clean! Please use the bins provided on-site and help us leave the venue just as lovely as we found it. We also kindly ask that you take any leftover rubbish or personal items with you when you head out. ♻️🧼💛




Disclaimer & Event Guidelines

This is a community-friendly event, and all participants are expected to behave in a respectful and responsible manner toward others. By attending, you agree to be patient, follow the event rules, and respect everyone's space, time, and contributions.

If you are bringing a homemade cake, you confirm that it has been prepared in a clean and safe environment to the best of your ability. Please note that food is consumed at your own risk, and the event organisers and venue accept no responsibility for allergic reactions or food-related illnesses.

Cakes that contain common allergens (e.g. nuts, dairy, eggs, gluten) must be clearly labelled to help others make informed choices.

This event will be photographed and filmed for use in future marketing, content, and social media promotion. By attending, you grant permission for your image and likeness to be used across both online and offline platforms by the event organisers.

You attend this event at your own risk. The organisers, volunteers, and venue are not liable for any injury, loss, damage, theft, or illness that may occur. Please keep an eye on your personal belongings - you are responsible for them.

Thank you for helping us keep this a fun, safe, and inclusive experience for all! 🍰💛

Bring your appetite, your friends, and your best bake. Everyone is welcome - just come ready to relax, connect, and enjoy a truly sweet day out!

events.id: Textured Bracelets-Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Textured Bracelets
events.venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
events.long_description:
This lively, hands-on workshop is designed for complete beginners, but it’s also a great opportunity for more experienced students to enjoy a creative session making their own unique bangle!

Everyone will leave with a beautifully finished bracelet of their own preferred texture.

We’ll begin by experimenting on a sample strip of copper, where you’ll practice creating textures using hammers, punches and stamps. Once you’re confident, you’ll move on to your main project: a 3mm wide flat strip bracelet in either sterling silver or copper, crafted entirely by you from start to finish. Along the way, you’ll learn essential jewellery-making skills including measuring, texturing, soldering, shaping, and finishing.

Students are free to personalise their bangle with textures or stamped designs. This could be a simple hammered finish, decorative patterns, or meaningful words, names, dates, or poetry lines - making your bracelet truly one of a kind.
Beginners will work with the 3mm strip provided, ensuring a rewarding project that’s manageable to complete. Wider metal is much harder to form and solder, so we are learning to walk before we can run ;)

Copper is included in the course fee; if you wish to work in silver, you can purchase it on the day.

Experienced students may choose to challenge themselves by making a wider bracelet from a flat strip or by creating additional bangles in silver wire. (Please note: extra silver for wider bangles is available to purchase at the workshop for experienced students only, and let us know if you wish to go wider so we can make sure we have the strip in stock.)

This workshop is a taster class: perfect for anyone seeking a fun, creative experience with a beautiful result, or for those looking to dip their toes into jewellery making and build foundational skills.

events.name: Tones of Silence; Futuna Chapel in Black & White with Dr Malcolm Doidge
events.venue: Futuna Close, off Friend Street, Karori, New Zealand 6012,62 Friend St, Karori, Wellington 6012, New Zealand, Wellington
events.long_description:
Tones of Silence; Futuna Chapel in Black & White with Dr Malcolm Doidge
Dr Malcolm Doidge presents his 360-degree time-lapse photography project, captured in Futuna Chapel across the 2023–2024 equinoxes and solstices. A short film of the project will be screened, followed by insights into the digital processes behind its creation.

About the speaker:

After completing his studies at the University of Canterbury School of Fine Art in 1984, Malcolm Doidge worked for the New Zealand Correspondence School as an illustrator. He received his first commission from Lincoln College (now University), producing the work 'Ascent' in 1984.

In more recent years Doidge has taught Creative Technologies at Weltec (Wellington) and completed a Doctor of Philosophy, Inside Arcadia: An immersive virtual phantasmagoria. His degree was conferred by Massey University, Toi Rauwhārangi College of Creative Arts, in 2022.

His work has been recognised by several awards including the Wallace Art Award (2004, 2006, 2009, 2013 and 2016), the Visa Gold Art Award (1998) and he was the premier award winner in the NCC Art Award in 2002.

events.venue: Martinborough Town Hall, 8 Texas Street, Martinborough
events.long_description:
Korimako Trio
Helene Pohl, violin; Rolf Gjelsten, cello; Michael Endres, piano

The concert opens with Zemlinsky's Trio in D Minor, a late 19th century example of Viennese Romanticism, lyrical, dense and emotionally expressive. This is followed by Janacek’s Violin Sonata (for violin and piano) deeply dramatic with folk elements. A return to Romanticism with Chopin’s Introduction and Polonaise Brillante in C major, for cello and piano follows and the concert concludes with Haydn’s Piano trio in A major (Hob.XV), bright and witty, with plenty of classical charm. A beautifully varied journey through four distinct musical eras, balancing full trio textures with virtuoso duo highlights.

events.id: Ascent up Maunga Rangitūmau-Te Rangi Lodge, 490 Bluff Rangitumau Rd, Masterton-Event Finder
events.name: Ascent up Maunga Rangitūmau
events.venue: Te Rangi Lodge, 490 Bluff Rangitumau Rd, Masterton
events.long_description:
Ever wondered what that high hill is just north of Masterton with the aerials on it?
This is the impressive Rangitūmau Maunga - important in the story of Haunui-a-Nanaia, who long ago came this way after pursuing his runaway wife Wairaka down the west coast of Te Ika a Māui.

The group will meet and part at Te Rangi Lodge, and set off together up the hill.
The tramp is a steady, but not steep, uphill climb to the top where there are 360 degree views.

Local writer, researcher and storyteller Joe Potangaroa (Ngati Kahungunu, Rangitane, Tuhoe, English) will participate, and share his knowledge of tikanga, taiao and Wairarapa history linked to Maunga Rangitūmau.

The walk will take 2 - 2.5 hours and is suitable for fit walkers & trampers. The walk starts at 200m elevation and climbs to 604m elevation.
Please note access is through a working farm, please observe all health and safety instructions given on the day.

Koha accepted for the cuppa tea provided.

events.long_description:
Paint a Mo, save a bro, supporting Movember

Get creative for a good cause! This November, we’re getting behind Movember with a special Paintvine event in Wellington supporting men’s health.

Grab your girlfriends, your partner, your dad, your brother – or anyone who’s keen for a creative night out – and join us as we paint our very own moustachioed masterpiece. And to help get you into the painting spirit, your ticket includes one house beer or wine to enjoy while you create. Cheers!

Our Paintvine artist will guide you step by step from a blank canvas to your finished painting, so absolutely no art experience is needed.

And because it wouldn’t be Movember without a magnificent Mo, everyone will get a stick-on moustache to wear on the night!

Paintvine is a proud supporter of Movember, with proceeds from these events supporting their work in men’s mental health and suicide prevention, prostate cancer and testicular cancer.

There’ll also be an opportunity to make an additional donation to Movember on the night if you’d like to contribute even more.

Whether you’re a seasoned painter or haven’t picked up a paintbrush since school, come along, get creative and help us support the health and wellbeing of the men we know, love and couldn’t imagine life without.

What is Paintvine?
It’s a fun social painting class where our artists will run you through step-by-step instructions on how to create your very own masterpiece in a fun and relaxed bar setting. Perfect for dates, catching up with mates or for meeting new friends!

We provide all the materials you need (high-quality canvas, acrylic paint, brushes). All you need to bring is your creative spirit! Our events are held in licensed venues, so you can purchase drinks to sip on while you paint. At the end of the night, you’ll leave with a painting you created yourself – you might even surprise yourself with what you can achieve!

For tickets, future events, FAQs and more info head to the Paintvine website ⇒ paintvine.co.nz

events.venue: Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Almost thirty years after the duo cut their teeth in the comedy clubs of Wellington, Flight of the Conchords are coming home. Fans can expect a career-spanning set. It will include hits from their Emmy-nominated HBO series and two critically acclaimed studio albums. 

After taking an eight-year break from performing, Bret McKenzie and Jemaine Clement burst back onto the live scene in 2026. They played two sold-out shows at Los Angeles’ Greek Theatre. That followed five intimate warm-up shows at Wellington’s Meow Nui. While they put the Conchords on ice for a few years, the pair both remained busy. Bret won an Academy Award for Best Original Song for ‘Man or Muppet’, wrote songs for ‘The Simpsons’ and‘The Minecraft Movie’, and released two solo albums. Jemaine has focused on the screen, creating comedy horror TV shows ‘Wellington Paranormal’ and ‘What We Do In The Shadows’. He’s also appeared in films including the last two ‘Avatar’ instalments. 

Don’t just think about it, get your tickets before they’re gone.

events.long_description:
Overview

Presentation & korero to equip youth workers with skills to support rangatahi with addictive traits in a culturally safe & responsive way

Explore how the teenage brain is wired for addictive behaviours, including cellphones, vaping, smoking and other substances. Learn to recognise early warning signs, respond effectively, and gain practical strategies to help young people build healthier habits and make positive choices.

The training is suitable for anyone who works with young people who would like greater knowledge and understanding, along with tools to support rangatahi overcome addictive traits in a safe and culturally responsive way.

This training is presented by the Nelson Tasman Youth Workers Collective, delivered by the Collaborative Trust and made possible thanks to support from Department of Internal Affairs and Rata Foundation. Limited spaces available so get in quick to reserve your placeTickets on sale through Eventbrite.There is no charge to attend this training for Nelson Tasman Youth Workers Collective members.

Not a member? Sign up here and take advantage of our free training opportunities.




Meet the kaiako;


Dr/Dame Sue Bagshaw
Dame Sue calls herself a 'youth worker with a medical degree'. Incredibly knowledgeable on all things youth... she has been a champion for positive youth development throughout her life, with notable mentions being that she founded Te Tahi Youth (youth one-stop-shop), The Collaborative Trust, and The Youth Hub in Ōtautahi Christchurch.

Ollie Flett
Youth Tutor Ollie Flett works as a youth wellbeing practitioner at St Bedes College in Christchurch in their wellbeing team and is a whānau support worker. He has a psych degree, a post-grad cert in counselling and has lived experience with neurodiversity, substances, online culture, and harmful gaming/technology use.

events.venue: Unity Books, 57 Willis St, Wellington
events.long_description:
Join us to launch Puke, a new book from essa may ranapiri. The book will be launched by Jasmine Sargent. Ruby Solly and Midden Rahurahu will read poetry in response to Puke.

Tuesday 10 November, 6pm
Unity Books Wellington
Free event – all welcome!

They first meet a million years ago, in the eruption of a volcano.

The second time, it’s in a liquor store: Hinenuitepo is buying a lighter for Mahuika; Hinemoana is picking up drinks.

Before long, they become entangled in rituals of mortality— love, hot chips, a carved bone strap-on, multiple evictions and a new puppy—all while holding down their duties as Death and the Sea.

But there is a great sickness rising in them both. The other atua have begun to disappear, and their world is slowly dying. Somewhere, an insidious power waits.

As the story shifts between our two lovers, Puke weaves a modern puuraakau of desire, decay and decolonisation.
