events.venue: Cavern Club,18 Allen St, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand, Wellington
events.long_description:
Getting Started in Standup - Wellington
Have you always wanted to try stand-up comedy but don’t know how to start?

Comedian and writer Neil Thornton brings you a fun, low-pressure comedy workshop.

Sign up here: https://www.nzcomedyschool.com/enroll

Suggested koha: $20

Everything you need to know to get a mic in your face:
-generating ideas
-joke writing
-effective delivery
-where and how to get practice
-how to avoid many common mistakes new performers make.


------
This class is also an intro to our upcoming "Complete Course" in Wellington

Getting Started (open to all): Tuesday 10 November 6:00pm-9:00pm (Cavern Club)
Class 1: Tuesday 17 November 6:00pm-9:00pm
Class 2: Tuesday 24 November 6:00pm-9:00pm
Class 3: Tuesday 1 December 6:00pm-9:00pm
Class 4: Tuesday 8 December 6:00pm-9:00pm
Graduation Show: Friday 11 December 8:00pm (Fringe Bar)

Price $450+gst - Includes all classes and materials, two private writing/coaching sessions, and your graduation video.

More info: https://www.nzcomedyschool.com/



In addition to his career as a stand-up comedian, Neil Thornton has been teaching for more than 25 years. He earned his BA in English from Carnegie Mellon University and his MFA in writing from the University of New Orleans.

He published fiction and essays in several literary journals and magazines and taught college English for 9 years, running classes in Creative Writing, Composition, Creative Nonfiction, Technical Writing, and Managerial Communication.

After moving to New York City in 2007, Neil became a working stand-up comic, performing everywhere from major comedy clubs to seedy dive bars in Washington D.C., Provincetown, Fire Island, and the Poconos. More recently, what was supposed to be a six-month adventure in New Zealand has turned into a permanent home.

Since then, Neil has made a big impact on the New Zealand comedy circuit. He has toured up and down the country and all over the world, entertaining audiences with his battles of understanding Kiwi culture and finding his own identity. He's a regular at The Classic in Auckland, and appeared in the TV3 comedy special "After Hours."

Neil now teaches from Wellington, New Zealand, where he continues to write, perform standup, and raise two giant Alaskan Malamutes.

events.name: LINDY LAB: Level up your Lindy!
events.venue: Newtown Community Centre - Te Whare Hapori o Ngā Puna Waiora,Wellington SCL Newtown, 74 Colombo St, Newtown, Wellington 6021, New Zealand, Wellington
events.long_description:
LINDY LAB: Level up your Lindy!
Calling all those who want to level up their Lindy! We have a special two week crash-course designed specifically for those who want to make the jump from beginner to intermediate (and those who want to brush up on their skills)!

Basically, if you're wanting to move up in your Lindy journey but not sure how to get there, these open-level workshops are for you!*

They’re also a great option for any intermediate dancers who want to build a solid foundation for 2027 and beyond, or for those who want to try switching leading/following!

Week 1 | Nov 10, 6:30pm-8:45pm: Swing-out deep-dive

Swing-outs are one of the fundamental moves that make Lindy-Hop, well, Lindy-Hop! They're awesome but can be tricky to master (journey not a destination!) In this 2h workshop we'll hone in on the craft and techniques that make swing-outs feel oh-so good, as well as introduce some fun styling and variations you can incorporate to make them your own!

Week 2 | Nov 17; 6.30pm-8:45pm: Improver essentials

Switching between the fundamental Lindy footwork can be a challenge! This 2h workshop is designed to build your confidence in moving between 6-count, 8-count and Charleston. On top of this, we'll be focusing on expanding your dance vocabulary so you can hit the social dance floor with style!

*For beginners who come to both workshops you’ll (pretty much) be ready to join intermediate classes in 2026! (Please still check in with the facilitators before committing to intermediate classes).

Venue:
Te Whare Hapori o ngā Puna Waiora | Newtown Community Centre.

Price:
$20/workshop. We want to make these workshops as affordable as possible so there's nothing stopping you reaching your Lindy goals!

**Please aim to arrive at least 10min before class starts so we can sign you in**

events.long_description:
Overview

Our Leadership & Management Part 2 workshop will equip leaders and managers with the skills to build high performing and motivated teams.

Learn how to make the transition from buddy to boss and lead a successful team. As John F. Kennedy once said, “leadership and learning are indispensable to each other”. Our Leadership & Management courses are designed to help you get the best performance from yourself and your team, providing you with the skills and techniques to become better than you ever perceived you could be.

The Leadership & Management Part 2 workshop will equip leaders and managers with the skills to build high performing and highly motivated teams; the skills to communicate effectively as a leader, become more self-aware, provide coaching and mentoring, deal with conflict in a constructive and productive manner along with developing ways to solve problems as a team.

This workshop also gives participants an understanding of the key concepts of leadership and leadership styles along with how to choose and implement a leadership style that is authentic and beneficial to both the organisation and the teams they serve.

Course Prerequisite: Participants must have a good understanding of leadership and management fundamentals and/or have previously attended the Business Training New Zealand - Leadership & Management Part 1 course.

For more information or to book: email info@biztrainers.co.nz or call 04 974 8790

events.name: Python ML & AI Bootcamp: 1 Day Practical Workshop in Wellington
events.venue: Level 4/6 Gilmer Terrace, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
About This Course

Duration: 1 Full Day (8 Hours)

Delivery Mode: Classroom (In-Person)

Language: English

Credits: 8 PDUs / Training Hours

Certification: Course Completion Certificate

Refreshments: Lunch, snacks, and beverages will be provided


If you would like weekend training sessions, kindly reach out to us at info@mangates.com for availability and scheduling.


Course Overview


The Machine Learning & AI in Python course empowers you to understand, build, and evaluate predictive models using Python. You will learn the fundamentals of supervised and unsupervised learning, model evaluation metrics, feature engineering, and get a glimpse into neural networks and deep learning. With practical hands-on exercises, this course prepares you to transition from theory to real-world machine learning applications.


Learning Objectives

By the end of this course, you will:

Understand core machine learning concepts and workflows

Build supervised and unsupervised models using scikit-learn

Evaluate model performance using appropriate metrics

Apply feature engineering techniques to improve predictions

Gain basic knowledge of neural networks and deep learning

Use Python for real-world AI and ML problem-solving

Target Audience

Data scientists, ML engineers, developers, and advanced Python users.

Why is it the Right Fit for You?

If you’re looking to take your Python programming skills into the realm of machine learning, this course is ideal. With a strong focus on applied learning and best practices, you’ll build models and analyze datasets that mirror real-world challenges. Overview

Think big! Explore bold ideas, fresh thinking and what makes us human, at Massey's hands-on day celebrating humanities and social sciences.

The Big Think is a festival of ideas for high school students, hosted by the College of Humanities and Social Sciences at Te Kunenga ki Pūrehuroa Massey University. Together, we'll explore how making sense of the world is a human and social thing.

Across all three Massey campuses this November, staff, students and graduates will share how the humanities and social sciences help us to understand what it means to be human, to live with others, and to act with care and purpose in a fast-moving, technology-infused, and often demanding world.

From communication and media to psychology, philosophy, planning, ethics, creative writing, emergency management, and even what we can learn about today’s world from history and classics, The Big Think shows how human-centred thinking helps us navigate change, make better decisions, and thrive in contemporary society.

You'll meet Humanities and Social Sciences staff, graduates and current students who will share their study and career journeys. Then, you'll get to have a go yourself, in a wide range of interactive workshops, from broadcast journalism skills to beta-testing a new psychology-based game to hacking the gaps in Wikipedia.

The skills that will future-proof you are human: come discover yours with us.

events.long_description:
Build culture by design, not by default - one ritual at a time.

Facilitate meaningful culture change and create connection through the power of workplace rituals.

This masterclass is for people who want to build stronger, more connected workplace cultures — and are ready to turn values and intentions into real, daily action.

Whether you're a leader, culture champion, facilitator, or change consultant, this training will give you the tools and confidence to run your own Workplace Rituals Workshops using the WRD (Workplace Rituals Deck).

Led by co-creator of the deck, Lotty Roberts, this is a hands-on learning experience rooted in emotional culture, intentional design, and purposeful leadership.

In this Masterclass, you'll learn:

What rituals are and why they are important

Why rituals matter in workplaces

The difference between habits and rituals

In depth knowledge of each of the 4 parts of the deck and why they are important

How to use our PARR model to craft rituals that stick

How to run the Rituals Audit

How to guide groups through ideation, crafting and action

Tips and tricks for using the deck first hand, along with the story and background behind the deck.

You'll walk away as a Certified Workplace Rituals Deck Practitioner, with confidence to run rituals sessions with your own teams or clients.

events.id: Duntulm Farm hilltop circuit tramp-Duntulm Farm, 820 Mangatarere Valley Road, West Taratahi, Carterton-Event Finder
events.name: Duntulm Farm hilltop circuit tramp
events.venue: Duntulm Farm, 820 Mangatarere Valley Road, West Taratahi, Carterton
events.long_description:
Explore the regenerating and mature bush on Duntulm Carbon Farm, with some of the tramp exploring the adjacent Tararua Forest Park. Mostly on single footpaths and some on farm tracks.
We should see mature rata, kahikatea, totara, rimu, miro, native clematis, possibly mistletoe and various orchids.
There will be extensive views both over the Wairarapa Plains and up to Taratahi/Mt Holdsworth.
The walk will cross the new bridge, go through a shallow crossing of Kiddie Creek, up into the "dress circle" near point 637, along to Holdsworth lookout, down to Duntulm Cottage for a cuppa, followed by a flattish walk out on farm tracks or an optional extra tramp up to pt 533 and down a different track back to the bridge.
Although there have been walks on Duntulm Farm most Wairarapa Walking Festivals, this is a different and fairly challenging route. We will take it reasonably slowly!

Terrain notes: steep hills, stream crossings, scrambly paths through the bush.
Have you comepleted a half-day tramp in the last 6 months?
Once registered, you will sent details on what to bring, suggested clothing, food, water and will need to supply an emergency contact person.

events.long_description:
Hickety Pips & Others - Aspects of Military Matters in Colonial Wellington 1845-1860

This tour covers a wide range of aspects of military service of early settlers, of soldiers serving in Wellington, and of their wives and children, and the contributions those with military experience made to the development of the city, to society and to economic development.

It traverses the lower part of the cemetery, includes some of the earliest burials, and is easy walking (not suitable for those with mobility issues).

Tour duration 1.5 hours, starting and ending at the Bolton Street Cemetery Museum, lower Bolton Street.

Cost $10 per person, children under 12 free, and good dogs on leads always welcome.

events.name: Wednesday Lost Wax Casting - 6 Weeks Course
events.venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
events.long_description:
A fantastic course that's full of fun and inspiration!

It starts on Wed 11 November and runs for 6 weeks till Wed 16 December, 5.30pm - 8pm.

Create interesting designs in wax, then send them off to be professionally cast in metal. Once your pieces are back, you will be taught how to cut, file and shape them into wearable pieces.

Level 1 students: Learn to work in both soft and hard jewellers' wax and send your waxes away to be cast. When they return, you will learn how to clean them up into finished jewellery and/or incorporate them into jewellery in multiple ways. We start with rings, but encourage students to think outside the box!

Level 2 students: Advance your carving skills and learn to set stones in your waxes. This can be done either by creating claws and other settings or trying the cast-in-place technique - an organic, exciting process.

Included in the class fee are all your different types of waxes, sandpaper and courier costs.

Not included are the casting and metal costs, which vary from student to student depending on what they want to make. Small castings can cost around $7 - $10, and metals are between $0.35 per gram for bronze - $4 per gram for silver. Please see details on our Regular Classes page.

Our booking system asks for payment to be made via credit card, PayPal or Afterpay on booking. If you do not have access to these payment methods or need to pay your course fee over time, please email us to arrange this ;)

events.id: From Plate to Page: An Evening with Peter Gordon-Samuel Marsden Collegiate School, 35 Marsden Avenue, Karori, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: From Plate to Page: An Evening with Peter Gordon
events.venue: Samuel Marsden Collegiate School, 35 Marsden Avenue, Karori, Wellington
events.long_description:
Peter Gordon is a chef, restaurateur, writer and fusion pioneer whose eclectic cuisine has had global reach. Join us at this special fundraising event for Katherine Mansfield House & Garden to hear about the books, travel, people and experiences that have shaped his life.

For forty years Peter has gathered ingredients, textures and techniques from around the world and brought them to diners at his award-winning restaurants such as The Sugar Club and The Providores, and into homes through his eight cookbooks. He has cooked for world leaders including Queen Elizabeth II and Barack Obama, presented shows for the Discovery Channel and Whakaata Māori (Māori Television), and appeared on the shows of Nigel Slater and Jamie Oliver in the UK and as a guest judge on MasterChef NZ. He is also the founder of the hugely successful UK charity event Who’s Cooking Dinner? and its NZ equivalent Dining for a Difference.

The evening will begin with a glass of Hunter’s Wines’ award-winning MiruMiru™ and delicious canapés in the foyer (a non-alcoholic option will also be available). We will then move into the auditorium for a conversation with Peter hosted by Katherine Mansfield House & Garden Director Cherie Jacobson.

This event is being held to raise funds for our Category 1 Historic Place and writer’s museum in Thorndon, which is open six days a week. We offer an annual programme of events and activities designed to encourage creativity and we host school and tour groups to share the life, literature and legacy of Katherine Mansfield.

events.id: Pukaha After Dark-Pukaha Mount Bruce National Wildlife Centre, 85379 State Highway 2, Mount Bruce, Masterton-Event Finder
events.name: Pukaha After Dark
events.venue: Pukaha Mount Bruce National Wildlife Centre, 85379 State Highway 2, Mount Bruce, Masterton
events.long_description:
As evening settles over the forest, head out along Pūkaha’s Loop Track, normally only accessible during the day, and make your way to the top of the reserve.
Along the way, experience the changing sights and sounds of the ngahere as daylight fades and the forest comes alive at night.

At the top, pause to enjoy a warming kawakawa tea and light snack before beginning the return journey under the night sky.
The experience will also include a short presentation exploring Pūkaha, our connection to the ngahere and the importance of protecting our dark skies.

This is a unique opportunity to experience a different side of Pūkaha and see what happens when the daytime visitors have gone home.

events.venue: Valhalla, Wellington
events.long_description:
Looking for something to do on your Wednesday?

November 11th we've got Adoneye, The Watchers (AUS) and Studio 4 to get you pumped for the weekend to come!

Adoneye hails from the tightly knit music circles of Wellington, New Zealand. Inspired by the raw emotion of grunge rock, like “Soundgarden” and “A Perfect Circle” and the crafted songwriter style of “Elliot Smith. They write with clarity and honesty. Relating an interplay of bittersweet truths and liberating mental alchemy, in an attempt to make sense of the human condition. Emphatically emotive and professionally executed, yet retaining a uniquely human disposition.

The Watchers are a high energy, alternative rock band Kaurna, Adelaide South Australia, known for their loud riffs and signature clownery. They have been drawing crowds with their electric stage presence and their head-banging originals inspired by the legends of rock n roll. Their third single set to be released in November, The Watchers are coming across from Australia to celebrate the release.

Studio 4 are a four piece band from Upper Hutt who love making music together with a variety of influences such as classic rock, indie and jazz. This raw high voltage fusion is a group you'l remember!

We hope to see you all there, this gig is pay what you can!!

events.id: National Dog Database-Venue To be Confirmed | Wellington CBD,Level 5, 111 The Terrace, Wellington, New Zealand-All Events In
events.name: National Dog Database
events.venue: Venue To be Confirmed | Wellington CBD,Level 5, 111 The Terrace, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
National Dog Database
Using the NDD to its full potential. Get hands-on and use realistic scenarios to explore and learn the functionality of the NDD website.

About this Event


Description

The National Dog Database went live 1 May 2006 and provides a countrywide overview of dog control in New Zealand.

It brings great benefits to the animal control industry including the ability to;

track classified owners and dogs
monitor the national infringement count of owners
look up out of district dog and owner details
locate dogs when only limited information is available;
and contribute accurate data to ongoing policy analysis.







Outline

Using the NDD training environment (it looks just like the live NDD system but contains fictional data), the NDD training workshop will explore the following areas:

Background – the history of the NDD project – from 2003 to present
TA Extracts – how information gets from your local system to the NDD and the feedback the NDD will give you as well as the different types of files you can send
Searching – how to get the best out of the search screen and how to interpret the results of your search
The ToDo List – what are errors, warnings, information and system notifications? Detailed discussion about what you need to do with them.
Automated and Manual Linking – National Duplicates – comparing dogs and owners that look similar but are in different districts, and how to manually search for other duplicates.
Security – passwords, adding new users or expiring old accounts, as well as the owner protected status.
Reports – what reports you can run and how to use them in your TA. Did you know there are 18 different kinds of reports that you can generate from the NDD and that you can use some of them to compare your TA’s data to a national summary?







Learning outcomes

With a focus on maintaining data quality, participants in the workshop will learn to use the NDD as a tool for animal control and further understand the importance of administrative roles at the local level. Following the completion of the NDD training workshop, NDD users will have the confidence to use the database to its full potential.







Audience

This course is suitable for managers, team leaders and users with animal control administrator responsibilities.







Prerequisites

To participate in the NDD training workshop you must be a registered user of the National Dog Database (employee or contractor). You are required to bring your own laptop.

events.long_description:
Well Ahead: Put your health on the agenda

An event for women balancing demanding careers, businesses and families, who are already invested in their health and want to understand it more deeply.

As energy, sleep, recovery and body composition shift through midlife, the right information matters.

Well Ahead brings together Dame Susan Devoy and a lineup of experts across health, nutrition, movement and healthy ageing to explore the science and strategy behind:

Energy and recovery

Sleep and stress

Nutrition

Strength and movement

Body composition

Hormonal changes

Perimenopause and menopause

Bone health

Genetics and individual biology

Well Ahead is designed as a connected conversation, not a series of standalone talks.

Each speaker builds on the last, giving you a clearer, more complete picture of your own health rather than a list of disconnected tips.

The day opens with an optional workshop, Your Genes, Your Choices, exploring genetics, DNA testing and the role our genes can play in understanding individual biology. The full programme continues into the afternoon and closes with a live panel and audience Q&A.

Practical information. Expert perspectives. One day, properly invested in your health.

Choose a Morning Workshop pass, Main Event pass, or the Full Pass for the whole day.




Click here to find out more.



“Women spend so much of their lives looking after everyone and everything else. Well Ahead is about putting your own health on the agenda, hearing from people who really know their field, and coming away with information and ideas you can actually use. You don't have to have all the answers. Sometimes you just need to make the time to start asking the right questions.”

- Dame Susan Devoy

Well Ahead is supported by a growing network of organisations across Wellington's business, professional, health, fitness and wellness communities, all helping us bring women together for an important conversation about health through midlife.

About Conquer Health

Conquer Health helps men and women understand their unique biology, so they can focus on what matters to their health today and make informed choices for the years ahead. Rather than one-size-fits-all health advice, Conquer Health combines advanced biological testing with a multidisciplinary clinical team to build a personalised picture of your health, delivered remotely anywhere in New Zealand.

Hosted by EdTechNZ Member  Alsu Sworder from Litmaps, this is an informal event that could formally change the trajectory of your life.

events.long_description:
Life and health insurance: rethinking the model

Customer expectations, product design, underwriting, claims and advice are all moving faster than traditional operating models can keep up with. At the same time, insurers are rethinking traditional products to meet the evolving needs of more New Zealanders, regulatory reform and a tough economic climate. That pressure is pushing insurers to rethink how they're built and to find new ways to support customers in sustainable ways.

Join the InsurTech community in Wellington on 12th November to hear how life and health insurers are innovating.

In the lead up to the launch of Acenda Life in New Zealand in 2027, we’ll hear what has been learned by Asteron Life following their exit from Suncorp and acquisition by Resolution Life Australasia with a further ownership structure to being a member of the Nippon Life Group.  The presentation will further focus on learnings from a digital, data and customer experience perspective.

Then a panel of insurance and insurtech leaders will look at the big issues and trends shaping the sector into 2027. They'll cover how AI is being used in practice today, the opportunities Open Data could open up, and what makes partnerships between insurers and insurtechs work. Hear from Asteron Life, Deloitte, Life Direct, Monvia, Partners Life and Simfuni.

Register now to attend this event and connect with insurance and data professionals. Generously supported by Deloitte and Asteron Life.


Date: 12 November 2026

Time:  5:00PM - 7.00PM

Location: Deloitte's offices, 20 Customhouse Quay.

Event Type: In person

Cost: Free for members of InsurTechNZ & $30 for non-Members

Supported by:

events.long_description:
Photography: Unlocking the Secrets to Captivating Images
Elevate your photography from ordinary to extraordinary and ensure your work stands out in the digital age. Creating captivating photographs and understanding what makes a photograph engaging is something every photographer should master. Camera settings are essential, but once you know them, you need to learn how to take photographs that stir emotions, impact your audience, and leave a lasting impression. After all, isn’t that the true purpose of photography? People don’t want to see the same landscapes or flowers they’ve seen thousands of times. But how do you turn what you love into something that makes people go, "Wow"?
Captivation in photography means stopping a viewer in their tracks, making them look, feel, and connect. It’s about delivering a photograph that enthrals, evokes profound emotions, and shifts perspectives.
In a world brimming with images, only a few have the power to truly captivate and linger in our memories.
 This pioneering course is your gateway to mastering the art of creating captivating photographs at a time when AI-generated images are saturating our visual landscape. Create something genuine and memorable—images that spark curiosity, evoke emotions, and inspire changes in perception. It's time to define your unique style, refine your vision, and make your mark.
 Course Outcomes
 By the end of the course, you’ll be able to: 
Identify the foundational elements that transform an ordinary image into a captivating one.
Create photographs that make people say "Wow" by applying techniques that add a spark of wonder to your shots.
Infuse your photographs with curiosity, making each frame a source of intrigue and interest.
Understand why some images linger in memory and how to make your photographs unforgettable.
Develop a unique style and vision that sets your work apart in the crowded digital landscape.

events.id: Son of Satan or prophet of peace? Hakaraia Mahika and the Tauranga War-National Library of New Zealand, 70 Molesworth Street, Thorndon, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Son of Satan or prophet of peace? Hakaraia Mahika and the Tauranga War
events.venue: National Library of New Zealand, 70 Molesworth Street, Thorndon, Wellington
events.long_description:
In his 1986 book 'The New Zealand Wars and the Victorian interpretation of racial conflict', James Belich noted that the nineteenth-century Bay of Plenty religious and military leader Hakaraia Mahika deserves more attention from historians.

Forty years later, Mark Derby’s forthcoming book 'Warrior Prophet – Hakaraia Mahika and the Tauranga Wars' proposes to provide that attention, along with an interpretive account of the New Zealand Wars in the Bay of Plenty, in which Hakaraia played a prominent and dramatic role.

Mahika was a key figure in the 1864 battle of Gate Pā, regarded by Belich as “arguably the most important battle of the New Zealand Wars.” He became a close and respected associate of Wiremu Tāmihana, Rewi Maniapoto and Te Kooti. Yet, today he is barely remembered outside his own tribal area of Waitaha-Tapuika, near Te Puke.

events.long_description:
‘He Has His Father’s Eyes’: Horror films and Cornelia Parker
Horror has long flickered at the edges of Cornelia Parker’s practice. This talk traces the network of horror references running through this exhibition, exploring how Parker mobilises classics Psycho and Rosemary’s Baby as found cultural objects—laden with symbolic charge, collective memory and anxieties that continue to haunt the present.

Speakers Aaron Lister (Head Curator Art, City Gallery Wellington, and co-curator of Cornelia Parker) and Chelsea Nichols (Senior Curator, The Dowse Art Museum) collaborate as Curator of Screams—an unholy entity dedicated to the twisted entanglements of contemporary art and horror cinema.

The talk will be followed by a screening of Rosemary’s Baby. Wear your best baby blue dress.

Overview

Reconnect with what matters, discover your strengths and learn simple tools to design a life that feels truly yours.

Design a Life You Love




Please try to arrive by 5:45pm so we can get everyone into the event and start on time at 6pm.




So often we go through life doing what is expected of us, without ever questioning why we are doing what we're doing. We chase promotions, juggle family life, and feel pulled in multiple directions at once. In this hands-on workshop, we will spend time reconnecting with what truly matters to us, reflect on our strengths and who we want to become, and use simple tools to decide where we spend our limited time and energy.

Event followed by a plant-based dinner and dessert, all included in your ticket!
Meet your host, Ruth:

Ruth is a lawyer, author, entrepreneur, and still very much figuring it out step-mum. She holds a degree in psychology and a coaching qualification. After burning out at 29, Ruth went travelling and spent some time reconsidering her own life. Out of this she developed the VIP Mindset (Values, Identity, and Priorities). Having found a better balance for herself, Ruth is passionate about supporting people to live with intention, building lives that feel both meaningful and sustainable.

Let go and move freely through music, rhythm and intuitive dance in an evening of expression, connection and release.

Into the Blue: Ecstatic Dance




Please try to arrive by 5:45pm so we can get everyone into the event and start on time at 6pm.




Step onto the dance floor, leave your shoes at the door and let the music guide you. Into the Blue is an evening of movement, freedom, expression and connection, inviting you to let go, move with the rhythm and simply be.

Ecstatic dance offers an opportunity to release stress, move through emotions, quiet the mind and reconnect with the body. Through intuitive movement and a carefully curated soundscape, you’ll be invited to explore presence, creativity and connection, both within yourself and with those around you.




Please stay for a delicious plant-based dinner and dessert afterwards, included in your ticket!

Meet Divya, your host: 



Divya attended her first ecstatic dance a few years ago and will always remember the feeling of pure joy, freedom, and connection it brought. During that experience, she felt inspired to one day host her own ecstatic dance. Having explored the world of DJing, she was drawn to creating a more intentional space where people could express themselves through movement and music.

Over the past year, dance has become an important practice for helping her process emotions, stay present, and reconnect with herself. She is excited to share a carefully curated journey of music, blending uplifting rhythms, grounding beats, and at times bass-heavy sounds that invite people to move, explore, and enjoy the experience in their own way.

events.id: Powell Hut Overnight Tramp-Tararua Forest Park, Mt. Holdsworth Rd, Carterton-Event Finder
events.name: Powell Hut Overnight Tramp
events.venue: Tararua Forest Park, Mt. Holdsworth Rd, Carterton
events.long_description:
Join the Wairarapa Walking Festival on this classic and epic tramp to Powell Hut.

The first day: we will walk from Mt Holdsworth car park up to Powell Hut. This is 5 to 6 hours of uphill tramping, with good tracks and steps. The hut is at the edge of the bush-line with glorious views (and cell phone access).

Powell Hut has (gas) stoves, a wood-burner and bunks with mattresses. There are long-drop toilets and a water tank collecting water from the roof.

The Wairarapa Walking Festival team have booked 20 bunks for this great adventure.

Bring water for the tramp, snacks (muesli bars, dried fruit, nuts, chocolate etc), picnic lunch for both days, dinner and breakfast, plus hot chocolate, tea or coffee. Also, basic toiletries, hut shoes, nightwear, sleeping bags and recommend earplugs.

The second day: depending on the group and the weather we will either return the same way of go onto the alpine tops, look at the alpine flowers and comeback down East Holdsworth track. We should be back at the car park by 3 or 4pm.

Essential to have tramping boots or solid walking shoes, wind and rainproof jackets and merino or fleece layers. A change of clothes to wear in the hut in case you get wet on the walk. Walking poles recommended if you have them.

D.O.C labels this walk an 'intermediate tramping track'. The car park is at 320m elevation and Powell Hut is at 1200m elevation.

Please note - once registered, you will be asked to provide Emergency Contact details of a friend / relative and whether you have been tramping in the last 6 months. The Walk coordinator for WWF will carry a PLB. There is good cell phone coverage from the Hut.

Ticket costs are only to cover bunk costs at hut. Tickets will go off-sale 2 days prior to enable logistics, check the weather for the trip.

Youth between ages of 12 - 16 require an accompanying adult to attend also.

Celia recommends downloading the free iNaturalist app before you go.

events.long_description:
Overview

Think big! Explore bold ideas, fresh thinking and what makes us human, at Massey's hands-on day celebrating humanities and social sciences.

The Big Think is a festival of ideas for high school students, hosted by the College of Humanities and Social Sciences at Te Kunenga ki Pūrehuroa Massey University. Together, we'll explore how making sense of the world is a human and social thing.

Across all three Massey campuses this November, staff, students and graduates will share how the humanities and social sciences help us to understand what it means to be human, to live with others, and to act with care and purpose in a fast-moving, technology-infused, and often demanding world.

From communication and media to psychology, philosophy, planning, ethics, creative writing, emergency management, and even what we can learn about today’s world from history and classics, The Big Think shows how human-centred thinking helps us navigate change, make better decisions, and thrive in contemporary society.

You'll meet Humanities and Social Sciences staff, graduates and current students who will share their study and career journeys. Then, you'll get to have a go yourself, in a wide range of interactive workshops, from broadcast journalism skills to beta-testing a new psychology-based game to hacking the gaps in Wikipedia.

The skills that will future-proof you are human: come discover yours with us.

Read less

events.name: This Is Grief: On the Road
events.venue: Unity Books, 57 Willis St, Wellington
events.long_description:
Grief is part of being human, but we still struggle to talk about it.
This Is Grief: On the Road is a free community event bringing honest conversations about grief, loss, love and the life that continues around them into communities across Aotearoa.

Join author and This Is Grief founder Kirsten O'Connor for a relaxed, human conversation about what grief really looks like, beyond the clichés, timelines and expectations we so often place around it. Kirsten will share from her own experience of grief and from her work writing and talking about loss, before opening the space for conversation and connection.

You don't need to have the right words. You don't need to share anything you don't want to. This is a space for anyone living with loss, or anyone who wants to better understand and support someone who is.

Come along, listen, talk if you'd like to, and be part of a conversation we don't have nearly often enough.

This is a free community event. Registration is recommended as places may be limited.

events.name: "Sitting Pretty" at Ata Rangi
events.venue: Ata Rangi Winery, 14 Puruatanga Rd, Martinborough
events.long_description:
Remember the original Toast Martinborough? Multiple vineyard visits, beautiful wines, and those long, progressive lunches that became part of the tradition? At Ata Rangi, we’re bringing a little of that magic back for one special evening.

Join us for Sitting Pretty - a sunset session celebrating Ata Rangi’s place in the old Toast Martinborough story, when our site was a stop on the festival circuit and Ruth Pretty’s much-loved food was part of the experience.

In collaboration with Rose & Smith, we’re revisiting some favourite dishes from Ruth Pretty’s menus of years gone by. Think whitebait fritters, asparagus with hollandaise, long-stemmed chocolate dipped strawberries, white crockery, linen napkins, cutlery, and the pleasure of taking your time over good food and a glass or two of Ata Rangi wine. It’s a nod to the familiar flavours and fond memories of yesteryear, and a good reason to make a few new ones.

Settle in amongst the vines, as the afternoon gives way to evening, with a relaxed yet festive atmosphere. Enjoy Ata Rangi wines, delicious food, great company and live music from Pat For President.

Whether you’re joining us to revisit a piece of the Toast Martinborough of old, or simply looking for a fun way to kick start the weekend ahead of Toast Martinborough (at The Runholder the following day), Sitting Pretty is an invitation to relax, raise a glass and celebrate where it all began.

Event details

Friday 13 November 2026
4pm–8pm
Ata Rangi, 14 Puruatanga Road, Martinborough

events.description:
Multiple vineyard visits, beautiful wines, and those long, progressive lunches that became part of the tradition?
At Ata Rangi, we’re bringing a little of that magic back for one special evening.
Join us for Sitting Pretty - a sunset session celebrating Ata Rangi’s place in the old Toast Martinborough story, when our site was a stop on the festival circuit and Ruth Pretty’s much-loved food was part of the experience.
Think whitebait fritters, asparagus with hollandaise, long-stemmed chocolate dipped strawberries, white crockery, linen napkins, cutlery, and the pleasure of taking your time over good food and a glass or two of Ata Rangi wine.

events.name: This Is Grief: On the Road
events.venue: Martinborough Books & Post, 6 Kitchener Street, Martinborough 5711, Martinborough
events.long_description:
Grief is part of being human, but we still struggle to talk about it.

This Is Grief: On the Road is a free community event bringing honest conversations about grief, loss, love and the life that continues around them into communities across Aotearoa.

Join author and This Is Grief founder Kirsten O'Connor for a relaxed, human conversation about what grief really looks like, beyond the clichés, timelines and expectations we so often place around it. Kirsten will share from her own experience of grief and from her work writing and talking about loss, before opening the space for conversation and connection.

You don't need to have the right words. You don't need to share anything you don't want to. This is a space for anyone living with loss, or anyone who wants to better understand and support someone who is.

Come along, listen, talk if you'd like to, and be part of a conversation we don't have nearly often enough.

This is a free community event. Registration is recommended as places may be limited.

events.name: Lost Wax in Three - Ring-making on Friday Nights!
events.venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
events.long_description:
Over three sessions, create your own unique ring using the age-old lost wax technique. This is a great opportunity to spend a Friday night getting creative and making something you can wear!

In weeks one and two, you will learn how to work with jeweller’s hard wax to design and shape your own ring. Experiment with texture, form and detail to create a one-of-a-kind piece. Your finished wax ring will then be sent away for casting in the metal of your choice.

There will be a week’s break before the third session to allow time for everyone’s waxes to be cast. In the final session, you’ll learn how to trim, clean and finish your cast, transforming your wax design into an original ring ready to wear.

More advanced students can use the sessions to develop their own ring designs in a supportive class setting.

Included in the class fee are all your different types of waxes, sandpaper and courier costs.

Casting and metal costs are not included and will vary depending on the size of your ring and the metal you choose. Small castings can cost around $6.65–$12, with metal costing approximately $7–$30 depending on whether you choose red bronze, white bronze or silver.

This class is suitable for teens and children aged 12 and over. Anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

events.id: A Wartime Evening at the RSA-Featherston Memorial RSA, 57 Fox St, Featherston-Event Finder
events.name: A Wartime Evening at the RSA
events.venue: Featherston Memorial RSA, 57 Fox St, Featherston
events.long_description:
Experience an evening of wartime food, music and memories at the Featherston RSA, celebrating the stories and spirit of the World War II era. Your evening will be themed around a warrant officers’ and senior NCOs’ mess dinner evening, from within a Second World War air raid shelter. As you eat your meal, your narrator will take you through the years of World War II, from the invasion of Poland and the miracle of Dunkirk, to the Pacific and Monte Cassino, all the way through to VE and VJ Day, plus much more in between.

The food will be loosely based on the type of fare people ate during the years of rationing - think potted meat, bangers and mash, and stewed apples.
Your meal will be slightly different though. Instead of potted meat, you’ll have a delicious pate, accompanied with melba toast and a cherry relish. This will be followed by exquisite gourmet sausages from Greytown Butcher, served with delicious creamed potatoes, peas, and onion gravy. Dessert will be a delectable apple pie, served with a sumptuous vanilla custard. The meal will be rounded off with cheese and biscuits.
You are highly encouraged to wear 1940s attire or military uniform, with a prize for best dressed man and best dressed woman.

Tickets available from EventFinda and the Featherston Memorial RSA - fstnrsaevents@gmail.com

events.long_description:
Enigma - Wellington
NZSO Artistic Advisor and Principal Conductor Gemma New with legendary pianist Sir Stephen Hough present a concert of charm, mystery and bold vision.

Programme:
Ross Harris Concerto for Orchestra (World Premiere)
Saint-Saëns Piano Concerto No. 5 Egyptian
Elgar Enigma Variations

Edward Elgar’s greatest masterpiece remains swathed in mystery.

His Enigma Variations, a set of 14 variations on a theme you never actually hear, has been the subject of both intense scrutiny and great love, thanks to the compositional genius and throbbing heart pulsing in these compelling variations.

Similarly, Saint-Saëns’ Fifth Piano Concerto has beguiled audiences with its Eastern-inspired sounds — hence its Egyptian nickname. To weave his own spell on us, legendary pianist Sir Stephen Hough returns to our shores. Praised by Limelight for possessing “an other-worldly stillness and strength [and] the perfect technique combined with the utmost poetic fluency”, Hough promises to transport us to another world.

We proudly premiere Ross Harris’ Concerto for Orchestra. A four-time winner of the SOUNZ Contemporary Award, Harris’ artistry and bold vision electrifies this newly commissioned work, driving the orchestra to new heights.

events.name: Sulfate - Live at Meow - And It Wants Album Release Tour
events.venue: Meow,9 Edward Street, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Sulfate - Live at Meow - And It Wants Album Release Tour
Feral, devolved and running on instinct, the six songs on Sulfate’s third album ‘And It Wants’ grapple between David Harris unleashing on his drum kit, Zac Arnold conjuring fuzz and feedback and Peter Ruddell’s taut, wiry guitar-work and commanding baritone. Written and recorded in New Lynn’s industrial area, this new batch of songs were created on a diet of Cormac McCarthy novels, Adam Curtis documentaries and the madness of gothic horror. Since recording, Sulfate's line up has expanded once more, introducing multi-instrumentalist Louisa Nicklin to the band's inexorable live performances.

Sonically, Sulfate set out some parameters at the outset of the album recordings - and it was important for things to sound real. The band wanted real instruments to be played, and, importantly, sound like they’re being played, by real, living people. This was a conscious reaction to the modern, online, perfect-existence, social media-ness of it all. Audio engineer Emily Wheatcroft-Snape was recommended to the band because of her ability to capture sounds with accuracy and precision - and she encapsulated the live band just as they had hoped.

Thematically, ‘And It Wants’ sees Ruddell clinging to optimism and joy while being subject to the existential nihilism of our current hypernormal, western reality. “Death is all through this record. The songs were born out of the feeling that there are no rules, that nothing matters, and that we all die. That we dance around the fact that death comes for us all, but we never really, truly, acknowledge it - it’s just too big or too heavy to have any kind of impact on our day to day existence. The intent is to provide a sonic backdrop to dance ecstatically, liberated, as the world around you burns. Find comfort and joy in things while you can, even as the end draws near and darkness begins to ruminate.”

‘And It Wants’ is out digitally, and on two exclusive vinyl variants via Flying Nun Records and Holiday Records on October 23rd.

events.name: Walk in the Dark Carterton
events.venue: Carterton Golf Club, Chester Road, Carterton
events.long_description:
This Walk in the Dark is held at the Carterton Golf Course.

Step into the beauty of the night with this unique offering for the Wairarapa Walking Festival. Hosted on the manicured grounds of a local golf course, this gentle evening stroll allows you to experience the magic of darkness without worrying about uneven paddocks or rough terrain.

As we walk together, the transition from dusk to dark will naturally unfold, helping us acclimatise to the night. For those new to walking in the dark, handy red-light torches will be provided to keep you comfortable. This is less about distance and more about slowing down, stepping slightly outside of your comfort zone, and embracing the calm of night.

Along the way, we’ll reflect on the value of darkness - its role in history, its impact on wellbeing, and its importance for the environment. We’ll then pause to share hot chocolate and, if the skies are clear, look up in awe at a canopy of stars. With star charts in hand, we’ll explore what the November night skies have to offer and why protecting them matters.

The evening concludes with simple, practical ways we can all help preserve our night skies - because our environment doesn’t end at the treetops, it stretches all the way to the stars.

events.long_description:
WELCOME SPACE BROTHERS is a documentary that dives into the extraordinary true story of the Unarius Academy of Science, an extraterrestrial-channeling spiritual school founded in El Cajon in the 1970s. Led by the dazzlingly outlandish Ruth E. Norman—revered as "Archangel Uriel"—Unarius evolved into a wildly inventive public-access television phenomenon. The group produced films that appeared to be elaborately campy space epics yet were, at their core, sincere therapeutic works. 

From The Source Family director Jodi Wille comes another mind-expanding voyage into the wild frontiers of American belief, bringing her singular blend of empathy, humor, and emotional insight to one of the country's most fascinating outsider communities. Produced by Caryn Capotosto (Won’t You Be My Neighbor) and Jodi Wille. Executive producers include Elijah Wood, Moby, and Oscar-winning filmmakers Phil Lord and Christopher Miller.

Please join us for the Wellington screening of WELCOME SPACE BROTHERS - brought to you by Erika Grant and Night Church Cinema. This is a dress up event - come dressed in your favorite UFO/Cult fit. There will be prizes for best dressed, and DJ's Oona Verse and Martyn Pepperell plus others will guide us into the wild starry night with space cult inspired dance tracks.

The bar and restaurant will be open for dinner and drinks. This is a one off event, not to be missed!!

“Wild and Very Trippy” - Jodi Wille

“If I didn’t know Jodi Wille’s film, Welcome Space Brothers, was a documentary, I’d swear it was a WTF, insane, sci-fi tale of weirdness. The story of Ruth is fascinating…..” - Alan NG, Film Threat 

“It’s a vision of healing, acceptance, peace, cooperation, and hope, expressed through an outpouring of unbridled creative energy. If that spells crazy, beam me up!” — Doug Harvey, Artillery

events.long_description:
Raurimu Thunder
Mainline Steam Heritage Trust is embarking on our biggest trip of the year. Modern diesel trains cover this route daily without a second thought, but we are doing something entirely different. We are throwing out the modern dampening, bypassing the mundane, and tackling New Zealand's greatest rail challenge the way it was meant to be conquered: with raw, untamed steam power.

Raurimu Thunder puts you trackside and onboard as our heavy heritage steam locomotive charges into the rugged heart of the North Island to take on the legendary Raurimu Spiral. This is a full day, high horsepower assault on a brutal mountain grade. No filters, no computer assists—just pure, unfiltered vintage engineering working at the absolute limit.

Relax in climate controlled comfort or head to the open air viewing platform to hear and see our heritage steam locomotive charge across dramatic landscapes and tackle the country's most legendary railway challenge. Large panoramic windows frame the unfolding wilderness, ensuring you enjoy every moment of the giant climb in absolute comfort, no matter the unpredictable Central Plateau weather.

How Your Day Flows:
The Scenic Approach: Settle into our premium carriages at your local station as the whistle blows and the journey begins. We steam smoothly through rolling rural valleys toward the base of the Central Plateau. Indulge in fresh barista coffee, artisan snacks, or a local craft beer from the fully stocked cafe carriage as the excitement builds.

Conquering the Spiral: Feel the earth shake as our locomotive battles the 1 in 50 grade of the world famous Raurimu Spiral. This 1898 engineering masterpiece overcomes a massive 139 metre vertical rise through a brilliant layout of horseshoe curves, deep tunnels, and a complete 360 degree loop. Experience the tight, coiling geometry firsthand from the outdoor platform, where you can practically see the front of the train loop right over the back.

The Trackside Photo Runby: Step off the train directly onto the rugged track ballast for the ultimate adventure highlight. Clear your camera lenses and find your vantage point along the tracks. Feel the anticipation build as the massive steam locomotive sets back out of sight, then marvel at the raw power as it charges back up the spiral for an unforgettable, full steam display.

The Atmospheric Return: Board your assigned premium carriage at the summit for a cozy, relaxing journey home. Swap stories with fellow travellers and enjoy a premium glass of regional wine from the salon bar as the train rolls comfortably into the night, concluding an epic day of New Zealand rail history.

Silver Star Dinner Service

As the day draws to a close and the train settles into its evening journey home, make the most of the experience with our Silver Star Dinner Service.

For $26.99 per meal, enjoy a freshly prepared dinner from Hungry Rush Ohakune, served during the return journey. It’s the perfect way to relax after a day of steam, scenery and adventure.

Choose your preferred dinner option when you book, with your selection made and paid for conveniently during checkout.

Your Dinner Choices:

The Wingman
Tender smoked chicken wings, marinated in chipotle buttermilk and served with crispy fries and a smoky hickory cola BBQ sauce.

The Burger & Fries
A juicy New Zealand beef burger with American cheese, grilled onions, pickles and house burger sauce, served in a fresh milk bun with crispy fries.

Fish & Chips
Fresh East Coast tarakihi in a light, crispy batter, served with golden fries, minted peas, fresh lemon and a house-made dipping sauce.

The No Meat Burger & Fries — Vegetarian
A delicious vegetarian burger featuring a seasoned vegetable patty with Swiss cheese, grilled onions, seasonal sauce and vegetable pickles, served in a fresh milk bun with crispy fries.

The Silver Star Dinner Service is completely optional and is not included in the standard ticket price. Dinner can be added to your booking during checkout for $26.99 per meal.

Timetable
Please note that the timetable below is provisional and may be subject to change pending final approval from KiwiRail. While we aim to operate to the times shown, departure and arrival times may be adjusted as operational planning is finalised.

events.long_description:
The Old Mill Track is an up and back route that runs from the Haurangi Road end to the west branch headwaters of the Tūranganui River (return).
It is approximately 4km one way (8km return), and follows a recently maintained tramping track that runs through regenerating native forest in the Aorangi Forest Park.

Transport will be provided by bus from the Martinborough town square to the Department of Conservation's Waikuku Lodge, where the walk will begin. (No access to Lodge)
Walkers will be delivered back to Martinborough town square at the end of the day.

This walk is suitable for fit trampers, with approximately 4 hours of tramping with the terrain including moderate hills to climb both up and down.

events.id: Kuratawhiti Heritage Loop-Greytown, Kuratawhiti Street, Greytown-Event Finder
events.name: Kuratawhiti Heritage Loop
events.venue: Greytown, Kuratawhiti Street, Greytown
events.long_description:
Kuratawhiti Street stretches between urban and rural settings and this guided walk will pause briefly at the boundaries at a number of significant buildings.
The walk skirts churches, parks, memorials and settler houses. Volunteers from the Greytown Heritage Trust will share histories and insights along the way.
At midpoint in the walk we will pause for coffee and pastries at Stable - a cafe set in a countryside garden. The last stretch of the walk is entirely rural, briefly touches the Waiohine and returns by a walking track formed from an unmade road. Against a backdrop of the distant Tararuas, we face expansive views across a farming landscape towards the eastern hills.

Participants will need sturdy walk shoes or sneakers with good tread.

The ticket price for this event includes a $10 donation to the Greytown Heritage Trust to develop their digital guide and $20 for a fabulous morning tea at Stable Cafe.

events.id: One Day Secular Meditation Retreat in Wellington-31 Lawson Place, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
events.name: One Day Secular Meditation Retreat in Wellington
events.venue: 31 Lawson Place, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
We know from ancient wisdom and modern psychology that meditation brings many benefits for our mental and physical wellbeing. It can reduce worry and pain, and improve calmness, focus, sleep, relationships and life satisfaction. The more time we spend meditating, and the more skilled we become, the greater the benefits.

So take a restorative break from your daily life, meet other meditators, and strengthen your practice at this small-group Sunday retreat. Everyone is welcome, whatever their level of meditation experience or preferred style. The retreat is beginner-friendly, and our approach is secular (meaning non-religious) which makes room for diverse beliefs.

The programme

We will begin with introductions, followed by a guided meditation that covers the core skills of both sitting and walking meditation. For the rest of the day, the meditation will be unguided apart from occasional bells to announce breaks, and to remind you to alternate between sitting and walking (if that's what you choose to do).

To help quieten the mind, many participants prefer not to talk again until the discussion circle at the end of the retreat. However some people like to chat with others during the breaks, and there is space allocated for this. The retreat leaders are always available for quiet conversations if you need support with your practice.

The venue

The Innermost Gardens hall is nestled between the central city suburb of Mount Victoria and the green town belt. This provides a peaceful nature-rich setting for the retreat, surrounded by community gardens to enjoy during the breaks or walking meditation.

There will be hot drinks and snacks available throughout the day. For lunch the participants bring a plate of vegetarian food to share. The venue has a full kitchen including cutlery, plates, bowls, fridge, stove, and a microwave.

The leaders

Bryan Royds is an adult educator and registered counsellor with a passion for wellbeing science and leadership development. He has been meditating and teaching meditation skills in groups for many years, including the well-researched methods of Mindfulness Based Stress Reduction (MBSR).

Sarah Jane Barnett is a writer and creative writing teacher at Massey University. She has been a Buddhist for ten years, practicing mostly Vipassana meditation. She also co-facilitates a meditation group for people who practice Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (an evidence-based modern psychotherapy and wellbeing method).

The registration fee is only $40 for waged and $20 for unwaged, fully refundable until one day prior.

events.id: Get the Job: STARR Interview Technique And Preparation-Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki St, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Get the Job: STARR Interview Technique And Preparation
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki St, Wellington
events.long_description:
Get the best results in job interviews. Learn how to approach behavioural questions and impress the interview panel. Ace interviews using the potent Starr method. Use it to your advantage by answering competency focused questions with winning replies.

Meet the demand for excellence in the job market head on. Learn how to utilise the Starr technique in the way that recruiters use it. That is, to define and seek out the skills and qualities of the best candidate. Master the Starr skills and feel confident in your next job interview.

Familarise yourself with the skills needed to ace your next interview. Learn the STARR method as an approach to responding to behavioural based questions. Understand how to use concrete examples from your life as proof that you possess the experience and skills for the job you are applying for. You’ll develop the key interview skill of being able to share your accomplishments through real-life examples.

In this course, you are taught how to identify specific example situations that are unique to you. You’ll learn how to confidently talk about the tasks involved and describe how you completed the key task and met its challenges. We’ll also consider the context of jobs you are interviewing for and how to choose examples that best show the desired skills interviewers are seeking.

By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:

Develop a higher level of confidence in approaching job interviews.
Identify the different components of the STARR acronym and apply them to the job interview context.
Identify what behavioural based questions are and why recruiters use them.
Successfully answer behavioural based interview questions by applying the STARR technique.
Develop skills in using real life examples to show transferable skills in the workplace.

Note: You must be a NZ citizen or resident to qualify for the free course fee option.  A condition of enrolment is that you must provide photo ID when you attend.

events.id: The Digital Minefield: AI, Misinformation, and Detox-Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington-Wellington High School
events.name: The Digital Minefield: AI, Misinformation, and Detox
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.

If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.

Together, workshop participants will demystify how artificial intelligence actually works, acknowledge some of the harms of this new technology, learn about the characteristics of mis/disinformation, build resilience against fake news, and explore why our brains weren’t built for the infinite scroll. You will walk away from the workshop with a better understanding of the hidden forces shaping your screen, equipped with real-world tools to cut through the digital noise.
 
Dr. Andrew Chen is a leading New Zealand specialist at the intersection of digital technology ethics and public policy. With a PhD from the University of Auckland in Computer Systems Engineering, Andrew brings a deep technical understanding and applies it towards systemic issues and interventions. With extensive experience advising public agencies and private companies on governing emerging technologies, Dr. Chen translates complex technical concepts into clear, accessible insights for the community. He is passionate about helping people understand technology's societal impacts, and thinking more deeply about what’s happening behind the scenes, so we can all navigate today’s complex digital landscape.
 
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.venue: Green Jersey Explorer Tours, 16 Kitchener Street, Martinborough, Martinborough
events.long_description:
Born from the shared vision of the Ruamāhanga Farm Foundation, Green Jersey Cycle Tours, Hau Ariki Marae, and the Aorangi Restoration Trust, this experience offers a meaningful way to connect and contribute to the natural world. We weave conservation, culture, arts and science into an immersive journey.

You will go off the beaten track and step into little known pockets of wildlife, meeting the people who are actively restoring them. At Ruamāhanga Farm, you will get hands-on with the restoration work yourself. At the lake along with the sounds of the night you will hear stories and original songs born directly from this landscape through our Te Reo o te Wai project. Beside the awa and in the heart of the bush, there will be guided space to slow down, reflect, and explore your own creativity.

events.name: Anzac Hall Complex Tours
events.venue: Featherston Anzac Hall, 62 Bell St, Featherston
events.long_description:
Tour this historically significant complex, built during World War I to provide recreation and hospitality for soldiers training at Featherston Military Camp.

Enjoy a fascinating guided tour of the historically significant Anzac Hall. The hall was first opened in 1916 as a recreation centre for the troops at the nearby Featherston military camp, with the families of the first European settlers donating the funds. The building was used as a hospital during the influenza epidemic of 1918-19. It is a Category One Historic Place. Be at the hall’s main entrance ten minutes before each tour starts.

events.id: Botanical Blues - Photographic cyanotype-Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Botanical Blues - Photographic cyanotype
events.venue: Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington
events.long_description:
In this workshop, you’ll discover the beautiful 19th-century photographic process of the cyanotype (often called a blueprint), known for its striking Prussian blue tones. In its earliest form, the cyanotype was used to record botanical specimens.

During our workshop, you’ll collect plants or foliage from the garden (or bring your own) to create delicate contact prints, OR you can create stencils for abstract designs. We’ll coat Japanese rice paper with light-sensitive chemistry, expose your designs in the sunlight, and develop them. We’ll also cut a matt board for your favourite final print. You can bring your own papers to test printing on, but they must be non-coated (able to absorb chemistry) and wet-strength.

All materials included.

Thirty minute lunch - bring a packed lunch to have in our historic home or explore the local cafes in Te Aro.

events.venue: Hāpua farm, 1094 Masterton Castlepoint Rd, Tauweru, Masterton
events.long_description:
Discover the beauty of Hāpua Farm, a property that combines rolling farmland with wetlands, native bush, and sweeping views of the surrounding hill country.
Led by Michael Birch, the walk begins on the farm’s airstrip, offering beautiful views of the Tararua Ranges before descending through farm tracks, open paddocks, and bush trails.

Along the way, explore wetlands created by large landslides 11,000–12,000 years ago, and continue east to two protected QEII covenant areas of native bush.
Here, you’ll encounter towering totara, matai, and kahikatea, as well as abundant birdlife including kererū and tūī.
Last year's participants had rave reviews of this walk!

Note: the terrain is a mixture of moderate and steep hills, including rough ground and bush tracks. You will need to climb over fences using stiles.

events.name: Think Better, Live Better
events.venue:
Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui Central Library
Wellington, Wellington
events.long_description:
Overview

Your mind is powerful but is it working for you? Join us for 5 practical tools that change how you think, feel and live every day.

Think Better, Live Better

A 2-hour workshop that changes how you think

Most of us have never been taught how to think. We've learned what to think - at school, at work, through experience. But the actual process running in the background? The stories we tell ourselves, the patterns we fall into, the way we focus our attention, nobody really teaches that.

This workshop does.

Think Better, Live Better is a practical, engaging two-hour session grounded in real psychology and delivered in plain English. No jargon, no theory for theory's sake, and no forced positivity. Just five powerful tools you can start using the same day.

What you'll learn

Tool 1 — Change the story: Your brain defaults to the worst interpretation of any situation. Learn to catch that automatic story, question it, and replace it with a more accurate and useful one. This single shift reduces anxiety and improves decisions you make under pressure.

Tool 2 — Watch your own mind: Most of us are so inside our thoughts we never stop to look at them. This tool teaches you to step back and notice your own thinking patterns - the loops, the traps, the habits, without being swept along by them. Once you can name a pattern, you're no longer ruled by it.

Tool 3 — Get curious about what goes wrong: We've been taught to treat failure as evidence that something is wrong with us. This tool flips that. Learn to approach setbacks with curiosity rather than self-judgement, seeing the lesson, adjusting the approach, and moving forward with more confidence.

Tool 4 — Choose where your mind goes: Your brain is wired to scan for what's wrong three times more than it notices what's right. That's not a character flaw, it's biology. This tool teaches you to train your attention deliberately, so you're not at the mercy of stress, habit, and fear.

Tool 5 — Stop wrestling with your thoughts: Some thoughts don't need to be believed or fought, they just need to be noticed and let go. This tool gives you a simple, usable technique to unhook from the thoughts that hold you back, without trying to think them away.

What to expect

This is an interactive, conversational workshop, not a lecture. Expect real examples, honest discussion, a bit of laughter, and moments of reflection. Every participant receives a personal workbook to use during the session and take home, so you leave with something practical in your hands, not just in your head.

You'll finish the two hours with a complete inner toolkit and one clear commitment to yourself about how you'll use it.

This workshop is for you if:

you find yourself stuck in worry, self-doubt, or overthinking
you want to respond to pressure and setbacks more confidently
you're ready to have more control over how you think and feel
you're curious about how your mind works and ways to optimise it.

Workshop details

Duration: 2 hours Includes: Personal workbook Group size: Intimate - maximum 12 participants Location: Wellington CBD

Come ready to be honest, curious, and a little bit surprised by what's possible.

Grief is part of being human, but we still struggle to talk about it.
This Is Grief: On the Road is a free community event bringing honest conversations about grief, loss, love and the life that continues around them into communities across Aotearoa.

Join author and This Is Grief founder Kirsten O'Connor for a relaxed, human conversation about what grief really looks like, beyond the clichés, timelines and expectations we so often place around it. Kirsten will share from her own experience of grief and from her work writing and talking about loss, before opening the space for conversation and connection.

You don't need to have the right words. You don't need to share anything you don't want to. This is a space for anyone living with loss, or anyone who wants to better understand and support someone who is.

Come along, listen, talk if you'd like to, and be part of a conversation we don't have nearly often enough.

Renowned historians Chris Pugsley and Buddy Mikaere, with local historian Neil Frances, explore New Zealand’s costly experience at Monte Cassino, including the stories of local men who took part.

FAQ’S

🗣️ Why do the tickets come in different price tiers?

Whilst there is no physical difference. There is only a limited amount of tickets we can sell. Therefore we operate a festival style ticketing model. The earlier you buy your ticket the cheaper it will be.

Yes, we offer a discounted ticket price for groups of 10 or more. These tickets can be found listed as the “Big Group Package!” above, orders for these tickets are restricted to a minimum of 10.

Once this event is sold out, there will not be any additional tickets released. In addition to this we will be unable to sell them at the door due to maximum capacity and health and safety regulations.

Our events take place at a variety of locations across the UK and Ireland. As each varies please ensure to check the specific venue's website for accessibility information.

Yes, if you are unable to attend an event you are welcome to sell your tickets on. We do not use names on tickets as a condition for entry.

GUARANTED TO SHIFT MORE THAT JUST AWARENESS ALONE.

events.long_description:
Create your own ring stack from copper, brass, and sterling silver in this fun and rewarding jewellery workshop.

Guided by experienced and supportive tutors, you’ll be introduced to the fundamental skills of jewellery making while creating a small collection of rings to take home.

During this 3-hour class, you’ll learn how to measure your finger, cut metal to size, and add textures and patterns using hammers and punches. You’ll also be shown how to solder your rings with a jeweller’s torch, before finishing them with filing, sanding, and polishing techniques.

By the end of the session, you’ll have crafted a thick sterling silver ring and a stack of copper or brass rings, including two plain round wires to texture as you like, and a choice of decorative brass pearl wire or square wire.

This class is ideal for beginners, groups of friends, or visitors wanting a memorable creative experience. Many students find jewellery making a mindful activity, offering a chance to slow down, work with their hands, and enjoy the rhythm of making.

The class fee includes all materials and consumables, such as solder, sandpaper, and polishing materials. Extra silver and other metals will be available for purchase in the studio for those who would like to expand their collection or upgrade one of their brass or copper wires to a second silver one.

Children aged 12 and over are welcome. Anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

events.id: Darren Watson Plays The Shed-46a Victoria Street, Alicetown, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand-Humanitix
events.name: Darren Watson Plays The Shed
events.venue: 46a Victoria Street, Alicetown, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Much-loved Pōneke blues and roots singer-songwriter Darren Watson is returning to his favourite Lower Hutt intimate venue, The Shed for the third time (with special guest Matt Hay).

For this visit the ex-Chicago Smoke Shop leader, ‘Planet Key’ songwriter, and multiple NZ Music Award nominee is bringing his musical compardre Matt Hay along to both open the show and accompany Watson on harmonica.

Watson’s latest album ‘Darren Watson sings John Hiatt’ was released just over a year ago to critical acclaim, including a 4-star review in US jazz and blues ‘bible’ Downbeat, and spectacular NZ chart success.

Opener Matt Hay’s latest album ‘Dog and Pony Show’ (produced by Watson) was judged ‘Best Americana Album’ at the 2024 Aotearoa NZ Folk Alliance Awards.

“ Matt brings his beautiful songs to open the show and then joins me blowing some beautiful, tasteful harp. I’m really enjoying playing with Matt again.”

Darren says this show, while still featuring a few choice Hiatt covers, will feature more of his own material old and new.

“ I’ve got some new things on the boil, and I’m really enjoying exploring my back catalogue. There’s a surprising amount of songs after forty odd years!.”

For the uninitiated, a Darren Watson show is big on dynamics, foot stomping blues grooves, and emotional pin-drop moments. There’s politics aplenty, and an awful lot of self-deprecating humour.

Watson is well-known as a powerful guitarist but what many people only realise once they hear him live is he can really sing.

Doors open 7pm for a 7.30pm start.

events.long_description:
Acclaimed indie band Flyte bring their signature blend of heartfelt lyricism and melodic craftsmanship to a special run of New Zealand shows this November.

Flyte have earned widespread acclaim for their refined songwriting and emotionally resonant sound, with a catalogue that showcases their evolution from classic British guitar pop to more expansive and introspective arrangements. Their releases have been celebrated for their lyrical honesty and rich harmonies, cementing their place as one of the UK’s most compelling contemporary bands.

Formed in London, Flyte are led by singer-songwriters Will Taylor and Nick Hill, whose close creative partnership underpins the band’s distinctive identity. They broke through with their debut album The Loved Ones and continued to build momentum with subsequent records, including This Is Really Going to Hurt and Flyte, earning praise for their timeless influences and modern sensibility. Their work captures themes of love, vulnerability and connection, delivered with a stripped-back elegance and attention to detail that has resonated with audiences worldwide.
For audiences in Aotearoa, these shows offer a rare opportunity to experience Flyte’s intimate and immersive live performance, bringing their finely crafted songs to life with warmth, precision and emotional depth.

events.long_description:
OFFICIAL SELECTION: Venice Film Festival -
OFFICIAL SELECTION: Telluride Film Festival -
OFFICIAL SELECTION: Toronto International Film Festival -

The latest film from British cinema royalty Danny Boyle (Trainspotting, Slumdog Millionaire), Ink charts the rise of Rupert Murdoch’s notorious newspaper The Sun, and the creation of the UK’s tabloid culture.

Guy Pearce (The Brutalist) stars as Murdoch, alongside Jack O’Connell (Sinners) as newspaper editor Larry Lamb, newly assigned to oversee the fledgling daily paper. Tasked with attracting new readers in the competitive British media market, Lamb devises a new tactic - throw anything onto the page that will turn heads, no matter the veracity.

The Sun sees a massive spike in readership, and this new broad scope allows Jules Davies (Claire Foy) to break through the male-dominated hierarchy. But as the paper circulation grows, so too does the number of its critics.

Already generating awards season buzz, the fast-paced and gripping Ink features riveting performances from its star cast, in a thrilling exploration of this controversial newsroom legacy.
