events.venue: San Fran, Wellington
events.long_description:
GOODNIGHT NURSE ARE BACK… AGAIN

New Zealand pop-punk favourites celebrate 20 years of Always & Never with one final run of shows




To celebrate the 20th anniversary of their debut album Always & Never, the band are coming out of retirement one last time for The Always and Never (Again!) Tour - three final shows across New Zealand before they hang up their studded belts for good.

For the first time ever, Always & Never will also be available on limited-edition purple vinyl, with pre-orders opening Monday 31 August.

Playing Auckland’s Powerstation on Friday 13 November, the band then head south for a show at Loons in Christchurch on Thursday 19 November before what promises to be a final show for the ages at San Fran in Wellington on Friday 20 November. Tickets for all dates go on sale 12pm Thursday 3 September from eccles.co.nz

Released in 2006, their debut album, Always & Never, has remained a favourite among pop-punk fans over the years. That album was the beginning of a nine-year career for Goodnight Nurse. They played hundreds of shows throughout New Zealand and Australia, released two NZ Top 5 albums and scored five NZ Top 40 singles.

“When we got back together in 2023 for the My Chemical Romance show, it felt like there was something special in the air,” says lead singer Joel Little, who has gone on to write and produce hit songs with artists including Taylor Swift, Lorde and Khalid. “So when the 20th anniversary of Always & Never rolled around, we thought, what better way could we possibly celebrate this than by reliving the glory days one last time?”

“We started making music to have fun with our friends, and just for the simple joy of doing it,” says drummer Jaden Parkes, now one of the lead singers of hugely popular band Leisure and the longtime Head of A&R at Sony Music NZ. “Playing these songs live again takes you right back to that feeling.”

And for day one fans, there’s one more reason to make this final tour a must-see.

Original bass player and fan favourite Paul Taite will be joining the band onstage for the tour, playing the songs he helped shape and bringing Goodnight Nurse full circle 20 years after Always & Never first landed.

The Always and Never (Again!) Tour will be Goodnight Nurse’s final three shows in New Zealand. For real this time. Tickets on sale 12pm Thursday 3 September




Limited-edition vinyl avalible for pre-purchase

Richard Dawkins is a world-renowned evolutionary biologist. When published in 1976, his book, ‘The Selfish Gene’, reframed our understanding of life, behaviour, and human nature. Now, 50 years later, he is coming to Wellington to reflect on the book’s revolutionary legacy. He explores what fifty years of science has confirmed or challenged and explains why its core questions are more urgent today than ever before. 
‘The Selfish Gene’ has remained a cornerstone of modern science. It introduced the gene-centred view of evolution and coined the now-ubiquitous concept of the ‘meme’. The ideas in it ignited global debate and five decades of subsequent research. Richard Dawkins is one of the most consequential scientific communicators of our time, so don’t miss the rare opportunity to hear him speak in person.

events.long_description:
Business Training New Zealand Leadership & Management Part 3 Workshop
Our Leadership & Management Part 3 workshop is a practical skills training course designed for people in a leadership/management position.

About this Event



Leaders today are expected to be the driving force of their teams. They are constantly under pressure to lead effectively in a business environment that is characterised by constant change. Our leadership and management courses offer participants the opportunity to develop the necessary skills to embrace this challenge and lead their teams through these times with confidence and pride.

Our Leadership & Management - Part 3 workshop is a practical skills training course designed for people already in a leadership/management position, or those about to take up a new role, who want to explore the latest thinking and models for effective management and leadership and build on the techniques acquired in our Part 1 and 2 workshops.

In today’s world, emotional Intelligence is a critical and powerful component of effective leadership. This 2-day course will equip leaders with the skills to become more ‘people smart’ by developing ways to lead with emotional intelligence. Participants will also learn how to inspire their people with a shared vision and align teams to company goals, along with the tools to lead and manage change, ways to become a more influential and persuasive leader and the tools to raise awareness and manage unconscious bias in the workplace.

Course Outcomes

Assess your leadership strengths and identify opportunities for growth
Learn how to become a more inspirational and influential leader
Understand the importance of emotional intelligence as a key leadership skill
Learn how to lead with emotional intelligence, develop leadership self-awareness and become more ‘people smart’
Communicate your goals, vision and purpose with greater clarity, confidence and inspiration
Inspire and align your team to your shared vision and goals
Understanding change and learn how to lead change and growth in your organisation
Apply strategies to motivate and inspire your people to embrace change and strive for positive outcomes
Understand what unconscious bias is and recognise its effects on your people and your organisation
Explain how you can manage your own unconscious bias and implement steps to raise awareness and manage unconscious bias in the workplace

Course Prerequisite: Participants must have a good understanding of leadership and management fundamentals and/or have previously attended the Business Training New Zealand - Leadership & Management Part 1 & 2 course.

For more information or to book: email or call 04 974 8790

events.long_description:
1 or 2 Day Presentation Skills Workshop

Limited tickets available. Get in now so you don't miss out!

When effective presenters speak, they do more than inform - they influence, persuade, and inspire. That isn’t down to magic or your personality; it’s method. With the right tools, anyone can build genuine connection and move a room.

This workshop is for leaders, emerging leaders, technical specialists, and professionals who want practical tools and techniques for speaking in both formal and informal settings.

Short on time? Attend 1 Day (Foundations) for all the core skills. Ready for a bigger shift? Choose 2 Days (Advanced) for one on one coaching and deeper transformation. Pick what’s right for you.

You’ll leave with the tools to present more clearly, confidently, and with the influence your role demands. This is not just for the stage. You will use these skills everyday.

The workshop format

Small group format for maximum practice and feedback (no massive groups).

Learning is adapted and personalised for maximum value (no cookie-cutter approach).

Hands on, practical learning, with easy to apply tools and techniques (no sitting around listening to theory).

The Effective Speaker - One Day Workshop (Foundations):

Tuesday 24th November

A hands-on day where you’ll learn our step-by-step SpeakerMap™ system to plan valuable presentations quickly and with ease.

You’ll learn the principles behind useful visuals, how to manage nerves, and three delivery techniques you can use immediately.

Foundations is best for technical experts who know their stuff but struggle to get it across, and nervous presenters who want a safe, practical reset.

What you’ll learn

Plan engaging content (fast)

Use the SpeakerMap™ to develop a clear Key Message and structure that keeps audiences attentive without overload.

Plan faster, make better decisions about what to include (and what to ditch).

 

Design useful slides (not wallpaper)

A simple but revolutionary way to design slides that support - not sabotage - your message.

Practical guidance on using AI to fast-track draft slides and create supporting documents (and how to avoid creating AI slop!)

How to use PowerPoint to keep you on track without putting your audience to sleep.

 

Keep nerves under control

A proven psychological approach to calm the mental chatter that causes waffling, speed talking, and blank moments.

Build a personal plan to shift focus from “me” to the audience and the outcome you want.

 

Deliver in a natural, engaging way

Three delivery techniques that help you look credible, be engaging and feel confident.

(For more intensive delivery coaching, check out Day Two)

 

Plenty of practice

You’ll practise each technique in pairs or threes - supportive, safe, and highly practical.

Includes

A full day of training

All food and drinks during the workshop

The Effective Speaker workbook

30minute one on one follow up session

Investment: $1,200 + GST

The Effective Speaker - Two Day Workshop (Advanced)

Tuesday 24th November & Wednesday 25th November

Gain all the skills from Day One - and then take them further. If presenting is central to your career growth, this is the coaching workshop you need.

Over two full days, you’ll create a significant shift in your communication skills.

Day One gives you the foundations to make presenting easier and more effective.

Day Two consolidates and extends these skills. You’ll go deeper into content planning, adapt the tools to your real work presentations, and get personalised coaching to develop your own authentic style.

You’ll also learn strategies for handling even the toughest audiences. The workshop is practical, hands-on, and focused on learning by doing - presenting, receiving coaching, and observing your peers.

If you’re ready for lasting, transformative change in your communication skills, the two-day option is the best choice.

What you’ll learn

Everything from Day 1 (Foundations) PLUS

Go deeper with planning

Apply the SpeakerMap to plan an actual presentation that you can give. 

Dive deeper into crafting valuable messages that you can use in the future. 

Rehearse in a way that actually works

A practical way to prepare when time is tight — so you own your words.

Shift from competent to compelling

One-on-one coaching targeted to your specific needs.

Video feedback plus our inside-out coaching methodology to reconnect you with the techniques you use naturally in conversation.

How to use silence, pace, notes, and the remote without looking stiff or artificial.

How to speak with energy and authenticity, not speed and panic.

Eliminate “ums” and “ahs”, look confident (even when you’re not), and create a sense of commitment that audiences feel.

An understanding of your personal communication strengths and the areas you need to focus on for growth.


Handle audiences like a pro

Strategies for side chats, interruptions, distractions, disagreement, and the odd angry voice - while staying calm and in control.




Includes

Everything in Day 1, plus:

A second full day of training

All food and drinks during the workshop

Videos of your presenting and coaching sessions

The Effective Speaker workbook

60minute one on one follow up session

Investment: $2,500 + GST

I developed a newfound confidence in my ability to communicate effectively, learned how to captivate an audience, and discovered strategies for managing nerves and overcoming stage fright. I would recommend this effective speaking course to anyone looking to enhance their communication abilities. It's not just another course; it's a transformative experience that will empower you to become a more confident and persuasive speaker" Alex Goryachev, New Zealand Green Building Council

Having felt fear in the past each time I have to present to large groups, for the first time I now feel like I have the tools, understanding and ability to approach presentations and conquer my fear. I can’t thank Jane enough.” Nadia Marsh, Head of Bids, Tonkin & Taylor

I feel we all learnt so much and I will definitely be taking her advice on how I can improve myself. This course was well above what I expected, Jane had a great way of communicating. Typically, people tune out or lose interest by the end of the day. This was not the case for us. I honestly thing it’s the best course I’ve been on in my 4 years with WCC." The trainer really made the course for me - she is sensitive and responsive to people’s needs and is genuine in her approach to give the learners as much out of the time as possible. A very polished and well-planned course.” Huia Grey, Department of Conservation

embroidery with beads workshop: Slow Down. Make something.

Join me for a cozy, beginner-friendly embroidery workshop designed for adults who want to learn something new and enjoy a creative evening together.

In this 2hour session, I’ll guide you through the basic stitches you need to get started with hand embroidery and help you start your own project on your item of clothing.

This workshop is all about slowing down, crafting together, and enjoying the process in a relaxed, welcoming space.

All materials are provided, and you’ll head home with:

A piece of practice fabric + a blank square for your next project

An embroidery hoop, needle, some thread and the fabric you need to finish your project



Soft drinks (hot and cold) and snacks will also be available to keep our creative energy flowing.

No experience is needed — just bring an item of clothing you’d love to transform (or a bag, a pouch, anything you can stitch on) and a willingness to try something new. I can’t wait to stitch with you 🤍

Please note, the workshop will be cancelled if less than 3 participants are signed up 7 days prior to the date.

events.name: The Sweet Caroline Tour — A Tribute to Neil Diamond
events.venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
One of the top singer-songwriters to come out of the United States’ 60s music scene was none other than Neil Diamond. With a career spanning five decades, Neil is behind many hits that have stood the test of time and still woo listeners around the globe. Now you get to hear a tribute to him at The Opera House this November. 
Imbuing long-loved hits with new energy, The Sweet Caroline Tour recreates the feel of the famous man with careful attention to detail. It focuses on recapturing the sound, look and charisma of one of the world’s greatest entertainers. 
At the concert, you’ll hear songs that made numerous top ten lists, won Grammy awards and earned an induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. Zac Coombs steps into the shoes of the original performer and brings his own musicality and showmanship to the stage. Don’t worry, you’ll hear all the timeless hits like Sweet Caroline, Song Sung Blue, Red Red Wine, Cracklin’ Rosie, Cherry Cherry, Crunchy Granola Suite, Shilo, Solitary Man, Kentucky Woman, I Am… I Said, and more. 
Relive an era when songs were written with heart, soul and honesty, and melodies stayed with you for a lifetime.

events.name: NZ Photographers of Cultural Collections Forum 2026
events.venue: 55 Cable Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
NZ Photographers of Cultural Collections is a group of photographers and imaging professionals working across Galleries, Libraries, Archives, and Museums across Aotearoa. We photograph cultural collections from paintings through to scientific specimens, and from intangible culture, through flat copy digitisation to 3D scanning. 

The forum is a chance to share knowledge and build professional networks. It provides valuable professional development that is otherwise hard to come by for this specialised field. We specifically aim to help smaller institutions by democratising specialist knowledge and building a network of support across the country. This year we have hybrid capability, and welcome physical event (paid) online-only (free) registrations.

This event relies on volunteers and institutional support. Thanks to Te Papa Tongarewa for donating the venue and kaimahi time, and National Services Te Paerangi for funding and administrative support and additional travel support for eligible attendees. Kaimahi from NZ maritime Museum, Auckland University of Technology, Auckland City Libraries, Puke Ariki and Archives NZ/National Library have collaborated to organise the event this year.

These contributions help keep costs down, the physical registration fee will help to cover a venue set up fee and a catered morning tea and lunch for in-person attendees.

Online attendees will receive an email with the zoom link closer to the date.

We intend to record the event via zoom. If we decide to distribute recordings in any form, we will seek the permission of speakers before doing so.

We'll be closing registrations for in-person attendees at 4pm Friday 6th Nov.

We have an online network here: https://groups.io/g/NZPCC
For any pātai please email us at: nzpcccommittee@gmail.com

Join us for Aotearoa's first Indigenous Tech Summit. Two packed days of keynotes and kōrero from indigenous innovators across the globe and Aotearoa.

For centuries, the vast expanse of Te Moana-nui-a-Kiwa was not a barrier separating our people. It was the original superhighway, connecting Indigenous navigators, traders and innovators across the Pacific.

The Indigenous Tech Summit 2026 reclaims this narrative.

Led by ancestral wisdom and cutting-edge digital capability, the summit brings together Māori and global Indigenous tech communities to navigate the future of artificial intelligence, data sovereignty, enterprise and workforce development.

Meditate & Create
Explore your creativity through intuitive Neurographic Art and a soothing sound bath, blending mindful expression with deep relaxation.

About this Event


Meditate & Create
Neurographic Art & Sound Bath experience

 


Please try to arrive by 5:45pm so we can get everyone into the event and start on time at 6pm.

 

Neurographic Art is a simple, intuitive art practice that invites you to slow down, soften the mind, and turn your thoughts and feelings into lines, shapes, and patterns. There’s no right or wrong way to create, and no artistic experience is needed.

Alongside the art practice, you’ll be guided through a deeply relaxing sound bath featuring singing bowls, chimes and flutes. Let the sounds create space to settle, listen inward and connect with your creative flow.

Come as you are, explore without expectation, and leave with your own unique piece of art.





Please stay for a delicious plant-based dinner and dessert afterwards, included in your ticket!



Meet your Artist Rowena

Kia ora, I’m Rowena and I’ve been teaching art to kids, adults, retirees, and folks on the margins for 15 years. I aim to make art and creativity as inclusive as possible, especially for the people who say, ‘I can’t do art.’





Meet your Sound Healer Alexandra

Alexandra is a sound healing practitioner devoted to nurturing healing in both mind and body. She believes that sound vibration holds the power to expand consciousness and restore harmony and balance in our lives. Her journey into sound healing began with the realization of how deeply sound vibration was affecting her psyche, making her more mindful of the music she listens to and the intention it carries. Along the way, she has drawn inspiration from the Bhakti Lounge Kirtan. Their music has profoundly influenced her own sound healing practice, inspiring her to explore sound as a tool for transformation, connection, and inner peace.

Yoga Nidra: The Art of Becoming
Pause, soften and turn inward with Yoga Nidra, a gentle journey of deep rest, reflection and trusting the quiet process of becoming.

About this Event


Yoga Nidra: The Art of Becoming





Please try to arrive by 5:45pm so we can get everyone into the event and start on time at 6pm.




As late spring unfolds around us, nature offers a gentle reminder that growth does not need to be rushed.

The buds open when they are ready.
The light returns in its own rhythm.
And beneath the surface, so much is quietly becoming.

This Yoga Nidra is an invitation to pause, soften and listen inwardly.

To honour where you have been.
To rest in where you are.
And to gently welcome all that is beginning to unfold.

You do not have to know exactly where you are going. Perhaps, for now, it is enough to trust the becoming.








After the event is over, enjoy an amazing plant-based dinner and dessert, all included in your ticket!



Meet your host Nicola

Nicola of Namaste Nicola is a dedicated yoga teacher with over 20 years of experience teaching across Australia and New Zealand. With more than 300 hours of training with international teachers, her approach is gentle, soulful, and deeply grounded in yoga philosophy. Nicola creates a calm and nurturing space where students can slow down, rest deeply, and reconnect with themselves through practices such as Yoga Nidra, Hatha, and Yin Yoga.

events.long_description:
Reel Rock 20 Film Tour - Wellington
Reel Rock 20 brings a new collection of films celebrating ambition, resilience and the relentless pursuit of the impossible.

About this Event



Reel Rock 20 brings the world’s greatest climbing stories back to the big screen with a thrilling new collection of films celebrating ambition, resilience and the relentless pursuit of the impossible.

This year’s program follows four extraordinary climbing journeys: Olympic champion Janja Garnbret sets her sights on Bibiliographie; Michaela Kiersch’s historic quest to achieve the ultimate climbing double of 5.15 and V15; Colin Haley’s legendary winter solo push on Cerro Torre; and Ben Mayforth’s determined pursuit of 5.13 as he continues to redefine what is possible in adaptive climbing.

JANJA GARNBRET
Olympic champion Janja Garnbret sets her sights on the legendary climb Bibiographie
Featuring: Janja Garnbret

MICHAELA KIERSCH
Michaela Kiersch sets out to make climbing history by becoming the first woman to complete the ultimate climbing double: sending both 5.15 and V15.

Her pursuit demands extraordinary strength, precision and perseverance as she pushes the limits of performance across two of climbing’s most difficult disciplines.
Featuring: Michaela Kiersch

COLIN HALEY
Elite alpinist Colin Haley lays everything on the line in a legendary winter solo push on Cerro Torre - one of Patagonia’s most iconic and unforgiving peaks.
Alone in extreme conditions, Haley takes on a bold alpine challenge where speed, commitment and survival are inseparable.
Featuring: Colin Haley

BEN MAYFORTH
Ben Mayforth redefines adaptive climbing through an intense and resolute pursuit of 5.13.
Driven by determination and an uncompromising approach to progression, Mayforth challenges expectations and expands the possibilities of adaptive climbing.
Featuring: Ben Mayforth

Tickets are on sale now at reelrockfilmtour.com.
NO REFUNDS OUTSIDE OF ADVENTURE ENTERTAINMENT'S CONTROL

events.long_description:
20 years on from its release, Cat Power’s album, The Greatest, still retains its mesmeric pull. A late-night classic, it still feels as intimate and raw as it did in 2014. Now you get the chance to hear the album in its entirety live at The Opera House in Wellington.   
The concert won’t just showcase this seminal album — it’ll sit alongside favourite songs from Cat’s catalogue over the past three decades. The concert will drift through heartbreak, survival, longing, and grace with the kind of restraint that only makes the emotional weight hit harder. From the slow-burn sway of Living Proof to the bruised beauty of The Greatest, these songs endure because they tell the truth softly.   
The support act for the Wellington concert is Lawrence Arabia. He is known for his sophisticated songwriting and distinctive blend of indie-pop, chamber-pop and psychedelic influences. Lawrence has toured extensively across New Zealand, Europe and North America.

events.long_description:
CLUEDUNNIT

DINNER WITH 'MURDER ON THE MENU'

Step into a world of intrigue, suspense, and unforgettable entertainment as InterContinental Wellington partners with Cluedunnit to present an immersive murder mystery dining experience. Guests will be transported into a captivating story where secrets unfold, clues emerge, and every guest becomes part of the investigation.

Combining exceptional hospitality with live theatrical entertainment, Cluedunnit invites guests to enjoy a delicious dining experience while questioning suspects, following leads, and working together to solve a thrilling mystery. From the moment you arrive, you'll be immersed in a world of drama, laughter, and unexpected twists.

Whether you're planning a unique night out with friends, celebrating a special occasion, or enjoying an unforgettable evening with colleagues, Cluedunnit at InterContinental Wellington promises the perfect blend of fine dining, mystery, and entertainment.

Guests will interact with a live cast of characters, uncover clues, and work together to crack the case, all while enjoying a delicious three-course dinner.

But beware, all is not as it seems. As secrets unravel and tensions rise, you'll need to decipher the clues, question the suspects, and piece together the evidence before it's too late. After all, where there's a will, there's a murder.

Where there's a mystery, there's a motive. Where there's a motive, there's a murder. The question is: whodunnit?

MURDER AT THE MANOR - The Story So Far...

It is 1929 and this English Cotswold beauty spot is celebrating the life of elderly heiress Rose Stimper, who, in an act of philanthropy, has bequeathed the village a large sum of money and left instructions that the villagers must decide how best to spend it. 

This will be a party like no other. Everyone has ideas on how to spend the money, and the entire village turns out to attend Pokeingham Hall, which has been thrown open for the first time in many years to host the event.

But beware, all is not as it seems. There are dark forces at work.

Enjoy a delicious three course dinner as you question the suspects, decipher the clues and work to crack the case. And please remember - where there’s a will, there’s a murder!


DINNER MENU:

STARTER: gf/v

MAIN COURSE: gf/v

Corn fed Chicken supreme, truffled portobello plin ravioli, ajo blanco, spring asparagus, chardonnay jus

VEGETARIAN MAIN COURSE: gf/df

Risotto prima vera Aged Acquerello rice, asparagus, green beans, peas, parmesan fondue

DESSERT: gf/v

Dark blood chocolate mousse, with raspberry and dark chocolate crumble.

We cater for all dietary requirements - please select the relevant option at checkout. 

BOOKING YOUR PLACE AT A TABLE: 

You will be seated around tables of 10. If it is likely that friends will be coming along too, it is best to book all your places at the same time to ensure you are all on the same table.

Please note, ticket sales will end 72 hours before the event.

info@cluedunnit.com.au

events.venue: Valhalla, Wellington
events.long_description:
Los Angeles post-punk band DECEITS has been building something real from the ground up. Since forming in 2021, longtime friends Kevin Moreno (Vocals/Instruments) and Francisco Saenz (Drums/Percussions) have self-released their entire catalog, quietly amassing millions of streams, selling out tours, and pressing vinyl that disappears just as quickly as it arrives. Their momentum has carried them from the underground to stages like Cruel World 2025 and across their first European tour, all while earning coverage from Post-Punk.com and the Los Angeles Times. DECEITS aren’t interested in playing it safe. Their take on post-punk rejects the genre’s colder edges in favor of something more alive, pulling in the color, rhythm, and emotional intensity of the Spanish-language music they grew up with. The result is a sound that feels both nostalgic and distinctly their own: moody, melodic, and impossible to stand still to.

This show is at Whammy Bar in Auckland

events.name: Yīn Yīn - New Zealand Tour | Wellington
events.venue: San Fran, Wellington
events.long_description:
Dutch groove-explorers YĪN YĪN are bringing disco, funk, psychedelia and dance to Wellington’s San Fran Friday 27 November and Auckland’s Tuning Fork on Saturday 28 November. 
Made up of Erik Bandt on guitar, Kees Berkers on drums, Jerôme Schere on keyboards and Remy Scheren on bass, YĪN YĪN are the kaleidoscopic instrumental quartet from Maastricht, Netherlands, renowned for their genre-bending records and transportive live experience. 
Emerging out of an experimental jam session in a remote ballet school village in 2017 that resulted in the making of their debut album The Rabbit That Hunts Tigers, the band have since created another three critically acclaimed albums and spent the better part of the last decade chasing rhythm across continents. 
With relentless international touring and performing everywhere from Fuji Rock Festival and Lowlands to North Sea Jazz Festival and Clockenflap they have been collecting sounds, textures and musical flavours like souvenirs, drawing from a multitude of influences such as ‘70s Thai Funk, Japanese City Pop and crate-dug global disco. Each project has evolved alongside the eager exploration to immerse their worldly experience into a sonic universe of their own.
Their latest of which,Yatta!, arrived in January 2026. A defining influence on Yatta! Is the cosmic allure of Italo Disco - the psychedelic futuristic dance music that emerged in Italy during the late 1970s and flourished throughout the 80s. “It has something of a mystique,” the band explains. 
“Because all the producers were using new recording techniques and effects and stuff like that, but there are not many pictures or videos of how they were creating things in the studio.You have to use your own fantasy and create your own story about how that music is created.”
This one sees the band into their most realised selves yet, translating into an unmissable live experience. “We tried to make a mix of songs that are very energetic and danceable and are party starters, but also have songs that take you on trips and are more easy. People can also just chill and relax and listen to the music and enjoy it.” - YĪN YĪN 

Aotearoa, get ready to move. YĪN YĪN are set to take on Aotearoa for the first time for two shows this November.

events.long_description:
After a sold-out tour in early 2026, Sir Tony Robinson brings his talk show back to Wellington. Catch ‘An Audience with Sir Tony Robinson’ at The Opera House. The television presenter, actor, and award-winning writer has an impressive decades-long career. Tony will divulge behind-the-scenes stories from his life on and off screen. He’ll then read from his fiction debut ‘The House of Wolf’, an epic tale of Alfred the Great and the bloody birth of England. He won’t hog the microphone the whole time — you’ll also get the chance to ask him questions. Expect masterful storytelling from Tony and lots of laughs from the audience. 

You might have seen Tony play Baldrick in Rowan Atkinson’s cult 80s sitcom ‘Blackadder’. In the show, his “I have a cunning plan” catchphrase and comedic timing made him a household name. He’s also celebrated for his work in historical broadcasting, which includes presenting 20 seasons of ‘Time Team’. His infectious enthusiasm for history continued, as he wrote his first novel aged 78. The book delves into the (often grim) realities of life for ordinary people caught between Saxon kings and Viking raiders.

events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Bicycle Maintenance for Beginners
Have you recently started riding a bicycle and want to make sure you can take care of it properly? Or have you been riding for ages, but have always been scared to fix anything yourself?
Are you unsure of how to pump your tyres, or how much oil your chain needs? Find yourself fumbling for words when trying to describe that clunking sound to the guy in the bike shop?
This one day course lays bare the nuts and bolts of bicycle mechanics for absolute beginners, as well as those with a little experience. Through practical experience working with your own bicycle, you will find out what needs to be done to keep it running smoothly. We’ll cover what to look out for when things start to wear out, and how to check for problems, so you can be confident your bicycle is safe to ride. You will also learn how to fix some of the most common mechanical problems, and learn about the correct terminology and tools to use.
Those who feel intimidated in bike shops are especially welcome in this course. No question is a stupid question!
Bringing a bike to work on is essential, preferably one that you are riding regularly, because the best way to learn is by building familiarity with your own ride. E-bikes are welcome, although the extra weight can mean they are more challenging to work on. Regardless of whether your bike is in pristine condition, or desperately in need of TLC, it is welcome on the course – bikes showing a bit more wear can be useful for the learning of the whole group.
Bring your pushbike along on the day.  If you have the following, please bring them as well:  A multi-tool and pump; chain oil and rag; lightweight close-fitting gardening or rubber gloves.
Note: A condition of enrolment is that you must provide photo ID when you attend.
(Please note this course is not exhaustive and is not a professional training course).
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
- Name most parts of a bicycle correctly
- Perform a quick safety check on any bicycle
- Fix a flat tyre
- Adjust your bike to fit your body
- Oil and clean your chain
- Identify and fix some common brake problems
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.name: DECEITS AOTEAROA TOUR 2026 - CHRISTCHURCH
events.venue: Valhalla, Wellington
events.long_description:
Los Angeles post-punk band DECEITS has been building something real from the ground up. Since forming in 2021, longtime friends Kevin Moreno (Vocals/Instruments) and Francisco Saenz (Drums/Percussions) have self-released their entire catalog, quietly amassing millions of streams, selling out tours, and pressing vinyl that disappears just as quickly as it arrives. Their momentum has carried them from the underground to stages like Cruel World 2025 and across their first European tour, all while earning coverage from Post-Punk.com and the Los Angeles Times. DECEITS aren’t interested in playing it safe. Their take on post-punk rejects the genre’s colder edges in favor of something more alive, pulling in the color, rhythm, and emotional intensity of the Spanish-language music they grew up with. The result is a sound that feels both nostalgic and distinctly their own: moody, melodic, and impossible to stand still to.

This show is at Space Academy in Christchurch

Tickets here

events.long_description:
By the time indie/folk singer songwriter Aldous Harding hits Wellington, she will have travelled across the UK and Europe with her Train on the Island tour. By the time the tour reaches the Michael Fowler Centre, it will be a finely oiled machine.   
Named after her fifth studio album Train on the Island, all ten of the album’s songs will appear in the concert, including One Stop, and Venus In The Zinnia.   
Aldous Harding captivates listeners with what Martin Pepperell describes as an ‘elastic and shape-shifting voice’. This, combined with eccentric performances, has catapulted the Lyttelton-born singer to fame. Her second album ‘Party’ won the Taite Prize in 2018, and The Barrel, from her third studio album ‘Designer’, won the 2019 APRA Silver Scroll award.

events.id: Eric Idle — An Evening of Idle Conversation-St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
events.name: Eric Idle — An Evening of Idle Conversation
events.venue: St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Relive the highs and bitter lows of one of the most beloved comedians and writers of all time. Eric Idle sits down to tell his incredible life story, live on stage at the St James Theatre in Wellington. From the giddy heights of Monty Python success to the trauma of childhood — this is unscripted and candid. The audience will also get the chance to put their own questions to him live on stage.

An Evening of Idle Conversation covers sixty years of show business. Eric will recall memories of the friends he has loved and lost including Graham Chapman, George Harrison, and Robin Williams. He’ll also cover fortunes made and squandered, feuds, reunions, a brush with cancer, and why, at 83, he is still looking on the bright side of life.

Along with five other comics Eric formed Month Python in 1969. The troupe’s absurdist sketches continue to influence comedy more fifty years later. Eric is perhaps most famous for writing the song Always Look on the Bright Side of Life, The Rutles (the world’s first mockumentary), and the musical Spamalot.

Natural Textured Rings - Taster - Wellington!
Make your own personalised ring - a gift for yourself or someone special! :-)

Learn the basic technique first in copper or brass, and then craft your final piece in silver!

Over this taster class, you’ll be guided through the process of heating and texturing metal, cutting and shaping with traditional jewellery tools. Use feathers, leaves, or fabrics to create a unique texture for a beautiful ring!

Learn to measure your finger, cut metal to length and texture it without rolling mill, hammers and punches. Then use a jewellers torch, sandpaper and polishing, and your beautiful new ring will be ready to wear.

This 3-hour class is ideal for beginners, groups of friends and visitors to the city.

Included in the class fee are copper and brass for practising on, a sterling silver ring strip and all consumables such as sandpaper, solder and chemicals. Extra metals are available for purchase in the studio.

Kids aged 12 (or so) are welcome to attend the class, but any person under the age of 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

Workshop fee is $165, Early bird pricing $148 (ends 2 November).

DOORS OPEN 6:00pm
SHOW START 7:00pm

Leaving Dublin, Ireland where he was born and raised until the age of 22, David got drunk on travel and never quite hit sobriety of it. He has lived and worked in twelve countries and visited over eighty. His shows draw on his wide travels, cultural observations, attempts at language study, (occasional) international drinking session(s) and being a mildly confused immigrant. 
David is the winner of the prestigious annual San Francisco Comedy Competition, (previous finalists include Robin Williams, Ellen DeGeneres and Dana Carvey) and runner-up in the Moth’s largest US Grandslam storytelling competition. Also a bestselling writer, David recorded his debut special Documented for Dry Bar Comedy in 2019, his follow up Cultural Appreciation in 202, and his award winning show Shelf Help in 2025. He has been featured on TED.com, Sirius XM, Just For Laughs, Netflix is a Joke Festival, RTE’s Late Late Show, The Irish Independent, Inc, NPR, and the Huffington Post among others. A festival favorite, David's videos have also gone viral many times over with over 800 million views and a social following of over 2 million people. More info: davidnihill.com

events.long_description:
Los Angeles post-punk band DECEITS has been building something real from the ground up. Since forming in 2021, longtime friends Kevin Moreno (Vocals/Instruments) and Francisco Saenz (Drums/Percussions) have self-released their entire catalog, quietly amassing millions of streams, selling out tours, and pressing vinyl that disappears just as quickly as it arrives. Their momentum has carried them from the underground to stages like Cruel World 2025 and across their first European tour, all while earning coverage from Post-Punk.com and the Los Angeles Times. DECEITS aren’t interested in playing it safe. Their take on post-punk rejects the genre’s colder edges in favor of something more alive, pulling in the color, rhythm, and emotional intensity of the Spanish-language music they grew up with. The result is a sound that feels both nostalgic and distinctly their own: moody, melodic, and impossible to stand still to.
Tickets here

NZFSS Conference 2026
Registrations open soon!

2026 NZFSS Conference
📍1 - 4 December 2026
📍Takina | Wellington

Register here https://www.nzfssconference.co.nz/

Conference Theme:
At the Confluence: Communities, Catchments, and our Freshwater Futures - Ngā Rerenga E Tūtaki Ana

Our 2026 conference explores the confluence: the place where flows meet, merge, and reshape one another. In freshwater science, confluences are dynamic hydrological junctions which create unique habitats and environments. For this conference it represents the meeting of people, knowledge systems, innovations, and aspirations that shape the future of wai in Aotearoa.

Hosting the conference in Te Whanganui‑a‑Tara/Wellington, where urban streams like Waimapihi and Kumutoto meet the great harbour Te Whanganui‑a‑Tara provides a powerful metaphor for integration across urban waters, catchments, and communities. As Aotearoa navigates changing climate pressures, evolving policy landscapes, disruptive technologies, and growing community involvement, this confluence becomes a space for meaningful collaboration and forward‑thinking action.

We look forward to welcoming you to WLG!

events.long_description:
Celebrate, connect and be inspired as we bring the Wellington Women in HealthTech community together to close out 2026.

Join us for an evening of conversation, connection and festive celebration, featuring a panel discussion with Kelsey Schwynn and Eileen Duddy from Health New Zealand | Te Whatu Ora Digital Services. They will share insights into their roles, the different pathways that brought them into digital health, and their experiences working at the intersection of strategy, design and delivery.

Date: Wednesday, 2 December 2026
Time: 5.00 pm–7.30 pm
Venue: Fujifilm, Level 9, 20 Ballance Street, Wellington

Evening programme

5.00 pm–5.30 pm: Arrival and networking

5.30 pm–6.30 pm: Panel conversation with Kelsey Schwynn and Eileen Duddy

6.30 pm–7.30 pm: Festive networking and end-of-year celebration

Meet our speakers

Kelsey Schwynn is a Digital Health Partner at Health New Zealand, with experience spanning health strategy, product leadership, service design and digital transformation. Before joining Health New Zealand, she was Chief Product Officer at Optimal Workshop and held senior strategic design roles in Australia and the United States. Her career has included supporting government agencies, not-for-profits and Fortune 500 companies through human-centred design, product strategy and large-scale digital change.

Eileen Duddy is a strategic digital health leader with more than 20 years’ experience in the health sector, including over a decade working across complex, cross-government initiatives. As a Digital Health Partner at Health New Zealand | Te Whatu Ora, she connects Digital Services with health sector stakeholders, translating clinical, operational and strategic priorities into aligned digital roadmaps and investment pathways. Eileen brings a pragmatic, forward-thinking approach to defining problems, aligning priorities and progressing initiatives that deliver meaningful outcomes for people, whānau and the wider health system.

Come along to hear two compelling career stories, exchange ideas with others across the HealthTech community, and celebrate the people and progress that have shaped another year for WiHT in Wellington.

9:00 Welcome and Industry Update

events.id: Allegra Krieger-San Fran, Wellington -Ticket Master
events.name: Allegra Krieger
events.venue: San Fran, Wellington
events.long_description:
New York based songwriter and composer Allegra Krieger brings her singular blend of folk, rock and indie pop to San Fran on 3 December, joined by special guest Elly Mae.

Known for songwriting that is intimate, understated and deeply observant, Krieger pairs soulful vocals with raw, vulnerable lyricism, moving through themes of love, loss and self-discovery with a striking sense of emotional clarity. Her work has earned praise from the New York Times, who described her as a “deceptively understated songwriter,” while Paste has celebrated the distinctive poetry running through her music. 

Having shared stages with artists including Jana Horn, Fust, Johanna Samuels, Shalom and Charlotte Cornfield, Krieger has steadily carved out a space of her own within contemporary indie songwriting, creating music that feels equally at home in moments of quiet reflection and full-band intensity. 

Opening the evening is Pōneke songwriter Elly Mae, whose dreamy guitar-led folk-noir draws from the textures of The Brian Jonestown Massacre, PJ Harvey and Mazzy Star. Since first appearing on Wellington stages in early 2025, she has gone on to perform at Newtown Festival, CubaDupa and Flying Nun’s A Month of Saturdays live series, with RNZ describing her sound as a “woozy ethereal slice of dreampop.” 

Together, the two artists make for an evening of evocative songwriting, atmospheric guitars and music built around the power of close listening.







San Fran holds a Supervised License, meaning minors are welcome to attend events at San Fran so long as they are accompanied by a legal guardian at all times whilst at the venue. Minors are of course not allowed to purchase alcohol under any circumstance.

events.long_description:
Pre-Christmas camp at Catchpool Valley, Remutaka Forest Park
Join us for a pre-Christmas camp in the Catchpool Valley. All campers welcome including tents, $10 per night for adults; $5 per night for children and young people aged 5-17 years; 0-4 years free.

This Department of Conservation campsite is part of the Remutaka Forest Park and situated on the road from Wainuiomata to the coast.

Toilets and cold showers available.

Onsite water must be boiled so it is recommended you bring your own drinking water.

There is no rubbish disposal or dump station at the campsite, so you must take all waste away with you.

Dogs must be under control and on a leash at all times.

There is plenty of room to camp.

Look for the All Points flag when you arrive.

Note that the gates to the Catchpool Valley close at 8pm and open again at 6am.

There are a variety of short and longer bush walks adjacent to the campsite..

You can also explore the local area including tracks up to the historic Baring Head Lighthouse.

You can either fill in a registration form and pay when you arrive or book and pay for your site in advance online at https://www.doc.govt.nz/parks-and-recreation/places-to-go/wellington-kapiti/places/remutaka-forest-park/things-to-do/campsites/catchpool-valley-campsite/

If you book online you will see for 4 options. Choose Catchpool Valley Campsite which is on the righthand side of the booking screen. This is the general camping area.

events.venue: Awhi Yoga and Wellbeing Centre, 15 Johnston St., Wellington
events.long_description:
Unwind from the stresses of the week and start your weekend in a state of relaxation. Yoga Nidra, often referred to as "yogic sleep," is a deeply restorative practice that promotes physical relaxation, mental clarity, and emotional balance. It's the perfect way to rejuvenate your mind, body, and soul: your hinengaro, tinana and wairua.

Yoga nidra is a powerful technique that directly works to heal your mind by removing samskaras - untying knots and mental impressions. This practice of learning to relax consciously is well regarded as an antidote for stress, anxiety, poor sleep amongst other health benefits.

Everyone is welcome to experience the profound benefits of Yoga Nidra, and no prior experience is required. For some people, however, Yoga Nidra’s prolonged stillness or internal focus can bring up strong emotions, memories, and/or sensations. You are encouraged to listen and respond in a way that feels safe for you — adjusting your position, keeping your eyes open, grounding yourself, or stepping out of the room at any time.

Yoga Nidra may not be suitable for everyone. If you are experiencing acute mental health challenges, unprocessed trauma, or conditions that make stillness or internal focus difficult, we recommend seeking guidance from a qualified healthcare provider or speaking with the teacher before participating.

events.long_description:
Summer Tour - Kāpiti
Don't miss some Baroque French and Italian delights with NZSO Concertmaster Vesa-Matti Leppänen and Aotearoa New Zealand soprano Anna Leese.

It is astonishing to consider the musical impact Giovanni Pergolesi made, considering he died of tuberculosis at the age of 26. Like Mozart, his early demise quickly became the stuff of legend — hundreds of works were (often falsely) ascribed to this Italian late-Baroque genius, while rumours swirled that his death was the result of murderous jealousy from musical rivals.

Led by NZSO Concertmaster Vesa-Matti Leppänen, we survey some of Pergolesi’s most brilliant opera — La serva padrona, Adriano in Siria, L’Olimpiade and Il prigionier superbo. We are delighted to have Aotearoa New Zealand soprano Anna Leese join us as we delve into music that glories in resplendent Italian Baroque colours and textures.

We complete this magnificent concert with a detour into the French-Baroque, with a suite from Jean-Philippe Rameau's Platée. C’est magnifique!

Generously supported by Ainsley Walter

Make a day of it. Gather your friends and whānau, plan your destination getaway, secure your accommodation and VIP parking early, and get ready to savour the flavours, sounds, and spirit of summer at Kāpiti Food Fair 2026.

Kāpiti Food Fair is where great food, great people, and great summer memories come together. As one of the Wellington region’s most anticipated food festivals, it offers a vibrant celebration of New Zealand’s food culture, bringing together the very best producers, artisans, chefs, entertainers, and food lovers for an unforgettable destination day out.

More than just a food event, Kāpiti Food Fair is a lively summer festival that celebrates the incredible talent and diversity of New Zealand’s food and beverage industry. Visitors can sample and shop their way through an exciting United Nations of flavours, discovering artisan products, boutique beverages, handcrafted treats, international street food, fresh produce, specialty ingredients, and unique home and kitchen products. It is a place to try, buy, eat, drink, relax, and uncover new favourites.

On the menu for 2026 ……. up to 10,000+ visitors, 250 vendor sites including a Kāpiti Artisan Producer Zone, an off-licence Liquor Zone, a Licenced Bar & Main Stage, the Seriously Pickled Kāpiti Kitchen, the Kāpiti Ice Cream Dining Room, FREE kid’s zone, ZEAL Zone buskers, roving street performers and much more!

Mazengarb Reserve Paraparaumu Kāpiti Coast
10am to 5pm RAIN or SHINE

TICKET COSTS
EARLY BIRD by 8 Nov:
$18 Adults | $13 Gold Card or Student ID (+ booking fees)

STANDARD from 9 Nov:
$23 Adults | $18 Gold Card or Student ID (+ booking fees)

AT GATE:
$30 Adults | $25 Gold Card or Student ID (Eftpos ONLY)

FREE up to 12 years ANYTIME

PARKING OPTIONS: $13 VIP & Gold Coin

MERCH (not sold online): $3 Bags

Booking fees will be added to the cost of your ticket and paid at check-out. Booking fees cover Humanitix costs, and everything else goes to their education projects that help to change lives. Kāpiti Food Fair has chosen to support Manaiakalani Education Trust that supports Māori, Pasifika, and disadvantaged learners in Aotearoa to increase student outcomes and get equal access to digital education.

TOP TIPS for a FANTASTIC DAY at the Kāpiti Food Fair:

TRANSPORT & PARKING
Allow extra travel time as the roads will be busy with many others making their way to the Fair.

DISABLED/MOBILITY parking is FREE and near Gate Entry 2, with parking marshals ready to assist. Let VIP parking scanners at the Scaife Dr Barrier Arm know that you need disabled/mobility parking and they will wave you through.

events.long_description:
Lady painters - Guided Walk
From colonial days to the present, many of our botanical artists have been extraordinary women who recorded in scientific detail New Zealand's unique endemic flora. During this 60-minute downhill walk we will see a selection of the plants they painted, and will be pleased to note how they remain 'healthy and happy' in our garden environment today.

Meet at the Cable Car Lookout, Upland Road, Kelburn.
Cost: $10 or Free for Friends – bookings required (you’ll get the option to choose your ticket type after clicking ‘Buy Tickets’)

This is part of the regular walks run by the Friends of the Wellington Botanic Garden. They run throughout the year with a different topic every time.

Join the Friends for only $30 a year and all the walks will be free, as well as other great benefits.

events.long_description:
For the first time in 10 years - Mark Moroney & David Shanhun are reuniting for a series of intimate shows across New Zealand in 2026. This special tour brings their signature blend of world-class guitar playing, heartfelt songwriting, rich harmonies, and light-hearted banter back to audiences around the country. Expect an evening of unforgettable music, plenty of laughs, and the kind of connection that only comes from two great friends & musicians sharing the stage.

This is your chance to see these two acclaimed guitarists and singer-songwriters LIVE in your town!

NEWLANDS COMMUNITY CENTRE - SAT 5th DEC.

💫 Seated Show

💫 Intimate Setting

💫 Cheaper $15 tickets for under 18s

💫 Doors open 6:30pm / show starts at 7pm (8:45pm finish).

Don’t miss your chance to experience these two exquisite musicians, live and up close.

MARK MORONEY

“A mix of huskiness and honey, Peregian singer, songwriter and acoustic guitarist Mark Moroney’s voice acts like a balm.” Frances Frangenheim, Salt Magazine.

Singer song writer and guitarist Mark Moroney radiates emotion, authenticity and soul.  His style and sound are distilled from a musical melting pot of folk, blues, roots, soul, jazz and pop. 

A favourite at festivals including Woodford Folk Festival (AU), The Mosaic Music Festival (Singapore), & The Bay Of Islands Jazz & Blues Festival (NZ), experiencing Mark live is an unmissable highlight of any show.

DAVID SHANHUN

"Once in a while you see an artist who is out of the ordinary." - The Shirley Ryder Show

David Shanhun has opened for Rock legends Foreigner, & Heart, and has performed in NZ, Japan, Australia, and the UK. His exquisite guitar work shines under his superb storytelling and songwriting. He's performed with Grammy Award winner Bryan White, and is known for his engaging live shows and heartfelt tunes.

events.long_description:
Tui Brewery Express: The Ultimate Christmas Party!
Climb aboard The Tui Express for the ultimate end of year office Christmas party! This is the perfect workplace celebration that beats the standard corporate dinner, making it an unforgettable scenic journey aboard our premium carriages. It’s the ultimate way to reward your hardworking team, swap out the boring boardroom, thank your favorite clients, and celebrate the year's wins with a spectacular Sunday on the rails.

The undisputed crown jewel of this journey is our passage through the spectacular Manawatū Gorge. With the old highway permanently closed, the rail line offers an exclusive, front row seat to this rugged natural wonder. Watch the dramatic river below and feel the history as we steam through the gorge's tunnels. There is no better place to capture an epic, casual end of year team photo than from our open air viewing platform, the ultimate vantage point for ditching the laptops, hearing the thunderous echo of the steam locomotive, and catching the crisp air of the Manawatū Gorge.

The festive celebrations start the second you step on board! Throughout the trip, our onboard licensed café carriage will be open. Your crew can sit back, relax, and purchase a range of alcoholic and non alcoholic refreshments to toast to your Q4 wins, along with hot espresso coffees and plenty of food, sweet treats, and snacks right from the rails as the stunning scenery rolls by.

Our tracks lead straight to Mangatainoka Station. Upon arrival, step off the platform and stretch your legs with a flat, leisurely 15 minute walk to the world famous Tui Brewery, or hop directly onto one of our dedicated transfer buses waiting for your group. Once at the brewery, relax and toast to your team's successes in the iconic historic grounds. Forget the awkward office Secret Santa and the sad boardroom sausage rolls, your ticket includes a delicious, hearty BBQ buffet lunch and a complimentary Tui beverage (or non alcoholic alternative) to celebrate a successful year together!

Your ticket covers your return journey from your chosen departure station in beautifully appointed premium carriages alongside exclusive rail only views of the Manawatū Gorge, rugged cliffs, and historic tunnels. You will have unrestricted access to the open air viewing platform for unbeatable team bonding, sightseeing, and staff photography, plus full access to the onboard licensed café carriage selling drinks, coffees, and snacks. At the destination, you get a freshly prepared festive BBQ buffet lunch inside the iconic Tui Brewery grounds, one complimentary Tui beer, cider, or non alcoholic beverage, and free transfer buses between Mangatainoka Station and the brewery.

Ali Whitton is a New Zealand-born, Yorkshire-raised singer-songwriter whose music is deeply influenced by the landscapes of both countries. In April he released his debut album, ‘Between the Forest and the Stars’. events.long_description:
UK music’s biggest underdogs, indie rock juggernauts The Reytons, keep charging forward on their unstoppable rise. Having flirted with overseas territories successfully over the past 5 years, the band are now heading out on their very first World Tour, and have announced their return to Australia and New Zealand this November and December

Renowned for their raucous live shows, and touted by many as the best live act of their generation, the British 4-piece pride themselves on their honesty and pure energy. Having taken their native UK by storm, with number one albums, sold out park shows and major festival headlines, the lads from Rotherham are taking on the world with their upcoming world tour.

In 2025 alone, they toured the UK, headlined Tramlines Festival and the iconic Wembley Arena. The upcoming world tour is a huge statement for a band who have hurdled every obstacle with nothing other than blue-collar grit and determination. It cements them as a band at the top of British music. The Reytons also recently announced their fourth studio album A Love Letter To A Broken Town - due for release in July.

Rooted in the rough around the edges humour and honesty of everyday life, The Reytons continue to channel their origins into everything they do, and A Love Letter To A Broken Town sees them staying true to those roots while pushing their sound forward with confidence and intent.

“I honestly feel like this album is the best we’ve ever done!” explains frontman Jonny Yerrell. "A lot of bands and artists like to change direction later in their careers, but that’s just not us. We absolutely love the style of music we make, the social commentary aspects and the people who turn up to jump around with us. Why would we change? Expect more, just bigger and better with a few surprises on the side! "

San Fran holds a Supervised License, meaning minors are welcome to attend events at San Fran so long as they are accompanied by a legal guardian at all times whilst at the venue. Minors are of course not allowed to purchase alcohol under any circumstance.

About the Liner Shipping Game

The Liner Shipping Game is a cutting-edge, simulation-based training solution that provides hands-on insights into the intricacies of liner shipping operations. It simplifies real-world processes, making it suitable for both industry newcomers and seasoned professionals.

Participants navigate realistic, customisable scenarios reflecting operational disruptions, key decision points, and challenges.

Key features include:

Booking Uptake: Manage dynamic booking requests while balancing capacity constraints and customer expectations.

Vessel Stowage: Plan and optimise vessel space, considering cargo types, weight distribution, and voyage schedules.

Terminal Operations: Coordinate port activities, manage container flows, and ensure efficient cargo handling.

The game's interactive nature provides practical experience and enhances skills in teamwork, revenue management, and process optimisation

.

For a closer look at the LinerGame experience, watch our official highlight video on YouTube.

Why Attend?

The Liner Shipping Game offers a rare opportunity to learn from top-tier industry experts while collaborating with peers from across the logistics sector. By attending, you will:

Understand Complex Operations: Experience the decision-making process of running a liner shipping service, covering end-to-end operations.

Enhance Your Skills: Improve your teamwork, strategic thinking, and revenue management capabilities in a fast-paced, risk-free environment.

Navigate Real-World Scenarios: Encounter challenges like port strikes, equipment shortages, weather disruptions, and overlapping booking regions, gaining critical insights into effective problem-solving.

Network with Industry Peers: Connect with like-minded professionals in a collaborative setting, exchange ideas, and explore new opportunities within the shipping and logistics sector.

Who Should Attend?

This workshop is ideal for:

Logistics & Supply Chain Professionals: Individuals involved in operations, planning, and management.

Importers & Exporters: Professionals managing supply chain activities and interested in gaining a broader understanding of liner shipping dynamics.

Freight Forwarders & Shippers: Those seeking to enhance their service offerings by understanding carrier operations better.

Port & Terminal Operators: Professionals responsible for terminal management and coordination.

Shipping Lines & Carriers: Executives and teams who want to refine their strategies and processes.

Due to overwhelming demand, The Pharcyde has been upgraded to Meow Nui!
All existing tickets remain valid. If you haven't grabbed yours yet, now's the time.
Few groups have had a greater impact on alternative hip hop than The Pharcyde.
Emerging from South Central Los Angeles in the early '90s, they rewrote the rules with their wit, originality and unmistakable chemistry, delivering two of the most influential albums of the era.
From the platinum-selling Bizarre Ride II the Pharcyde to the genre-defining Labcabincalifornia, classics like "Passin' Me By," "Runnin'," "Drop," "Otha Fish" and "Ya Mama" continue to inspire generations of artists and remain essential listening more than 30 years later.
The Pharcyde's legacy extends far beyond their own catalogue. They helped open the door for a more playful, soulful and inventive style of hip hop, collaborated with a then- emerging J Dilla, worked with visionary director Spike Jonze, and proved that creativity could be just as powerful as bravado. Their influence can still be heard across modern hip hop, while their timeless live show continues to win over audiences around the world.
Featuring Imani, Slimkid3, Fatlip and DJ Cee Brown, this is your chance to experience one of hip hop's defining groups live.
Secure your tickets early and don't miss the opportunity to see true pioneers of alternative hip hop when they return this December.

events.venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Former Haas F1 boss Guenther Steiner brings his new live show, ‘No Team Orders’, to The Opera House in Wellington. The 2026 season gave Formula 1 new cars, new rules, and new teams on the grid. Days after the final race, Guenther unpacks it all. He shares his take on which teams cracked the rule changes first and which young drivers stood out. Expect blunt opinions and stories from inside the paddock. 

Guenther has spent more than 30 years in motorsport. He started in rallying, working with drivers such as Colin McRae, a three-time Rally New Zealand winner. He later ran Jaguar Racing in Formula 1. Then he built the Haas team from scratch and led it for a decade. You might have seen him on the Netflix series ‘Formula 1: Drive to Survive’, where his colourful honesty made him a fan favourite. He famously claims he has never watched it. He has also written two books, ‘Surviving to Drive’ and ‘Unfiltered’. Today, he is CEO of the Red Bull KTM Tech3 MotoGP team. 

The evening is a live conversation on stage, followed by an audience Q&A. Bring a question of your own and put it to Guenther directly. Join whether you’ve just discovered him or you’ve followed Formula 1 since you were a wee one. Book your seats, and leave with enough insider secrets to impress at the work Christmas party.

events.venue: San Fran, Wellington
events.long_description:
UK psychedelic heavyweights Uncle Acid & The Deadbeats return to Australia and New Zealand this December, bringing their dark, hypnotic live show to stages across the country.
The brainchild of Kevin Starrs, Uncle Acid & The Deadbeats have spent over a decade carving out a singular space within the global heavy music landscape. Since emerging in 2009 from the depths of the British underground, the band have built a reputation for their unmistakable fusion of warped psychedelic pop, downer blues and doom-metal intensity.
Too bold and idiosyncratic to be easily defined, Uncle Acid’s sound is steeped in haunting melodies, layered vocal harmonies and eerie, cinematic arrangements, offset by crushing riffs and a persistent sense of unease. It’s a sonic world that feels both deeply nostalgic and completely otherworldly, cementing Uncle Acid & The Deadbeats as one of the most compelling live acts in contemporary rock.
With their last visit to our shores in 2020, Australian audiences can expect a set that traverses the band’s cult catalogue, delivered with the immersive intensity that has made them a must-see worldwide.

She’s known for her deadpan delivery and understated punchlines. Fan-favourite comedian Urzila Carlson is back in time for Christmas with a brand-new show — Fatty On a Yacht. Ever felt like you don’t belong? Like everyone else got the memo — and you turned up in the wrong outfit, on the wrong day, on the wrong yacht? According to Urzila, Fatty On a Yacht is for anyone who’s ever tried to squeeze into a space — physical or social — and thought, “This can’t be right”.

In 2025, she won the prestigious People’s Choice Award for most tickets sold at the Melbourne International Comedy Festival for an incredible fourth time, after wins in 2019, 2022 and 2023. In 2019, she was presented with the Rielly Comedy Award from the Variety Artists Club of New Zealand for her contribution to New Zealand entertainment.

Street party music!

Born in Otautahi, Yurt Party have spent the past few years riling up dancefloors around Aotearoa, playing backyards, clubs and festivals including Electric Avenue, CubaDupa, Twisted Frequency, Shipwrecked and Woodford Folk Festival (Aus).

Their high-energy instrumental music takes inspiration from Balkan, Latin and Dub. The tunes are made for dancing, leaving you with a smile on your face and sore legs in the morning!

Joined by DJ Everybody co-founder of festival circuit regulars 'Tempo Schmempo' collective with dynamic sets of house, techno, disco, and funk.

events.name: Jazz and Beyond Workshops 2026
events.venue: 91 Kelburn Parade, Kelburn, Wellington 6012, New Zealand  ·  Accessibility info
events.long_description:
Jazz and Beyond for students 19 and under

December 14–17, 2026

Coordinated by Chris Beernink, Dave Wilson, Daniel Hayles, Andrew Faleatua, Lance Philip. Proudly supported by the Tauranga Jazz Society.

Take it to the next level as a player or vocalist at the Jazz and Beyond Workshops! Young musicians from across Aotearoa come together to dive into jazz and connected styles, working closely with some of the country’s leading performers and educators. In a friendly, inclusive environment, you’ll grow your skills, make new musical connections, and learn alongside other students your age from all around the motu.

Here’s what’s in store:

small group ensembles led by professional musicians

developing improvisation skills in supportive settings

an introduction to music production

listening sessions that expand your skills

inclusive jam sessions where all are welcome

ensemble performances at the end of week concert

And more!

If you're 19 or under with at least a year of experience on your instrument or in vocal training, you’re welcome to join. Choose from trumpet, trombone, saxophone, clarinet, flute, bass, piano, guitar, drums, vibraphone, or voice.

The workshops are held at the New Zealand School of Music–Te Kōkī at Te Herenga Waka-Victoria University of Wellington. Follow the Jazz and Beyond Workshops on Instagram or Facebook for the latest updates. Email jazzandbeyondworkshops@gmail.com with any questions.

Schedule

The workshops run 9:00am-4:30pm Monday through Thursday, with evening activities including concerts and our inclusive jam sessions Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday. Students perform in a closing concert on Thursday afternoon.

Accommodation

Students arrange their own accommodation. Often students from outside Wellington stay together in groups with a parent chaperone. Options for housing near Victoria University of Wellington include backpacker hostels and hotels. If you have a group of 15 or more, University Student Housing may be an option. Email jazzandbeyondworkshops@gmail.com if you'd like to pursue this option.

Meals

Lunch for the four days is available for purchase at many convenient locations on campus, or students may bring their own lunch.

Equipment

Provided equipment includes drum kits, guitar and bass amps, pianos/keyboards, microphones and PAs for vocalists.

All brass and wind players should bring their own instruments.

Drummers: you are required to bring your own cymbals, sticks, and hi-hat clutch.

Guitarists and bass players: you are required to bring your own instruments as well as cables (leads).

Preparation

All students with one year of experience on an instrument or in vocal training have the skills required to participate, so no musical preparation is required. On the first day, students will play a very short audition to be placed in an appropriate ensemble. Guidelines for this short audition will be sent to all registered participants in advance of the workshops.

Cost

Early bird price: $325 - register before 19th October

Standard price $350 - on or after 19th October

Registration is open to all until all spots are filled.

We are dedicated to ensuring all students can participate in the workshops without financial constraints. If the cost poses a barrier, please email us at jazzandbeyondworkshops@gmail.com and we will find a solution to facilitate your participation!

SaaSmas Party — Wellington 2026

The calendar year is nearly done, the dashboards are probably still open, and your Q4 pipeline has either been heroic, character-building, or both. Either way, it’s time to down tools and come hang with the SaaS squad.

Join us for our SaaSmas Party in Wellington — a relaxed, mildly ridiculous, very well-earned night with the people building, scaling, funding, selling, marketing, supporting and generally holding together SaaS companies across Aotearoa.

Last year gave us a rock paper scissors competition involving the mayor, musical tree performances, and a human pyramid built from our kind sponsors. We’re not saying we’ll top that. We’re just saying the bar has been set in a deeply strange place.

Come along, bring a colleague, and help us wrap up the year properly. There’ll also be SaaSmas parties in Auckland and Christchurch, so if Wellington isn’t your local, keep an eye out for the one closest to you.

Date: Thursday 17 December 2026

Time: 5:00PM - 2:00AM

Location: Dockside bar, Wellington

Event Type: In Person

Cost: $30 for members & non-Members

Note: Festive energy encouraged. Human pyramids are not officially encouraged, but apparently not impossible!

events.long_description:
North Pole Express Kapiti: 10am - Saturday, 19 December 2026
Be whisked away on the North Pole Express to meet Santa, sing, and celebrate this special time of year.

About this Event


'Nice List' presale: 12pm, 25 June 2026 - 5pm, 1 July 2026. Password required.
Public sales commence 1 September 2026.
No tickets will be held during presale, any remaining tickets will be offered to the public from 12pm on 1 September 2026. To join the 'Nice List' visit the .
If you would like to purchase a private carriage for your group on this service, please email prior to 22 June 2026.



Join the magical journey to meet Santa!
Your tickets include:
Entertainers
Carolling
Iced cocoa
Cookies
Souvenir Mug
A special souvenir from Santa
Santa
Extra surprises along the way
Our Candy Class and Claus Class Guests travel in comfort and receive extra treats along the way.


Prepare to be surrounded by the magic and wonder of the Christmas season!
Families will love the magical train ride in one of our specially decorated carriages. You’ll meet Santa, sing, and celebrate this special time of year.
Set to the sounds of carols passengers are invited to join us to be whisked away on the North Pole Express. Delight in the magic of Christmas as the train departs for a journey to collect Santa who has been magically transported to an undisclosed location along the tracks.
From the distance the North Pole Express arrives then the train Conductors invite you and the other passengers to climb aboard shouting “All aboard!”.


All Aboard
During the first leg of the journey wide-eyed children of all ages are invited to engage with characters who are eager to hear what makes the Christmas season special to them.
You’ll meet the conductor, and join in the fun singing and dancing with your hosts and a few other characters who will appear in your carriage on the journey.
At the 'North Pole' Cocoa Class passengers enjoy their iced chocolate from their souvenir mug, and a delicious cookie served by our North Pole Express hosts. Candy and Claus Class passengers will be served aboard the train on the way to the North Pole.
Along the journey Santa appears in your carriage to present each passenger with their very own Christmas ornament. During the trip, characters in each carriage lead passengers in carolling and entertainment as the train makes its way back home.
Children UNDER 2 years (0-23 months) and travelling on the lap of an Adult are FREE. All Passengers 2 years old and over must hold a purchased ticket.

Please note: Seating in our Candy and Claus Classes is strictly limited. Candy and Claus Class Guests receive some extra surprises and treats along the way.
Seating in all carriages is arranged in a configuration of 4 seats as per normal train travel. North Pole Express always endeavour to ensure those who book more than 4 seats are seated in close proximity to each other to ensure they can enjoy the experience together. Children under the age of 2 and travelling on the lap of an adult travel for free.
Wheelchair access: Due to the age and design of the carriages it is not possible to board whist seated in a wheelchair as the entrance is stairs and the doorways are very narrow. However we will be pleased to convey passengers of limited mobility whenever possible provided they can step onto the train from the platform, climbing a step and move to their reserved seats with the help of an able bodied carer. Our crew would assist guiding the passenger up the step onto the train and arrange for the storage of the wheelchair in the guards van. The wheelchair must be able to be folded up and cannot be used on the train. Please let us know when booking if you need wheelchair assistance.

Photo credit: John Bovis

events.id: Astrophotography Masterclass: Capture the Southern Sky-Star Safari Observatory, 1169 Ponatahi Road, Carterton-Event Finder
events.name: Astrophotography Masterclass: Capture the Southern Sky
events.venue: Star Safari Observatory, 1169 Ponatahi Road, Carterton
events.long_description:
Spend an evening under one of the world’s finest dark skies and learn how to photograph the Milky Way, constellations and deep-sky objects. This immersive masterclass is designed for curious explorers, hobby photographers and anyone who has ever looked up and wished they could capture what they saw.

Your instructor is an experienced astro-educator, and you’ll be taken step by step through the art and science of night-sky photography with DSLR or mirrorless cameras. You’ll learn how to focus at infinity, choose the best camera settings, build compositions under the Milky Way, and work with RAW files, noise control and exposure strategy. You’ll photograph live star fields and leave with images you can genuinely be proud of.

No astronomy expertise or prior astrophotography experience is required — just your curiosity. Bring a camera and tripod if you have them, but if not, you can still attend, learn from telescope-linked imaging feeds, and gain the skills and confidence to shoot the cosmos on your own.

Held at Star Safari, right in the Wairarapa dark-sky heartlands, this experience takes place under the same southern skies recognised by Lonely Planet as one of the world’s top stargazing destinations. If you’ve ever wanted to try astrophotography, this is the moment, and this is the place.

What you’ll gain:
- Confidence to shoot the night sky
- Proven camera settings and workflow
- Real photos of the Milky Way and southern star fields
- Knowledge you can use anywhere the southern sky is visible
- A rare, premium learning experience under a world-class sky

Perfect for couples, travellers, creatives, astronomy lovers, and anyone who wants a deeper connection to the night.

Spaces are limited to keep the experience personal.
