North Pole Express Kapiti: 1pm - Sunday, 20 December 2026
Be whisked away on the North Pole Express to meet Santa, sing, and celebrate this special time of year.

About this Event


'Nice List' presale: 12pm, 25 June 2026 - 5pm, 1 July 2026. Password required.
Public sales commence 1 September 2026.
No tickets will be held during presale, any remaining tickets will be offered to the public from 12pm on 1 September 2026. To join the 'Nice List' visit the .
If you would like to purchase a private carriage for your group on this service, please email prior to 22 June 2026.



Join the magical journey to meet Santa!
Your tickets include:
Entertainers
Carolling
Iced cocoa
Cookies
Souvenir Mug
A special souvenir from Santa
Santa
Extra surprises along the way
Our Candy Class and Claus Class Guests travel in comfort and receive extra treats along the way.


Prepare to be surrounded by the magic and wonder of the Christmas season!
Families will love the magical train ride in one of our specially decorated carriages. You’ll meet Santa, sing, and celebrate this special time of year.
Set to the sounds of carols passengers are invited to join us to be whisked away on the North Pole Express. Delight in the magic of Christmas as the train departs for a journey to collect Santa who has been magically transported to an undisclosed location along the tracks.
From the distance the North Pole Express arrives then the train Conductors invite you and the other passengers to climb aboard shouting “All aboard!”.


All Aboard
During the first leg of the journey wide-eyed children of all ages are invited to engage with characters who are eager to hear what makes the Christmas season special to them.
You’ll meet the conductor, and join in the fun singing and dancing with your hosts and a few other characters who will appear in your carriage on the journey.
At the 'North Pole' Cocoa Class passengers enjoy their iced chocolate from their souvenir mug, and a delicious cookie served by our North Pole Express hosts. Candy and Claus Class passengers will be served aboard the train on the way to the North Pole.
Along the journey Santa appears in your carriage to present each passenger with their very own Christmas ornament. During the trip, characters in each carriage lead passengers in carolling and entertainment as the train makes its way back home.
Children UNDER 2 years (0-23 months) and travelling on the lap of an Adult are FREE. All Passengers 2 years old and over must hold a purchased ticket.

Please note: Seating in our Candy and Claus Classes is strictly limited. Candy and Claus Class Guests receive some extra surprises and treats along the way.
Seating in all carriages is arranged in a configuration of 4 seats as per normal train travel. North Pole Express always endeavour to ensure those who book more than 4 seats are seated in close proximity to each other to ensure they can enjoy the experience together. Children under the age of 2 and travelling on the lap of an adult travel for free.
Wheelchair access: Due to the age and design of the carriages it is not possible to board whist seated in a wheelchair as the entrance is stairs and the doorways are very narrow. However we will be pleased to convey passengers of limited mobility whenever possible provided they can step onto the train from the platform, climbing a step and move to their reserved seats with the help of an able bodied carer. Our crew would assist guiding the passenger up the step onto the train and arrange for the storage of the wheelchair in the guards van. The wheelchair must be able to be folded up and cannot be used on the train. Please let us know when booking if you need wheelchair assistance.

Photo credit: John Bovis

events.long_description:
Race Of Champions is an internationally renowned event. Winners from a range of racing disciplines go head-to-head on a purpose-built tarmac circuit constructed inside Hnry Stadium. Unlike traditional motorsport events, every driver competes in identical cars, putting the focus firmly on skill behind the wheel. 

The first drivers confirmed for Wellington include four-time Formula 1 World Champion Sebastian Vettel and Formula 1 race winner Valtteri Bottas. Supercars champion Chaz Mostert and New Zealand rally star Hayden Paddon are also coming. More competitors are to be announced for this Wellington exclusive event. 

Since its launch in 1988, Race Of Champions has brought together stars from Formula 1, World Rally Championship, IndyCar, NASCAR, Le Mans, and other top-tier racing series. Previous competitors have included Fernando Alonso, Lando Norris, Valentino Rossi, Mika Häkkinen, and Michael Schumacher.

events.name: GÓI BÁNH XUÂN 2027 | Vietnamese New Year Rice Cake Workshop

events.long_description:
GÓI BÁNH XUÂN 2027 | Vietnamese New Year Rice Cake Workshop
🧧 GÓI BÁNH XUÂN 2027 | VIETNAMESE NEW YEAR RICE CAKE WORKSHOP

🍃 Wrap a cake, share a story, and celebrate Vietnamese traditions together!

Tết không chỉ là dịp đón năm mới mà còn là lúc gia đình sum vầy, cùng nhau gìn giữ và trao truyền những nét đẹp văn hoá Việt Nam.

Have you ever wondered how traditional Vietnamese rice cakes are made? Or perhaps you miss the familiar feeling of preparing bánh chưng and bánh tét with your family back home?

Join Viet Hub NZ for a hands-on cultural cooking workshop where we come together to discover the stories, traditions and flavours of Vietnamese Lunar New Year.

🌸 WHAT WILL WE EXPLORE?

🍃 Bánh Chưng – Traditional square sticky rice cake, symbolising the Earth and gratitude to our ancestors.

🍃 Bánh Tét – A cylindrical sticky rice cake commonly enjoyed during Tết, particularly in Southern Vietnam.

🍃 Bánh Ú – A pyramid-shaped sticky rice cake wrapped in leaves, representing another beautiful part of Vietnamese culinary heritage.

During the workshop, you will:

🌱 Discover the cultural stories and meanings behind traditional Vietnamese rice cakes.

🌱 Learn about ingredients and traditional wrapping techniques.

🌱 Enjoy a hands-on experience guided by our facilitator, Yung Nguyen.

🌱 Connect with families, friends and community members through food and storytelling.

🌱 Create meaningful memories while helping pass Vietnamese traditions to the next generation.

No cooking experience needed! Whether you're Vietnamese, have children curious about their heritage, or simply love exploring different cultures, everyone is welcome.

📅 EVENT DETAILS

Date: Saturday, 16 January 2027

Venue: Te Mako Naenae Community Centre, Lower Hutt

Facilitator: Yung Nguyen

Organiser: Viet Hub NZ

🎟️ Spaces are limited. Registration is essential.

💛 MORE THAN JUST A COOKING WORKSHOP

For many Vietnamese families living overseas, the scent of sticky rice, the sound of leaves being folded and the joy of preparing food together bring back precious memories of home.

For our younger generation, this is an opportunity to discover where they come from, connect with their roots and create their own Tết memories.

And for our wider New Zealand community, it's an invitation to experience the warmth, stories and traditions of Vietnamese culture.

Because traditions are not only something we remember. They are something we share, practise and pass on.

Come wrap a cake, share a story and welcome Tết 2027 with us! 🧧

Viet Hub NZ | Registered Charity CC64272

Uplifting Culture. Creating Opportunity. Empowering People. Together.

events.long_description:
Tora Bombora - 2027
The Return of Tora Bombora.

Wellington Anniversary Weekend, 22 - 24 January, 2027

After five incredible festivals and a four year hiatus, Tora Bombora is returning for the sixth edition - Tora Bombora Ono

For four summers, the paddocks sat quietly. The stages slept, the winds kept moving across the hills, and the coast returned to its familiar rhythm. But some things never really leave. They simply wait.

————————————————————

Ticket System and Key Dates

'Tora Bombora Whānau'
To keep the community close and the kaupapa even closer, if you have attended Tora Bombora in the past, you are already 'Tora Bombora Whānau' which gives you first access to tickets (keep an eye on your inbox). The remaining tickets will be released to people who sign up via our website to become a part of the 'Tora Bombora Whānau'.

How it works
1. Enter 'Tora Bombora Whānau': Sign up to the Tora Bombora waiting list and join the whānau before the link closes.
Link opens Monday, 6th July.
Link closes Sunday, 9th August.

2. Keep an eye on your inbox: Once the link has closed, you'll receive an email with a 'Tora Bombora Whānau' access code that gives you access to purchase tickets to Tora Bombora before they are released to the general public. Each whānau member may purchase up to four tickets.
Whānau ticket access and lineup out 10th August

3. General ticket release
Tuesday, 11th August - If any tickets remain after the whānau link has been sent out, they will be released in a public sale.

If this sounds like your kind of gig, put your name in the hat. The coast will do the rest.
All other info can be found at www.torabombora.co.nz

————————————————————

CAMPING: This is included in your ticket price. The festival begins at 3.00 pm Friday the 20th Jan. The camping zone will be situated on-site, right on the Pacific Ocean where you can swim, fish, surf, play and chill out.

FOOD AND SHOPS: Tora is isolated. This means no shops for 45 minutes so please make sure you bring more than enough food and gear as Martinborough is the nearest town. There will be plenty of food trucks at the event.

————————————————————

Festival Terms & Conditions:

*THIS IS AN R18 EVENT & RIGHT OF ADMISSION IS RESERVED.

**WASTE POLICY IS BRING YOUR OWN, TAKE YOUR OWN.

————————————————————

LOCATION

313 Te Awaiti Road, Tora Beach, Martinborough, South Wairarapa, Wellington, 5782

Drive time from Wellington: 2 hours 15mins.

SUMMER MELTDOWN - We're set to ignite your summer with an unforgettable fusion of sound, energy, and culture.

﻿

Bringing you a powerhouse lineup featuring Aotearoa's most iconic artists, SIX60, Katchafire, The Black Seeds, Troy Kingi, Ria Hall and Tiki Taane. This is the moment music fans have been waiting for - and the countdown to one of summer's biggest festivals starts right now!

﻿

TICKET DATES

Pre-sale: Thursday 10th Sept, 8am

Public Sale: Friday 11th Sept, 8am

﻿

SIX60

Returning to Wellington for the first time in 2 years to headline Summer Meltdown, SIX60's story has always felt larger than life, and their music even more so. What began as Dunedin flatmates jamming for fun has evolved into a sound that's unmistakably their own. Get ready for a full-scale spectacle of inescapable anthems.




KATCHAFIRE

Katchafire's journey from the mighty H-Town to the world stage is rooted in pure Māori pride and classic reggae spirit. Blending vibrant rhythms and uplifting grooves with cultural depth, Katchafire bring an authentic, soul-soaked reggae experience to Summer Meltdown.

Returning to their Wellington roots, The Black Seeds bring their reputation for irresistible grooves, signature warmth, rhythm and world-class energy to the Summer Meltdown stage with a live show that hits with big-beat funk, dub, soul and roots-reggae.

TROY KINGI

One of Aoteraroa's most creative artists, Troy Kingi's 10/10/10 project - ten albums, ten genres, ten years - has earned major accolades and cemented his position as a fearless creative force. Performing with his live band, The Cactus Handshake, Kingi brings a genre-shifting, bold and boundary-defying show to Brewtown.

A powerful live performer shaped by kapa haka and dedicated to elevating te reo Māori, Ria delivers a fierce and deeply soulful set.

events.long_description:
A recent review by 13thfloor.co.nz of a Pachyman set at Whammy celebrated the way Pachy used his magic sound to "immediately create a space nobody wanted to leave". We didn't want him to leave either, so we're bringing him back to Aotearoa this January. On Sunday 24 January he takes over Pōneke's hallowed San Fran for a double header with Trans-Tasman supergroup The Lahaar.

Over four albums, Pachyman has proven himself a dedicated craftsman in the lineage of dub reggae. He has mastered the methods of King Tubby and Scientist: vintage gear, glorious walls of sound, and an intuitive grasp of the power of repetition. Since his triumphant last visit in early 2025, Pachy "Pachyman" Garcia has released what critics are calling his most adventurous record yet, the dubtastic Another Place. On it he brings together the many scenes that have recontextualised dub, from the synth-pop of William Onyeabor and Yellow Magic Orchestra to Basic Channel's amniotic dub techno. With even stronger Latin flavours running through his sublime Lovers Rock and Studio One-inspired sounds, this will be a supercharged version of the Pachyman shows we've seen before.

Standing toe to toe with him are The Lahaar. The band brings together some of the brightest lights of the Australian and New Zealand jazz and electronic soul scenes: Julien Dyne, Horatio Luna and Lachlan Stuckey (Surprise Chef), and a revolving cast featuring members of Fat Freddy's Drop, The Circling Sun and Avantdale Bowling Club. Their self-titled debut on the UK's Soundway Records draws on late-'70s New York proto-rap disco instrumentals, Nigerian boogie, Jamaican dub and vintage cop-movie funk. Live, they're a full-blown big band of horns, flutes, vibraphone and congas, moving from high-energy percussive dance-floor heat into deep, meditative dub. It's the perfect match for Pachy's dubwise science.

Two headline acts and one very big night. Don't sleep on it.

"Pachyman is not to be slept on" – Aquarium Drunkard

events.long_description:
He’s been referred to as the God of the comic essay. Author David Sedaris is a savant of sardonic wit. Wellington gets to experience his razor-sharp sense of humour when he visits to promote his latest book - ‘The Land and Its People’. David will take to the stage to read from the collection of essays and freshly minted diary entries. This will be followed by a candid audience Q&A session and an extended book signing that — true to form — will run as long as it needs to.   
In ‘The Land and Its People’ he reflects on what it means to be a foreigner, a brother, and a lifelong friend — trying on the role of caretaker after his partner Hugh’s hip-replacement surgery. Equal parts tender and devastating, it’s classic Sedaris: the kind of writing that makes you laugh until you feel guilty, then laugh again anyway. It has been said that listening to him read is an affirming, joyful experience that leaves a person feeling as if their cup has been filled right to the brim.

Granted furlough from the gulag, Daft Rocket is crossing the ditch in 2027 and heading to Auckland for the first time with riffs in tow. His first trip Down Under was a sold out scorcher across Sydney, Brisbane, and Melbourne in 2025. Now, The Boy Who Riffed is bringing his frenetic, spellbound optimism to the information chamber of this haunted planet we call home. This month-long trek will span 17 shows across 11 cities throughout Australia and New Zealand - creating a rift in the space time continuum that may take decades to amend. Mostly improvised, rarely sanctified, and remarkably canonized, this mercurial hour of standup comedy is sure to bring families together around a yule log of proficient proletariat rhetoric that neither holds firm a universal truth or chooses to establish a solid foundation as to the nature of words in general. Ultimately: it's riffing, it's good for us, and we're just as happy with a good book - we shudder to consider it any other way.

Casey Rocket: As Above, So Down Under - Wellington Granted furlough from the gulag, Daft Rocket is crossing the ditch in 2027 and returning to The Lucky Country with riffs in tow.
After a sold out scorcher across Sydney, Brisbane, and Melbourne in 2025, The Boy Who Riffed is bringing his frenetic, spellbound optimism to the information chamber of this haunted planet we call home.
This month-long trek will span 17 shows across 11 cities throughout Australia and New Zealand - creating a rift in the space time continuum that may take decades to amend.
Mostly improvised, rarely sanctified, and remarkably canonized, this mercurial hour of standup comedy is sure to bring families together around a yule log of proficient proletariat rhetoric that neither holds firm a universal truth or chooses to establish a solid foundation as to the nature of words in general.
Ultimately: it's riffing, it's good for us, and we're just as happy with a good book - we shudder to consider it any other way.

events.long_description:
Presented by: SBM
Propagandhi will make their long-awaited return to Australia and Aotearoa in early 2027, marking their first shows in the region in nearly eight years.
The ever-evolving standard-bearers of politically charged punk have actively kicked against musical confines and bro-punk conservatism, promoting a message of anti-fascism since 1986. Distilling their DNA of breakneck riffs, hardcore ethos, and radical consciousness, their message remains as vital, and volatile, as ever.
The tour comes in support of the Manitoba, Canada-based outfit’s eighth album, *At Peace*. In true Propagandhi fashion, it’s smart music for dangerous times. “Everything I’m singing about is still coming from being the same person that wrote and sang our first record *How to Clean Everything* in 1993,” Chris Hannah states, recalling the band’s snarky skate-thrash origins.
“But what we’re putting into the songs now, probably reflects more despair than 30 years ago when we had similar perspectives, but with strands of hope and naivete. Now it’s the existential dread of eking out a life worth living in this completely failed society.”
Propagandhi are set to bring their incendiary live show back to Australia and Aotearoa, drawing from a body of work that continues to challenge, confront, and inspire.
New album "At Peace" out now Propagandhi.com

events.long_description:
If you‘ve ever said “I‘m a feminist but...”, The Guilty Feminist Podcast: Live is for you. Host and comedian Deborah Frances-White returns to Wellington with her new series, ‘The Road to Gilead Project‘. Settle into a seat at The Opera House to watch a podcast happen live on stage. In this series, Deborah talks with comedians, artists, authors, academics, and activists. Expect equal parts comedy and deep-dive discussion. 

The Road to Gilead Project takes its name from Gilead, the nightmare state from Margaret Atwood‘s ‘The Handmaid‘s Tale‘. Deborah thinks some of today‘s headlines are starting to read a lot like the book. Around the world, hard-won rights for women and LGBTQ+ communities are being challenged. So how do you get off the road to Gilead? Deborah‘s answer is a joyful resistance, with plenty of laughs along the way. 

Since 2015, Deborah has turned the fear of being a ‘bad feminist’ into a multi-award-winning podcast with more than 200 million downloads. Guests confess the gap between their principles and their everyday habits. Nobody is perfect, and that‘s the point. Come along to experience everything you love about The Guilty Feminist, with a new focus.

events.long_description:
Following the sell-out success of their European summer tour, System Of A Down is heading to Hnry Stadium for its only New Zealand concert. Wellington audiences will also be entertained by warm up act and alternative rock icons Faith No More. 
This concert marks System of a Down's first Wellington show, and their first time playing in Aotearoa in more than a decade. Blending metal with diverse influences including jazz, opera, and Armenian folk, System Of A Down have sold more than 42 million albums worldwide. They released their debut self-titled album in 1998, but it was not until the release of 'Toxicity' in 2001 that their popularity exploded. Heavy music fans can expect a massive career-spanning set filled with the songs that have defined the genre for more than 25 years.
It's been a long time between Wellington shows for Faith No More. The last time the San Francisco-based band played in the capital was 1997. Responsible for such classics as Epic, Midlife Crisis, and a distinctive cover of The Commodores' Easy, they've developed a die-hard following over the last 40 years. 
Together the bands will bring decades of hard rock (and its fans) to Wellington for what promises to be one of the most electrifying nights of heavy music the city's ever seen.

events.venue: Valhalla, Wellington
events.long_description:
KYLESA have announced their return to Australia and New Zealand. After more than a decade away, the legendary American group brings their iconic blend of stoner rock, psych, sludge, metal and punk to venues across Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Auckland & Wellington.

Tickets here

Kylesa is a force of nature, a band whose sonic range and primal heaviness stunned & awed listeners for 15 years before they went dark in 2016. Formed in Savannah, Georgia in 2001, the group made their name with a series of EPs and records and relentless touring schedule. They gained a legion of fans from all over the world and dipped their toes into several different scenes as “Stoner Metal” or “Psych Metal / Indie Sludge” wasn’t necessarily on the menu. Pulling from indie rock, punk, classic heavy metal, doom, death, psychedelic and kraut rock, the band really sound like no one else.

Journalist David Peisner of Spin described them as dark psych-metal titans, practicing an aggressive, but hazy, stoner vibe...a strange amalgamation of Black Sabbath, Black Flag and early Pink Floyd.
Lead by guitar and vocal duo Laura Pleasants and Phillip Cope, Kylesa have picked up where they left off with a legendary new rhythm section in tow featuring Roy Mayorga ( Nausea, Soulfly, Stone Sour, Ministry, Jerry Cantrell ) & John John Jesse ( Nausea) rounding out the lineup.

Kylesa cemented their place as key figures in creating the Georgia metal scene by bringing forth a unique, unmatched, experimental wall of sound that is as relevant today as it was at the time.

They returned to perform at the 2025 Roadburn Festival, followed by announcements from ArcTanGent Festival, Inferno Fest and A Colossal Weekend. Since then they have made selective appearances at festivals and theatres across the globe and will finally descend on Australian and New Zealand shores in February 2027.

events.long_description:
For the first time in an ever evolving 21 year history, the explosive and genre defying French act IGORRR at last cast their unclassifiable magic across Aotearoa, New Zealand. Created and spearheaded by French multi-instrumentalist Gautier Serre, the IGORRR name has expanded from one man's pseudonym to become a full group identity, which has brought a new level of intensity into the live representations.

Initially influenced by the likes of Meshuggah, Chopin, Cannibal Corpse, Bach, Domenico Scarlatti, Taraf De Haidouks And Aphex Twin, traces of these artists can be found littered across IGORRR's discography, but Serre has never been interested in remaining static or merely recycling ideas, and his work has dramatically evolved accordingly. With a truly unique sound blending a multitude of complex layers, Serre excudes total musical freedom by combining all of his disparate tastes into one chaotic, cohesive universe.

ONE SHOW ONLY

events.long_description:
A blend of Irish-language rap and sharp social commentary has built an international following for Kneecap . The hip-hop trio, made up of Mo Chara, Móglaí Bap, and DJ Próvaí, made a name for itself with raucous live performances. Formed in Belfast in 2017, Kneecap’s popularity skyrocketed following the release of the 2024 biographical film ‘Kneecap’ in which the group’s members each played themselves. Their previous visit to Wellington in 2025 was described by The Post as “explosive”, with the crowd eating out of the palm of their hand from the moment they took the stage. 

That tour was followed in 2026 by the release of third album ‘Fenian’ which has seen the group expand its sound to something darker and even more controversial. The trio will be joined in Wellington’s TSB Arena in February by Aotearoa’s own DJ, producer, and artist Lady Shaka. Expect a night of high-energy hip-hop, razor-sharp lyrics, and one of the most talked-about live shows on the touring circuit.

events.name: Awakening the Subtle Body with Joan Hyman
events.venue: Level 1/175 Vivian Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
About the training

This immersive training invites you to awaken the subtle body through the practice of yoga. The subtle body is the energetic field that connects body, breath and mind.

Over the course of this 3-day training, we explore how movement, breath and awareness shape the flow of prana. Through asana, pranayama and meditation, you will deepen your connection to the more subtle layers of your practice and refine how you move, breathe and sequence with intention.

What you will explore

The foundations of yoga energetics including prana, nadis, bandhas and chakras

the relationship between physical alignment and the energetic flow

Sequencing as a tool to guide prana through the body

Pranayama and meditation as gateways to the subtle body

Safe and intelligent progressions toward more advanced postures

Any questions? Head to our FAQ at the bottom of the page.

SCHEDULE

The training is 3 full days with each day designed to lead on to the next. Lunch break is from 12-1:30pm.

Friday 9am - 4pm - Sequencing towards arm balances

We explore sequencing as a roadmap for practice and learn how arm balances support lightness, strength and flow. Themes include prana, the five koshas, bandhas and biomechanics as a gateway to the subtle body. The day ends with pranayama practice.

Saturday 9am - 4pm - Sequencing towards inversions and inner body awareness

A deeper exploration of inversions and their effect on the inner body. We study the nadis and sushumna and how sequencing supports inward awareness. The day closes with restorative postures and meditation.

Sunday 9am - 3:30pm - Sequencing for backbends and subtle body integration

Backbends to uplift prana and access the more subtle layers of practice. We will explore the chakras as the most refined energetic layer and integrate everything through sequencing, meditation, and pranayama. A quiet inward ending to conclude the training.

THE VENUE: BHAKTI LOUNGE

The Bhakti Lounge is located in the heart of Wellington CBD, at level 1, 175 Vivian Street. It has been operating for twenty plus years and is 100% volunteer-run, community first events space.

YOUR TEACHER

Joan Hyman, Senior Yoga Teacher and founder of the School of Yoga (USA)

Joan Hyman is the director and founder of The School of Yoga, an authentic international teacher training program focused on continuing education. Her grounded teaching style seamlessly supports her students as they emerge from their practice with the rich and bright energy that yoga has to offer.

Joan’s teachings come from an organic and intuitive place, as she draws upon the combined studies of Ashtanga and Iyengar yoga as well as Ayurveda and meditation. An authentic modern-day yogi, Joan's love and devotion show up in her practice and throughout her teaching. You will leave her class feeling transformed and deeply aligned.

Joan spent fifteen years as a distinguished YogaWorks Senior Teacher before bringing her expertise to Wanderlust as the Director of Teacher Trainings in 2016. Now, with over twenty years of experience leading retreats, trainings, and international workshops, Joan travels the globe and teaches online, leading her own signature trainings. She has created The School of Yoga, which is a professional education program, helping students and inspiring teachers to work towards their five hundred hours Yoga Alliance Certification. A leader in the yoga community, Joan’s open-hearted approach to teaching yoga keeps both her inner spirit and her students continuously evolving.

YOUR HOSTS

Sarah Marriott and Liz Birkett

Yoga teachers (500YTT) Sarah Marriott and Liz Birkett warmly welcome you! Having studied with Joan Hyman since 2018, they are excited to bring her to Wellington shores once again, so she can share her extensive knowledge of Yoga with Aotearoa's Yoga community. 

FAQ

How much is the 3 day training?

It is $520 (early bird) however this increases to $550 from November 1st, 2026.

Can I attend one or two days?

Sorry, no. This is a 3 day training with each day designed to lead on to the next. Please email Sarah and Liz if you have further questions about this.

Who is this training for?

This training is for dedicated practitioners and teachers who feel curious about the energetics behind the physical practice and who want to deepen their experience beyond alignment alone. This training is open to teachers and dedicated yoga practitioners. You do not need to be a teacher to join. A regular yoga practice and curiosity to dive deeper is enough!

Do I need to bring a yoga mat or any props?

We have mats, and props (blocks, straps bolsters) however you are welcome to bring your own.

Is there parking at the venue?

Street parking:
Best option is to Uber or car pool if you can as street parking is capped at 2 hours (around $5 per hour) during the week and 3 hours (around $3/4) in the weekend.

Car parks:
The Hope Gibbons Parking (68 Taranaki Street) is a 2-3 minute walk from the venue or there are other parking buildings 5 minutes away (E.g., Garrett Street Car Park)

What are the lunch options?

Of course you are welcome to bring your own lunch/snacks. However, there are plenty of cafes and restaurants available to you on nearby Cuba street. You have 1.5 hours for lunch so you may like to dine in, take a drive or head to Oriental Pde for a walk!

The Bhakti lounge also serves a delicious plant-based lunch Mon-Fri at a very affordable price.

I'm from out of town. Is there accommodation nearby?

Yes there are plenty of options just a short walk away.

https://sojournhotels.co.nz/
https://www.themarionhostel.com/

events.long_description:
Homegrown Wellington band Drax Project are booked for a very special gig — the grand reopening of Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall. After a 13 year hiatus, the building is back online and who better to christen it than a local band with an international reputation? 
Drax Project fuses pop, R&B, hip-hop, and jazz. They formed in 2014 after meeting in Wellington (members studied Jazz Performance at Victoria University and Whitireia Polytech). After capturing local audiences busking on the streets, they launched a professional career. Since then, they’ve released two albums, toured extensively, and opened for global heavyweights Christina Aguilera, Ed Sheeran, and Camila Cabello. 
Joining Drax Project on the bill is one of the city’s most beloved artists. Oscar-winning Bret McKenzie will open the evening alongside his eight-piece Wellington-based band, The State Highway Wonders. 
When Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall officially reopens in February, it will be 13 years since the iconic venue closed for refurbishment and strengthening. This landmark concert, full of Wellington talent, is the perfect way to honour the city’s rich cultural and musical legacy.

events.name: Gillian Welch & David Rawlings
events.venue: Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
The traditional sound of Appalachian music. bluegrass, country, Americana, and folk will fill the Michael Fowler Centre in February. American singer-songwriters Gillian Welch and David Rawlings blend the traditional music practices together in their first New Zealand concert in over a decade. The partners on stage and in life have 30 years of experience collaborating over haunting covers of folk greats. You might hear songs like Look at Miss Ohio, Orphan Girl, and Empty Trainload of Sky. Expect sparse magical arrangements and exquisite lyricism. 

Since their last visit to Wellington, they've been busy writing and producing music. Their recent album, ‘Woodland’, is the first attributed to both of them. Despite collaborating on most things, previous albums were billed individually. The album shares the name of their Nashville studio Woodland, lost to a tornado in 2020. 

You might recognise Gillian’s voice from the Coen brothers film ‘O Brother, Where Art Thou?’. She contributed to the soundtrack and snuck into the film itself. David is also a record producer and fronts the band Dave Rawlings Machine. Together, the pair are winners of multiple Grammy Awards and a slew of other accolades.

events.long_description:
Drax Project and Friends | Town Hall, WELLINGTON
DRAX PROJECT TO HEADLINE GRAND REOPENING OF
TE WHARE WHAKARAUIKA WELLINGTON TOWN HALL SATURDAY 20 FEBRUARY 2027

Hometown heroes Drax Project are set to make history as the first act to perform at Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall when the doors officially reopen on Saturday 20 February 2027, marking the first event in the iconic venue since its closure for refurbishment 13 years ago.

The landmark concert will honour Wellington’s rich cultural and musical legacy, with Drax Project returning to the city where they first captivated audiences as buskers on central Wellington’s streets, before launching a career that would see them become one of New Zealand’s most successful acts.
Joining them on the bill is one of the city’s most beloved global names, Bret McKenzie, who will open the evening alongside his
eight-piece Wellington-based band, The State Highway Wonders.

Tickets go on sale at midday Friday 19 June from ticketmaster.co.nz

The show will also feature a host of surprise special guests throughout the night, including some of Drax Project’s favourite collaborators, inspirations and friends, creating a uniquely Wellington occasion and a celebration of the wider New Zealand
music whānau.

For Drax Project, being invited to reopen the historic 122-year-old building is a true full-circle moment as they explain
“This is going to be a very special gig for us! We all met while at uni here and Wellington is where we got our start. The Town Hall closed before Drax became a thing, but playing there is something we've always dreamt of doing as a band.”

Since emerging from Wellington’s busking scene, Drax Project have built an international career that has seen them amass nearly a billion streams resulting in 34 Platinum certifications globally. Renowned for their live show, they have toured extensively across the world including sharing stages with Ed Sheeran, Christina
Aguilera, Camilla Cabello and George Clinton. Though their music has sustained international success, Wellington remains at the heart of the band's story, making their return to reopen one of the capital’s most treasured venues a fitting homecoming.

Don’t miss your chance to be a part of this historic night. Tickets go on sale midday Friday 19 June from ticketmaster.co.nz

events.name: Shen Yun
events.venue: St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Picture fairies drifting out of clouds and generals charging into battle. Now add tight choreography and a live orchestra. Shen Yun is coming to Wellington’s St James Theatre in February. Bring your kids along to this family-friendly show. It celebrates thousands of years of Chinese culture through classical dance and music. Dreamy scenery and costumes frame every piece. 

The orchestra blends Western symphonic and traditional Chinese instruments. These include the erhu and pipa. You don’t need to swot up about China beforehand. Bilingual emcees introduce each piece, and song lyrics are translated on the backdrop. 

The two-hour show packs in 20 pieces. One moment, you’re experiencing a legend. The next, you’re in a new region or dynasty. Mongolians ride horseback across the grasslands and generals show off their battlefield heroics. You’ll also see the philosophical works of Lao-Tzu and glimpses of heavenly realms. The stories are ancient legends of love, loss, and humour. 

Each year, eight companies, with 500 artists, perform the production across 20 countries. Every season is brand new, from the dances and music to the costumes, stories, and backdrops. Academy Award-winning actor Cate Blanchett called it “exquisitely beautiful”. Come and find out if you agree with her.

The world’s longest-running classical crossover act celebrates 30 years of magnificent singing. The music ensemble The Ten Tenors was formed in 1995. Since then, they have toured over 3,500 shows across 34 countries. Their signature brand of music featuring 10-part harmonies has been enjoyed by more than 100 million people worldwide. 

The Ten Tenors have become renowned for their dynamic, choreographed performances. Their skilful technique lets them transition seamlessly between operatic arias, soulful ballads, chart-topping pop, and rock songs. They have shared the stage with iconic artists including Lionel Richie, Rod Stewart, Andrea Bocelli, Willie Nelson, Alanis Morissette and Christina Aguilera. They have also appeared extensively on TV. 

Following a four-year hiatus, The Ten Tenors make a grand return to New Zealand in March. The breathtaking 30th anniversary show will feature their signature 10-part vocal harmonies.

In February 2027, DEL AMITRI return to Australia with Past to Present: Four Decades of Their Greatest Hits a celebratory tour showcasing the songs that defined their remarkable career, from early indie beginnings to international chart success.
Formed in Glasgow in 1982 by Justin Currie, Del Amitri found their long term creative backbone in guitarist Iain Harvie, whose presence has been central to the band’s sound for decades. Their breakthrough came with the 1989 album Waking Hours, featuring the enduring hit ‘Nothing Ever Happens’ and the deliciously catchy ‘Kiss This Thing Goodbye.’ The early ’90s brought further global recognition with ‘Always the Last to Know’ and their biggest US success, ‘Roll to Me,’ which reached Number 10 on the Billboard Hot 100 and remains a worldwide jukebox favourite.
Across seven studio albums, Del Amitri have sold over six million records, earning a reputation for sharp songwriting, wry lyricism and melodic, emotionally resonant rock that continues to connect across generations.
After a hiatus in the 2000s, the band returned for sold out reunion tours and, in 2021, released Fatal Mistakes, their first collection of new music in 18 years, reaffirming their signature sound for both long time fans and new listeners. Del Amitri are currently in the studio recording their new album which is set for a release later this year.
In 2027, the band celebrates their legacy with a powerful, career spanning Australian tour Past to Present: Four Decades of Their Greatest Hits.

events.long_description:
Formed in Sheffield in 1980, the band ABC brought a mix of new romantic, post-punk, and disco-funk to dancefloors. Now, 45 years since they began, they're making their way to New Zealand. Expect a set packed with sharp suits, polished pop, and some of the band’s best-known tracks. 
Charismatic singer Martin Fry fronts ABC. He's likely to serenade you with many of the band's favourites including The Look Of Love, Poison Arrow, All Of My Heart, and When Smokey Sings. All of them made it into the top 20 hits in the New Zealand music charts at the time. ABC’s debut album, ‘The Lexicon Of Love’, reached number one in New Zealand for three weeks and stayed in the album chart for 33 weeks. Even after all this time the songs still draw people to the floor to dance.

His stand-up show ‘Here If You Need Me’ will have the audience at the Michael Fowler Centre laughing heartily. Kevin’s observational comedy has drawn more than two million fans across the globe. events.long_description:
The Great Kāpiti Race 2027
🏁 THE GREAT KĀPITI RACE – SUNDAY 7 MARCH 2027 🏁

Kāpiti… THE RACE IS ON!

Grab your team and get ready for a day of clues, challenges, puzzles, mystery locations and probably a fair bit of ridiculousness as you make your way around the Kāpiti Coast.

Think adventure race meets treasure hunt — but this is NOT a fitness race! You don't need to be super fit, fast or particularly coordinated 😂 You just need a team that's ready to have some fun.

🗺️ HOW WILL IT WORK?
You'll start the day at our official starting point, where your team will receive your first clue.
Solve it correctly and it'll lead you to your next location somewhere around Kāpiti.

When you arrive, you might need to:
🧩 Solve a puzzle
🎯 Complete a challenge
🔎 Find something hidden
📸 Take a photo or video
🤪 Do something completely ridiculous
📍 Check in at a local business or location
🗺️ Work out where your next clue is sending you

Complete it and you're onto the next one!

Expect to discover local businesses, attractions, parks, sports facilities and places around Kāpiti you may never have visited before.

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 WHO CAN ENTER?
Teams will be 2–5 people and kids are absolutely welcome!
This is designed to be something families, couples, friends and workmates can all do.

You will need your own vehicle to travel between some checkpoints, and at least one team member will need to be an adult.

📅 THE IMPORTANT STUFF
DATE: Sunday 7 March 2027
TIME: Approximately 10am–4pm
LOCATION: All around the Kāpiti Coast
TEAM SIZE: 2–5 people

🏆 AND YES… THERE WILL BE PRIZES!
We'll have major prizes, spot prizes and plenty of opportunities to win things throughout the day.
And winning won't necessarily just be about being the fastest. 👀

events.long_description:
👑 ਮਹਾਰਾਣੀ ਜਿੰਦਾਂ — ਪੰਜਾਬ ਦੀ ਆਖ਼ਰੀ ਮਹਾਰਾਣੀ 👑 Maharani Jindan- The Last Queen of Punjab
👑 ਮਹਾਰਾਣੀ ਜਿੰਦਾਂ — ਪੰਜਾਬ ਦੀ ਆਖ਼ਰੀ ਮਹਾਰਾਣੀ 👑
🔥 ਇੱਕ ਸ਼ੇਰਨੀ ਦੀ ਕਹਾਣੀ… ਜਿਸਨੂੰ ਇਤਿਹਾਸ ਕਦੇ ਭੁਲਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਸਕਦਾ! 🔥

ਉਹ ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਇੱਕ ਮਹਾਰਾਣੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਸੀ…
ਉਹ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਦੀ ਧੀ, ਇੱਕ ਮਾਂ, ਇੱਕ ਯੋਧਾ ਅਤੇ ਹੌਸਲੇ ਦੀ ਮਿਸਾਲ ਸੀ। ❤️

ਜਦੋਂ ਹਾਲਾਤਾਂ ਨੇ ਉਸਨੂੰ ਝੁਕਾਉਣ ਦੀ ਕੋਸ਼ਿਸ਼ ਕੀਤੀ, ਉਹ ਹੋਰ ਮਜ਼ਬੂਤ ਹੋ ਕੇ ਖੜ੍ਹੀ ਹੋਈ।
ਜਦੋਂ ਉਸ ਤੋਂ ਉਸਦਾ ਪੁੱਤਰ, ਉਸਦਾ ਰਾਜ ਅਤੇ ਉਸਦੀ ਆਜ਼ਾਦੀ ਦੂਰ ਕੀਤੀ ਗਈ, ਫਿਰ ਵੀ ਉਸਦੇ ਦਿਲ ਵਿੱਚੋਂ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਲਈ ਪਿਆਰ ਅਤੇ ਸੰਘਰਸ਼ ਦੀ ਅੱਗ ਨਹੀਂ ਬੁਝੀ।

⚔️ ਮਹਾਰਾਣੀ ਜਿੰਦ ਕੌਰ — ਸ਼ੇਰ-ਏ-ਪੰਜਾਬ ਮਹਾਰਾਜਾ ਰਣਜੀਤ ਸਿੰਘ ਦੀ ਮਹਾਰਾਣੀ ਅਤੇ ਮਹਾਰਾਜਾ ਦਲੀਪ ਸਿੰਘ ਦੀ ਮਾਤਾ — ਦੀ ਇਹ ਗਾਥਾ ਸਾਡੀ ਆਉਣ ਵਾਲੀ ਪੀੜ੍ਹੀ ਤੱਕ ਪਹੁੰਚਣੀ ਚਾਹੀਦੀ ਹੈ।

🎭 Rang Manch Karee Theatre Group Melbourne ਵੱਲੋਂ ਮਹਾਰਾਣੀ ਜਿੰਦਾਂ ਦੀ ਜ਼ਿੰਦਗੀ, ਸੰਘਰਸ਼, ਮਾਂ ਦੀ ਮਮਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਪ੍ਰਤੀ ਉਸਦੇ ਅਟੁੱਟ ਪਿਆਰ ਨੂੰ ਜੀਵੰਤ ਰੂਪ ਵਿੱਚ ਮੰਚ ’ਤੇ ਪੇਸ਼ ਕੀਤਾ ਜਾਵੇਗਾ।

🇳🇿 ਹੁਣ ਇਹ ਇਤਿਹਾਸਕ ਨਾਟਕ Wellington ਵਿੱਚ!

📅 ਐਤਵਾਰ, 7 ਮਾਰਚ 2027
📍 Little Theatre, Lower Hutt, Wellington

❤️ ਆਓ ਆਪਣੇ ਬੱਚਿਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਵੀ ਨਾਲ ਲੈ ਕੇ ਆਈਏ।
ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਦੱਸੀਏ ਕਿ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਦੇ ਇਤਿਹਾਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਮਹਾਰਾਜੇ ਹੀ ਨਹੀਂ — ਮਹਾਰਾਣੀਆਂ ਨੇ ਵੀ ਇਤਿਹਾਸ ਰਚਿਆ ਹੈ।

✨ ਇਹ ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਇੱਕ ਨਾਟਕ ਨਹੀਂ…
ਇਹ ਸਾਡੇ ਇਤਿਹਾਸ ਦੀ ਆਵਾਜ਼ ਹੈ।
ਇਹ ਇੱਕ ਮਾਂ ਦੇ ਦਰਦ ਦੀ ਕਹਾਣੀ ਹੈ।
ਇਹ ਇੱਕ ਔਰਤ ਦੇ ਅਟੁੱਟ ਹੌਸਲੇ ਦੀ ਕਹਾਣੀ ਹੈ।
ਇਹ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਦੀ ਸ਼ੇਰਨੀ — ਮਹਾਰਾਣੀ ਜਿੰਦਾਂ ਦੀ ਦਾਸਤਾਨ ਹੈ। 👑🔥

🙏 ਇਸ ਇਤਿਹਾਸਕ ਪੇਸ਼ਕਾਰੀ ਦਾ ਹਿੱਸਾ ਜ਼ਰੂਰ ਬਣੋ ਅਤੇ ਇਸ ਸੁਨੇਹੇ ਨੂੰ ਵੱਧ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਧ ਸਾਂਝਾ ਕਰੋ।

📞 ਆਪਣੇ ਸ਼ਹਿਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਸ਼ੋਅ ਕਰਵਾਉਣ ਲਈ ਸਾਡੀ ਟੀਮ ਨਾਲ ਸੰਪਰਕ ਕਰੋ।

events.id: Új-Zéland kiscsoportos körutazás – kalandtúra a világ végén-Wellington, New Zealand-All Events In
events.name: Új-Zéland kiscsoportos körutazás – kalandtúra a világ végén
events.venue: Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Új-Zéland kiscsoportos körutazás – kalandtúra a világ végén
https://hellovilagvlog.hu/uj-zeland-kiscsoportos-korutazas-kalandtura-a-vilag-vegen/

Készen állsz arra, hogy eljuss a világ egyik legvadabb és legérintetlenebb tájára? Az Új-Zéland kiscsoportos körutazás – kalandtúra a világ végén azoknak szól, akik nem csak látni szeretnének, hanem valóban átélni akarják a természet erejét és változatosságát. Utunkat az Északi-sziget különleges világában kezdjük: Auckland, Hobbiton, Rotorua és Wai-O-Tapu gejzírmezői, gőzölgő hőforrásai és vulkáni tájai már az első napokban megmutatják Új-Zéland nyers arcát. A Lake Taupō partján haladva érkezünk meg a Tongariro Nemzeti Parkba, ahol drámai vulkáni panorámák és alpesi környezet vár ránk — itt nem csak nézelődünk, beleállunk az élménybe. A főváros, Wellington után átkelünk a Cook-szoroson, és megérkezünk a Déli-szigetre. A Picton környéki fjordos partvidéktől az Abel Tasman térség aranyhomokos öblein át vezet az utunk tovább. A vad West Coast mentén elérjük a különleges formájú Pancake Rocks szikláit, majd a lenyűgöző Franz Josef-gleccser világát. A túra csúcspontjai közé tartozik Te Anau és a legendás Milford Sound, ahol hajóra szállva függőleges sziklafalak, vízesések és mély fjordok között haladunk. Ez nem egy klasszikus városnézős túra, hanem egy tartalmas, természetközeli Új-Zéland kiscsoportos körutazás, ahol rövid idő alatt meglepően sok mindent látunk, mégsem rohanunk. Kiscsoportban utazunk, rugalmasan, a legszebb panorámautakon haladva — mert a világ végén nem sietni kell, hanem megélni minden kilométert.

https://hellovilagvlog.hu/uj-zeland-kiscsoportos-korutazas-kalandtura-a-vilag-vegen/

events.id: Tony Martin: From Seedling to Sensation – How New Zealand Creates the Apples and Pears of the Future-Hawkes Bay,Wellington, New Zealand-All Events In
events.name: Tony Martin: From Seedling to Sensation – How New Zealand Creates the Apples and Pears of the Future
events.venue: Hawkes Bay,Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Tony Martin: From Seedling to Sensation – How New Zealand Creates the Apples and Pears of the Future
Have you ever bitten into an apple and wondered where it came from?

Not the orchard.

Not the supermarket.

But the very first idea that eventually became the fruit in your hand.

Creating a new apple or pear variety isn't something that happens overnight. It can take years of research, testing, patience and innovation before a single piece of fruit reaches consumers.

Join Tony Martin, Chief Executive of Prevar, for a fascinating behind-the-scenes Learning Lunch exploring how New Zealand is helping shape the future of fruit.

From understanding changing consumer tastes to developing entirely new varieties, Tony will reveal the remarkable journey from seedling to supermarket shelf and the science, strategy and creativity that make it possible.

You'll discover how some of New Zealand's most successful apple and pear varieties were developed, what makes a fruit variety stand out in global markets, and why innovation in horticulture requires both long-term thinking and bold decision-making.

Best of all, this isn't just a conversation.

Guests will enjoy a guided tasting of different apple and pear varieties, offering a rare opportunity to experience firsthand the flavours, textures and characteristics that breeders spend years developing.

This is a wonderful opportunity to look at something familiar in a completely new way.

Meet Tony 🎤

Tony Martin is Chief Executive of Prevar, the innovation and commercialisation company behind many of New Zealand and Australia's leading apple and pear varieties. With more than two decades of leadership experience across agribusiness, innovation and international markets, Tony works at the intersection of science, consumer insight and global horticulture, helping bring world-class fruit varieties from concept to consumers around the world.

What We'll Explore
• How new apple and pear varieties are created
• The science and strategy behind fruit innovation
• What consumers really want from future fruit varieties
• The journey from research programme to supermarket shelf
• Why innovation often requires patience, persistence and long-term thinking


📍 Location: FoodEast-Haumako, Hawke's Bay
📅 Date: Wednesday 10 March 2027
🕙 Time: 11:00am – 1:30pm
☕ Refreshments: Lunch and fruit tasting included
🎟️ Tickets: $95 per person

👥 Hosted by Love Heart
Warm, welcoming learning experiences designed for people who enjoy discovering new ideas and meeting interesting people.

events.name: CubaDupa
events.long_description:
One weekend every March, CubaDupa takes over some of Wellington’s central city streets for an epic party. The free annual festival brings a carnival vibe to the end of the summer. It offers live music, street theatre, dance, parades, and other cultural experiences. 
CubaDupa is New Zealand’s largest outdoor arts and music festival. It takes place over two days on Cuba Street and the surrounding roads, right in the heart of Wellington. The festival is suitable for the whole family with performances and activities running throughout the day and night. Multiple performance spaces showcase New Zealand’s emerging musical talent alongside established artists. The lineup usually includes over 140 local and international acts.

events.id: Miss Saigon-Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
events.name: Miss Saigon
events.venue: Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Tragic pop-musical Miss Saigon hasn’t played Wellington in over 15 years. Fabulous soloists, a 40-strong local choir, and a live orchestra are rectifying that in 2027. G&T Productions brings a semi-staged concert to the Michael Fowler Centre. This format puts the performers and music front and centre. Set during the final days of the Vietnam War in 1975, Miss Saigon is a heartbreaking, bold, and gripping musical theatre piece. 

From the songwriting team behind ‘Les Misérables’, Miss Saigon is a tragic love story of a young Vietnamese woman (Kim) who falls in love with an American soldier (Chris). Saigon falls, and their story unfolds alongside the Engineer, a ruthless survivor chasing his own ‘American Dream’. 

Wellingtonian Maya Handa Naff plays Kim. She has previously sung the role in the United States. Maya is an actor, director, and teacher whose Wellington performance credits include ‘Wicked’ (Glinda) and ‘Les Misérables’ (Eponine). Director and actor Kyle Chuen plays Chris. Laurence Mossman returns as Thuy after performing the part on Australian and international tours. Expect to hear songs like I’d Give My Life for You, Why God Why, and Bui Doi.

The Weave - Sheol
The first weekend game for The Weave LARP campaign, a futuristic fantasy game in Wellington.

About this Event



*********

Don’t look down. The sky is clear and blue. When you breathe in for the first time after your months-long voyage, the fresh air tastes impossibly sweet.

Don’t look down. A single star rests in the heavens, yellow and warm. Shoals of silvery fish dart through picturesque waves.

Don’t look down. The islands quake and churn beneath your feet. Alerts appear hourly on your screens about impossibilities, measurements beyond rational explanation.

You look down. What lies beneath? What might be unearthed from the strata of the past? What has been forgotten? And what should have remained buried?




What's going on?

A week ago, three ships landed on the planet called Etsen. The Highmit Research Mission has journeyed to this planet, across the vast dangers of space, to help the planet’s scientists understand the impossibility of measuring a second star in a 100 kilometre diameter patch of their sky.

You landed at Scion. It’s small, compared to the average communities on your home planets. Not even 5000 people. But it’s the largest settlement in Etsen’s affected zone. And it’s a strange new environment for many of you, perched on an island in a temperate archipelago.

The research mission’s primary team has already set up their main base of operations in Scion. Alongside the limited number of specialised Etsenite scientists, they are beginning initial research into the planet’s anomaly.

A few days ago, a small settlement in the affected zone, Axis, reported abnormal technological errors. Yesterday, a different settlement, closer to Scion, reported similar malfunctions.

You are members of the secondary research team dispatched to Axis. Your task sounds simple enough.

Identify the cause of the errors.
Prevent them from spreading further.

But, just like the impossible second star, you suspect nothing is as simple as it seems.




*********




OOC information

Sheol is the first weekend game of The Weave LARP.

The game is running on 20-21 March 2027 in Wellington at Khandallah Scout Hall (11A Station Road, Khandallah, Wellington 6035).
The game runs for 2 full days. There is no overnight accommodation. You will have the opportunity to leave a small amount of gear on-site overnight.
Players are self-catered. We are currently working with a generous volunteer to see if we can cater our crew. The crew will get confirmation closer to the start of the game if we can cater them.
The game is open to new player-characters, pending available tickets.

This game is 18+.




Tickets

Tickets go on sale Tuesday 29 September at 7pm through Eventbrite. Participants who attended the July 2026 day game will have early bird access. You must buy a ticket to secure your place. Ticket costs do not include Eventbrite fees.

Find the NZLARPs discount code by logging into your NZLARPs account and looking at the event page ( https://nzlarps.org/events/detail/356). If your NZLARP membership details are still pending or you can't figure out how to log into the website, ask us for the code in an email at .

Direct from Belgium, Slow Pilot invite audiences into the world of Jeff Buckley, performing his music with sensitivity, precision and a deep respect honouring the songs that still mean so much to so many

Slow Pilot are the only band worldwide capable of awakening the true soul, mystery, and magic of Jeff Buckley’s work. Singer Pieter Peirsman delivers a breathtaking vocal performance, capturing Buckley’s tone and emotional intensity with incredible accuracy. Jeff Buckley remains one of the most captivating and influential figures in modern music history. His singular studio album Grace has long transcended cult status, becoming a global touchstone for artists and audiences across generations and borders. Today, Buckley’s legacy continues to grow and resonate internationally, inspiring new listeners while remaining deeply meaningful to those who have carried his music with them for years.

That renewed global attention has been further intensified by the recent release of the acclaimed documentary It’s Never Over, Jeff Buckley, which has reignited worldwide fascination with his life, his voice, and his artistic depth. The ongoing attention around Buckley once again highlights what fans have always known. His music remains emotionally powerful, fragile, and strikingly relevant.

events.id: NZSQ — Strings in the Earth & Air-Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall-Wellington NZ
events.name: NZSQ — Strings in the Earth & Air
events.venue: Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall
events.long_description:
A concert of traditional Irish airs and folk melodies will be presented at a concert at the newly opened Wellington Town Hall in April 2027. Join Tom Delany and Dave Flynn for traditional and contemporary works in NZSQ — Strings in the Earth & Air. Tom Delany will play the uilleann pipes, while Dave Flynn will be on the guitar. ‘Uilleann’ means ‘elbow’ in Irish. The uilleann pipes are powered by the elbow, pumping air instead of the Scottish bagpipes that use the lungs. 

The concert takes its name from James Joyce’s poetry collection ‘Chamber Music’. Most of the poems in the collection revolve around the twin themes of love and music. ‘Strings in the earth and air’ is the poem that opens the collection. The concert forms part of New Zealand String Quartet’s In Collaboration series. With roughly one in six Kiwis being of Irish heritage, there are enduring connections between Ireland and Aotearoa. This concert brings those ties to life through poetry, song, and strings.

Tom Delany plays uilleann pipes, guitar, and bouzouki, and sings. As a founding member of Irish ensemble FOURWINDS, he has toured the world. He is known for playing traditional Irish music in a daring, free-flowing style. Dave Flynn is a composer and guitarist who offers a unique blend of Irish trad, minimalism, and jazz. His work has been performed by leading ensembles in venues across the globe.

events.venue: St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
There’s never been a group, let alone a supergroup, in rock history quite like it. Now you get to see a tribute to their huge success. In 1988, a group of five rock legends joined together to form The Traveling Wilburys. They were Bob Dylan, George Harrison, Jeff Lynne, Roy Orbison, and Tom Petty. 
Across four years, they produced two mega albums, a slew of hits and won a Grammy. They never toured. Now, a tribute band, The Travelling Wilburys Collective, is on tour and it’s visiting the St James Theatre in Wellington. 
You’ll get to hear some of their biggest and most celebrated hits like Handle with Care, End of the Line, Tweeter and the Monkey Man, and She's My Baby. Along with these original hits, you’ll get served classics from each individual artist and the groups they were in. That includes The Beatles, The Heartbreakers, and ELO. 
The Traveling Wilburys Collection bring together the collective talents, excitement, and magic that the original quintet had to offer. Join them for a night of fun and nostalgia.

events.name: Sunset Boulevard
events.venue: Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall
events.long_description:
The New Zealand professional premiere of one of Andrew Lloyd Webber’s most celebrated musicals is coming to Wellington. Sunset Boulevard takes centre stage at the newly restored Wellington Town Hall in April. Local company WITCH Music Theatre is presenting an epic site-specific production as part of the venue’s grand reopening programme. 

In a major coup for the production, acclaimed Tony Award-nominated performer Keala Settle will be playing the main role, Norma Desmond. Keala has strong iwi links to New Zealand so she sees this opportunity as a homecoming. She is best known for her role as Lettie Lutz in ‘The Greatest Showman’ and for her powerhouse performance of the Golden Globe-winning song “This Is Me” from the film. 

Sunset Boulevard has earned major acclaim across Broadway and the West End, including seven awards from 11 Tony Award nominations for its original 1994 Broadway production. It’s 2023 revival won seven Olivier Awards from 11 nominations. The production, designed specifically for the Town Hall’s refurbished auditorium, marks the New Zealand professional premiere of the musical.

events.name: Menopause The Musical
events.venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Described as the ultimate ladies’ night out, Menopause the Musical has been delivering laughs across the globe for years. Now the fun-filled musical about ‘the change’ returns to Wellington for one night.
Set in a department store, four women meet by chance while shopping for a black lace bra. Though they couldn’t be more different, they quickly discover a shared bond over memory loss, hot flushes, night sweats, and mood swings. What follows is a hilarious, heart-warming musical told with love, laughter and the greatest hits of the 60s, 70s and 80s. The laughter-filled 90-minute production gets audiences out of their seats dancing and singing along to clever parodies of beloved pop classics.
Winner of over 40 Tony Awards, Menopause the Musical has entertained more than 17 million fans worldwide. It’s been translated into nine languages and performed in more than 500 cities. The show’s enduring appeal lies in its honesty, hilarity and heart. It celebrates women everywhere and turns shared experiences into shared joy.

events.long_description:
The last in a trilogy of cycling-themed plays skids into The Wellington Opera House in May.  Writer-director Gregory Cooper and seasoned Kiwi actor Mark Hadlow collaborate once more to bring their cycling trilogy to a close. The one-man play 'WOBIL: Wise Old Bugger in Lycra' follows previous installments ‘MAMIL: Middle Aged Man In Lycra’ and ‘GOMIL: Grumpy Old Man In Lycra’. Expect familiar faces, trademark physical comedy, plenty of laughs, and a fair bit of heart too.
Mark is one of New Zealand’s best-known actors. You might have seen him on screen in ‘King Kong’ or ‘The Hobbit’, or a host of live professional theatre shows on stages around the motu.  Gregory's past work includes ‘That Bloody Woman’. This latest chapter sends Wayne on his hardest hill climb yet. With help, and hindrance, from a few old friends and enemies, he’s determined to go out in a blaze of lycra glory. Get ready for one last spin through friendship, ageing, and resilience.

events.long_description:
Presented by: Destroy All Lines
British legends Squeeze are returning to New Zealand in April 2027 with their Tried, Tested and Trixies Tour, celebrating 53 years of classic songwriting and standout music hits from one of the UK’s pioneers of Brit-pop music.
Founded in 1974 by Chris Difford and Glenn Tilbrook, Squeeze are one of pop’s best-loved bands with a catalogue of sky-high classics such as ‘Up the Junction’, ‘Tempted’, ‘Cool for Cats’, ‘Another Nail in My Heart’ and ‘Labelled with Love’, whose live shows are legendary and, as The Guardian wrote, “pop perfection”.
Squeeze remain one of the most revered and distinctive music outfits in UK pop history. Led by the unparalleled songwriting duo Glenn Tilbrook and Chris Difford, their legacy spans over five decades of masterful songwriting, stellar live performance, and cultural impact; between 1978 and 1996 they had no fewer than 11 singles in the UK Top 40, with six in the Top 20. Many more of their songs have been woven into the very fabric of the British songwriting tradition – alongside those of The Beatles and The Kinks – influencing everyone from Lily Allen to The Killers.
Coming to New Zealand to mark 50+ years of Squeeze and celebrate the release of their new album, Trixies, will be Glenn Tilbrook, bassist Owen Biddle, percussionist Steve Smith, keyboardist Stephen Large, drummer Simon Hanson, guitarist Leon Tilbrook and backing vocalist Danica Dora.

events.long_description:
Portland, Oregon producer, singer-songwriter and storyteller John Craigie returns to New Zealand in April 2027 on his I Swam Here Tour.
 
Following his first New Zealand shows in 2025, Craigie returns with his latest album, I Swam Here, out now on Zabriskie Point Records. Written and produced by Craigie, the album was recorded between New Orleans and Astoria, Oregon, bringing together the musical spirit of the Gulf Coast with the quieter sounds of the Pacific Northwest.
 
For more than a decade, Craigie has built a devoted following through his warm, sharply observed songwriting and live shows that pair music with humour and storytelling. His touring has taken him across the U.S., Europe and Australia, with appearances at Newport Folk, Pickathon, Edmonton Folk Festival and High Sierra, and performances alongside artists including Gregory Alan Isakov, Sierra Hull, Brett Dennen and Jack Johnson.
 

I Swam Here follows 2024’s Pagan Church, Craigie’s collaboration with TK & The Holy Know-Nothings, which spent six weeks at #1 on the Americana Albums chart. Expansive yet intimate, the new record marks another chapter for Craigie while retaining the sincerity and conversational songwriting that have become central to his work.
 

Craigie returns to San Fran, Wellington on Thursday 15 April and The Tuning Fork, Auckland on Friday 16 April 2027, returning to the same venues that hosted his first New Zealand tour in 2025.

events.long_description:
Every second counts. That’s the theme of The Curious Case of Benjamin Button. Having taken London and New York by storm, the hit musical is now making its way to Wellington, New Zealand. 

Described by WhatsOnStage as “The best British musical in decades” the show is an enchantingly beautiful and truly unordinary story. It follows Benjamin Button who is born old and bound to the fate of growing younger each day, Benjamin wants nothing more than to live a little life. But will he ever find a place to belong?   

The Olivier Award-winning musical is based on the 1922 short story by F Scott Fitzgerald. The story also inspired a 2008 movie. Now for the first time out of Broadway and the West End it travels to Australasia and Wellington has scored the premier. It brings a big heart, a foot-stomping score, and 15 remarkable actor-musicians who, among them, play 30 instruments. Get ready for a sweeping live score and a show epic in scale but intimate in feeling.

events.long_description:
Presented by: Destroy All Lines

St. Paul & The Broken Bones are a powerhouse soul ensemble from Alabama known for their electrifying live shows and impassioned vocals. Formed in Birmingham in 2011, the band features Paul Janeway (vocals), Jesse Phillips (bass), Browan Lollar (guitar), Kevin Leon (drums), Al Gamble (keyboards), Allen Branstetter (trumpet), Chad Fisher (trombone), and Amari Ansari (saxophone).

Their new self-titled sixth album marks a creative renewal—melding the band’s adventurous spirit with a return to soulful, song-focused roots. Recorded at the legendary FAME Studios and produced by Eg White (Adele, Celine Dion), the record blends psych-funk grooves, gospel-tinged ballads, and cinematic rock flourishes. Tracks like “Sushi and Coca-Cola” and “Going Back” reflect both personal introspection and the band’s deepened identity after a decade of evolution.

St. Paul & The Broken Bones have shared stages with The Rolling Stones, Lizzo, and Black Pumas, and performed at major festivals like Coachella, Glastonbury, Lollapalooza, and Bonnaroo. Even Sir Elton John took notice, inviting them to perform at his Oscar party. Blending rock & roll, soul, R&B, and more, the band continues to captivate audiences around the world.

events.name: Kia Mau
events.long_description:
Kia Mau is an arts festival that showcases innovative Indigenous performances. Held every two years, the festival lights up Wellington's winter. See contemporary performances by leading Tāngata Whenua , Tāngata Moana, and global Indigenous artists. The two-week festival includes dance, theatre, music, and visual art. Audiences can expect to be challenged and thrilled by new work from Aotearoa and beyond.
Kia Mau was first held in 2015, founded by two leading Aotearoa creatives. Hone Kouka (Ngāti Porou, Ngāti Kahungunu, Ngāti Raukawa, Kai Tahu) is the Artistic Director and Chief Executive. Mīria George (Ngāti Kearoa, Ngāti Tuara, Ngāti Awa, Ngāti Kūki ‘Āirani) is the Executive Director.
Hone and Mīria describe themselves as innovators. They push boundaries, redefine forms, and forge new paths. They say the festival is not just a platform for presentations, it’s a hub for kōrero and whanaungatanga . The festival has a strong influence on many artists and plays an important role in shaping New Zealand’s contemporary arts scene. “Kia Mau has continued to thrive because of the imagination and commitment of our artists. And of us to them,” says Mīria.

events.id: Black Ferns vs British and Irish Lions-Hnry Stadium, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
events.name: Black Ferns vs British and Irish Lions
events.venue: Hnry Stadium, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
The first-ever Howden British and Irish Lions women‘s series is coming to Aotearoa in 2027. With five games across the country, Wellington is to play host to one of three Test games. The competition is sure to be fierce and the atmosphere electric. 
Sitting at the halfway point between Rugby World Cups, the tour will offer high-calibre clashes between two rugby powerhouses. Ben Calveley, CEO of The British & Irish Lions, said the tour marks “something truly special for the women’s game.” With the first-ever tour title on the table, you can expect both teams to leave it all on the field. Let‘s fill the cake tin with stomping feet and edge-of-your-seat screams. The Wellington game is Test number two of the series, so pull on your jersey, warm up your pipes and get ready for Black Ferns fever to sweep the city. 
Tickets go on sale late 2026.

events.id: The Michael Jackson HIStory Show-The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
events.name: The Michael Jackson HIStory Show
events.venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Celebrate the creative genius and musical talent of one of the greatest pop singers. The Michael Jackson HIStory Show promises to be a riveting live performance. The full-scale production at the Opera House pays tribute to one of the most significant cultural figures of the 20th century. Expect a stellar live band, choreographed dancers, and authentic costumes. 

Garth Field is at the centre of this performance. He’s often described as electrifying in his role as Michael. Garth is a triple-threat performer with impeccable vocals, dancing, and acting. 

The show tracks Michael’s journey from his early days as a member of the Jackson 5 to his groundbreaking theatrics in the 80s. It goes on to acknowledge his continued domination of pop culture into the 21st century. Hear all the hits like Thriller, Billie Jean, Bad, Beat It, Don’t Stop Til You Get Enough, They Don’t Really Care About Us, and many more.
